metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Natal ID
metas.note: Natal, Rio Grande do Norte
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Neon-Yellow Horizontal ID
metas.note: Neon-yellow horizontal IDs are specific to Sao Paulo. Do not confuse with Campo Grande or Vitoria (they have vertical, and smaller, neon-yellow IDs)
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Neon-Yellow Pole ID
metas.note: Neon-yellow, vertical IDs can be found in Campo Grande, MS and Vitoria, ES. Do not confuse with horizontal neon-yellow IDs (Sao Paulo)
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Onitel Sticker
metas.note: Unique to Luziania, GO
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Open Electric Box
metas.note: Open or trashed electric boxes appear frequently in Maraba and Santarém (both Para).
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Orange Lamp
metas.note: Orange Lamps are common in Belem.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Orange Lamp Arm
metas.note: Very common in Teresina, one of the most well-known urban Brazil metas.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Outer Dashed Lines
metas.note: Outer Dashed Lines can rarely be found in Rio Grande do Norte or other northeast states.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Para specific Pole ID
metas.note: Pare uses these state-wide pole IDs.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Paraiba ID
metas.note: This ID is uncommon, but unique to Paraiba (most common in the capital Joao Pessoa).
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Paraiba Lamp
metas.note: The shape matters.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Parana Black Paint Pole ID
metas.note: Pole IDs in Paraná are usually made up of black paint and yellow or white painted text. They do not appear in the capital of Paraná: Curitiba.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess, Plonk It

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Parana Black Square
metas.note: This tiny black paint is rarely found on larger poles in Paraná. Still worth a quick scan, especially in urban locs.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Parana Road Pole Paint
metas.note: Utility poles in Paraná on intersections are sometimes painted with the street name. This is because metal signs are expensive. This is also possible on Northern Rio Grande do Sul ladder poles. An exception is the town of Sinop, Mato Grosso.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess, PlonkIt

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - PARE on stone
metas.note: Stone road markings are unique to Caxias do Sul, RS.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Pencil Pole Top
metas.note: This little hat on the top, which makes the whole pole resemble a pencil, is most common in Rio de Janeiro, but can also be found in Manaus and Distrito Federal.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Piles of Dirt Meta
metas.note: Common in Boa Vista
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Pole Company
metas.note: Electricity company names in Brazil are commonly engraved onto the poles, with their names sometimes corresponding to state names. For example, CELPA stands for Para, COSERN for Rio Grande do Norte or COELCE for Ceara.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Pole Paint starting with letter
metas.note: Yellow paint with black numbers, starts with a letter. Possible in Bahia and Pernambuco. The letter is often specific to a town. Goias uses similar paint IDs, but they consist only of digits.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Pole-Attached Sign
metas.note: Some poles in Curitiba, PR have street signs attached to them. Curitiba still uses regular, generic street signs, though.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Pole-Wrapped Sign
metas.note: These blue pole-wrapped signs are unique to Campo Grande.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Porto Alegre ID
metas.note: Porto Alegre, Rio Grande do Sul
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Porto Velho Pole ID
metas.note: Porto Velho, Rondonia
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Recife Lamp
metas.note: Recife, Pernambuco
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Rectangle on Pole Arm
metas.note: Unique for Recife. Can be faded or even have different colors. It's the shape that matters.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Red Brick Pavement
metas.note: Some roads in Acre are made of red brick.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Red Gravel
metas.note: Most roads in Piauí have red gravel on the side of the road. Some roads in Generation 4 now have tarmac and kerbs, but some gravel shoulders remain.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Red Sticker on Lamp
metas.note: This red sticker below the lamp is unique to Fortaleza.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Rio de Janeiro Lamp
metas.note: Curvy lamp arm, usually big head.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Rio de Janeiro Landbridge
metas.note: This map west of the city of Rio de Janeiro is unique due to the water in the south, the roadlines (double yellow - double broken yellow - single broken white) and the little wall in the North. Rio mountains can be seen in most sections of the road to the North.
metas.footer: Source: Unique Roads of the World by Figsy

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Rio De Janeiro Polepaint
metas.note: This yellow polepaint, similar to Sao Paulo, but with all numbers, can be found in Rio de Janeiro.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Rio de Janeiro Taxi
metas.note: Taxis in Rio de Janeiro are completely yellow.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Rio Weird Pole
metas.note: When there is something out of the ordinary happening with the pole, it's Rio de Janeiro.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Roraima Lamps
metas.note: Lamps in Roraima have a similar style but have different colours in the main cities. Boa Vista, Normandia, and Mucajaí have red lamps, Rorainópolis has blue lamps, Pacaraima and Iracema have green, and Caracaraí has yellow.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Round Pole
metas.note: Alongside ladder poles, round poles can often be found across the south of Brazil, especially São Paulo. These poles are cylindrical and made of concrete.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Salvador Lamp Arm ID
metas.note: Long yellow ID on the lamp arm, can be very hard to spot.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Salvador Sidewalk

metas.note: Santarem, Para

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Sao Luis ID
metas.note: This rare ID is specific to Sao Luis. However, the embedded Maranhao IDs are more common.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Sao Luis Pointy Lamp
metas.note: Pointy front of lamp head, blue or yellow top light.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Sao Paulo Lamp
metas.note: Straight long lamp neck, with tight top bend, usually thin head.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Sao Paulo Pole
metas.note:
Assymetrical crossbeam and insulator position with a long support bar reaching to the middle of the longer part of the crossbeam.

Extremely common in Sao Paulo, common in Rio Grande do Sul. Less common Rio de Janeiro, Espirito Santo and Mato Grosso do Sul (where it appears most oftenly in Tres Lagoas). Rare in Mato Grosso.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Sao Paulo Polepaint
metas.note: Sao Paulo Metropolitan Area has these yellow pole paints with a three letter code. The letters stand for the town. SPU is the most important code, standing for the main city.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Serra dos Orgaos
metas.note: This road can be found North of Rio de Janeiro (city). It is a concrete road with black tar behind the road lines.
metas.footer: Source: Unique Roads of the World by Figsy

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Short Gamma + Box
metas.note: Short crossbeam, support bar and electricity box at the end of the crossbeam. Only found in Belem. (unlike the regular Gamma pole with box which can also be found in Salvador and Rio de Janeiro).
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Small Red Tactile Pavement
metas.note: Small tile, circular bumps, red tactile pavement is very common in Vitoria, ES. (Do not confuse with Florianopolis, which has large tile red tactile pavement).
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Southern Sidewalk
metas.note: You can often see pavements in Rio Grande do Sul that have brown tiles but are either jagged and random, or square. This style can sometimes be seen in Santa Catarina.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Speedbumps
metas.note: Yellow dashed lines and speedbumps are very common in Brasília. (but not unique)
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Spool Insulators
metas.note: These insulators have a shape resembling a spool of thread. They are found mostly in Rio de Janeiro and Espírito Santo, and have been seen in Ceará.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Square Paint ID
metas.note: This ID with two sections, the upper one being a square with a number in it, appears in Pernambuco.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Striped Curbs
metas.note: Black and white striped curbs are common in Boa Vista.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Surprising Wooden Pole
metas.note: In Porto Alegre, there is noticeably more foliage, cleaner, and more spacious than any other city which makes the common wooden poles look somewhat out of place.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Teresina ID
metas.note: Long & Horizontal ID
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Thick Bottom Insulator
metas.note:
They're found almost anywhere, but can still resolve some 50/50s:

They are only rarely found in Rio Grande do Norte.

Also they're less common in Pernambuco, Parana, Santa Catarina.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Thin Long Insulator
metas.note: Insulators in Ceará can sometimes be uniquely long and thin. They are in Goiás too, but are rare.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Thin Red Stripe
metas.note: A road with a thin, red stripe out of gravel can be found east of Teresina, Piaui.
metas.footer: Source: Unique Roads of the World by Figsy

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Tiny Lamp - Araruna
metas.note: "Tiny Lamps" are unique to Northwest-Paraná. This specific one is unique to the town of Araruna.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Tiny Lamp - Cianorte

metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Tiny Lamp - Cruzeiro do Oeste
metas.note: "Tiny Lamps" are unique to Northwest-Paraná. This specific one is unique to the town of Cruzeiro do Oeste.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Tiny Lamp - Loanda
metas.note: "Tiny Lamps" are unique to Northwest-Paraná. This specific one is unique to the town of Loanda.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Tiny Lamp - Maringa
metas.note: "Tiny Lamps" are unique to Northwest-Paraná. This specific one is unique to the town of Maringa.

metas.note: "Tiny Lamps" are unique to Northwest-Paraná. This specific one is unique to the town of Paranavai.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Tocantins specific lamp
metas.note: This lamp with a short arm and top light is specific to Tocantins.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Tocantins specific lamp
metas.note: This blue lamp with top light and the unique pattern on the underside is specific to Tocantins.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Tocantins specific lamp
metas.note: This long blue lamp with a top light and a unique pattern on the underside is specific to Tocantins.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Transparent Mushroom Insulator
metas.note: Transparent, mushroom-shaped insulators are common in Alagoas. They less frequently appear in Coastal Santa Catarina. Rarely, they also appear in coastal Rio Grande do Sul, coastal Sao Paulo and in Sergipe.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Trident Pole
metas.note: Poles with these wide insulators in a trident formation are common in Maranhão. The insulator itself is common across many states, but not in this configuration.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Two Part Lamp - Goias Variant
metas.note:
2-part lamp, most commonly seen in Minas Gerais and Goias. This particular variant with a the pole visible underneath is more common in Goias.

Otherwise, this pole appears in Rio Grande do Norte and Rio Grande do Sul (very useful if you have North/South vibe), spill in Distrito Federal and extremely rarely in Para, Mato Grosso and Rondonia.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Two Part Lamp - Minas Gerais Variant
metas.note:
2-part lamp, most commonly seen in Minas Gerais and Goias. This particular variant - with both parts enveloping the lamp - is more common in Minas Gerais.

Otherwise, this pole appears in Rio Grande do Norte and Rio Grande do Sul (very useful if you have North/South vibe), spill in Distrito Federal and extremely rarely in Para, Mato Grosso and Rondonia.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Uberaba ID
metas.note: In Uberaba, pole IDs start with 2 or 3, and sometimes with 1. In Belo Horizonte, meanwhile, they start with 0 or 1. They do not appear in any other cities in MG.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Uneven Stone Pavement
metas.note: These uneven but mostly square stone roads are seen in western Rio Grande do Sul and west Santa Catarina. The soil will often be very dark in these regions too.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Vitoria Electric Boxes
metas.note: Metal electricity box, sandwiched between plastic electricity boxes are very common in Vitoria, ES.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Vitoria Streetsign
metas.note: Unique streetsign design in Vitoria.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Weird Road Layout
metas.note: Roundabouts and weird layout roads that are mostly empty, and perfectly flat, are common in Palmas.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - White Mushroom Insulator
metas.note: Bahia uses these unique white insulators sometimes.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - WiFi-Password Pole-ID
metas.note: If you find pole IDs with codes that resemble WiFi-passwords (mix of digits, upper- and lowercase letters), you're in Curitiba, PR.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Wooden Pole
metas.note: Some states also use wooden poles. They are most commonly seen in Rio Grande do Sul, Roraima, Amazonas, and Rio de Janeiro.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Yellow Outer Lines
metas.note: Yellow outer lines on urban roads are very common in Curitiba.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Yellow Stick
metas.note: This yellow stick is common in Rio Branco, and often has a sign attached to it.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - Zig-Zag lamp arm
metas.note: In Brazil, this Zig-Zag lamp arm is unique to Caxias do Sul.
metas.footer: Source: Brazil Urban Metas by Cheddarman and Antidotess

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure - ZigZag-Topbar
metas.note: This pole configuration, featuring a zigzag-shaped top bar resting atop a flat crossbar, is exclusive to Ceara and Roraima. The pole is usually much larger than a regular electricity pole.

metas.name: Brazil - Infrastructure -6+ Ridge Insulators
metas.note:
These insulators have six or more ridges.

Commonly found in:

  • Bahia, Tocantins, Maranhao
  • Para, Mato Grosso, Mato Grosso do Sul
  • Parana Santa Catarina

Uncommon in:

  • Acre, Rondonia, Amapa
  • Piaui, Goias, Sao Paulo, RGDS

Rarely in:

  • RGDN, Rio de Janeiro

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - Acre Landscape
metas.note: Acre has a unique landscape of small grass hills and sparsely growing trees. The roads often do not cut around the hills like in most of Brazil, but ride the hills instead. A similar landscape can also be seen near Maraba in the state of Pará.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/brazil for more clues.

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - Amazon Rainforest
metas.note: The Amazon is a dense rainforest that compromises 40% of Brazil's total area. Not many roads are within it, but those that are, mostly go through either biodiverse forest or grassy hills with sparse trees.

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - Amazonas 319
metas.note: The Amazonas 319 has a very lush, bright green and tropical landscape, as it cuts through the Amazon rainforest. The road is flat and mostly unpaved, featuring bright orange soil. However, closer to Manaus the road becomes paved. There are wooden or ladder poles alongside the entire stretch. It is covered by the blue Generation 4 car.

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - BR-163 in Para
metas.note: The Pará section of the 163 is often hilly, curvy, dry, and sometimes hazy. It has a wide range of amazonian vegetation. The road is frequently trafficked, usually by transportation trucks. It is covered by the blue Generation 4 car.

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - BR174 in Amazonas
metas.note: This road can be recognized by the Amazonian looking trees and the NW/SE angle. It always has Gen 4 and an exposed, blue car front.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/brazil for more clues.

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - BR230 in Amazonas
metas.note: This wide dirt road has Amazonian trees and a blurred car. You will not find other cars on the road. It's the only East-to-West angle road in that area.
metas.footer: Source: Unique Roads of the World by Figsy

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - BR230 in Para
metas.note: This road looks like an Amazonian road with the trees and dense rainforest. It runs east-west, slightly to the south. The road looks like its stained with mud
metas.footer: Source: Unique Roads of the World by Figsy

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - BR319, North of Porto Velho
metas.note: This road is characterized by it's Amazonian look and the SW-NE road angle. Some sections of this road are overcast and/or showcase a flat landscape.
metas.footer: Source: Unique Roads of the World by Figsy

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - Caatinga landscape
metas.note: Northeastern Brazil can be identified by its dry soil, shrubs and succulents (the Caatinga landscape).

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - Caatinga landscape - rain coverage
metas.note: Northeastern Brazil can be identified by its dry soil, shrubs and succulents (the Caatinga landscape). In rainy season coverage, the shrubs are still recognizable, but can be deceptively green.

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - Corvo Branco
metas.note: This road in eastern Santa Catarina is characterized by its windyness and by the steep mountains and cliffs along its side. It can feel like your driving with the clouds. The road goes through Corvo Branco which is a famous tourist attraction.
metas.footer: Source: Unique Roads of the World by Figsy

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - Dunas da Sabiaguaba
metas.note: This road east of Fortaleza is characterized by its unique pavement and the sanddunes along the road.
metas.footer: Source: Unique Roads of the World by Figsy

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - Exposed Rock
metas.note: Espírito Santo, and the surrounding areas, often have large mountains with exposed rock.

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - Flat Wetland
metas.note: Coastal regions in Rio Grande do Sul are recognisable due to being a rare flat wetland, which is uncommon in Brazil.

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - Landbridge in Rio Grande do Sul
metas.note: Recognizable by the swamp-like landscape, the pine trees along the road and the Lagoon It runs at a SE-NW angle.
metas.footer: Source: Unique Roads of the World by Figsy

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - Noronha Rocks
metas.note: Ilha de Fernando de Noronha is similar in vegetation to NE-Brazil and has large exposed rocks.

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - North of Uiramuta road
metas.note: This very unique looking road features rolling hills, which is unusual for the rather flat Roraima. It is a windy dirt road and despite being green, it lacks trees. What seperates this from the road south of Uiramuta is that it's more skinny and steeper.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/brazil for more clues.

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - Rio Grande do Sul Landscape
metas.note: The landscape in Rio Grande do Sul can be hilly or flat with lush, green fields. Southern areas can have some resemblance to Uruguay.

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - Rollercoaster Road
metas.note: The 364 through Acre is very recognisable due to the rollercoaster-like landscape and road: the road uniquely rides the hills rather than snaking around them. There is usually no traffic, and is covered mostly by Generation 3 with an antenna.

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - Roraima Landscape
metas.note: Rural locations in Roraima are mostly open grassy plains with large, distant mountains in the background. Occasionally, you are on roads within the mountains. Furthermore, the grass in Roraima is distinctly thin, and grows in bunches.

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - Serra do Mar
metas.note:
Serra do Mar is a high mountain range that runs close to the coast from Parana to Northern RGDS.

If you have a high altitude road going on the mountains, instead of in the valleys, you're likely here.

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - South of Uiramuta
metas.note: This very unique looking road features rolling hills, which is unusual for the rather flat Roraima. It is a windy dirt road and despite being green, it lacks trees. What seperates this from the road south of Uiramuta is that it's less skinny and less steep.
metas.footer: Source: Unique Roads of the World by Figsy

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - Southeast Hills
metas.note: Minas Gerais, Rio de Janeiro and Espírito Santo often have rolling grassy hills.

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - Swampy Road
metas.note: A very swampy road (PA-154) can be found Northwest of Belém. Notably, there are very few trees, and the soil is very red.
metas.footer: Source: Unique Roads of the World by Figsy

metas.name: Brazil - Landscape - Uneven Stone + Corn
metas.note: This beautiful road west of Cascavel and South of Toledo, by the PR-585 is characterized by the uneven red stone pavement and the corn plantation next to it.
metas.footer: Source: Unique Roads of the World by Figsy

metas.name: Brazil - Trekker - Amazonian Trekker
metas.note: This Amazonian trekker combines boat and walking coverage on and near the Madeira and Aripuana rivers, south of the 319. They are seen travelling through dense rainforest and small villages.

metas.name: Brazil - Trekker - Lençóis Maranhenses National Park
metas.note: The beautiful National Park of Northeast Maranhão, known for its sand dunes with pools of water, has walking trekker and vehicle coverage. The truck is white with a black bed. The landscape can vary from beach to sandy wetland.

metas.name: Brazil - Trekker - Noronha Boat Trekker
metas.note: There is boat coverage around the island of Ilha de Fernando de Noronha.

metas.name: Brazil - Vegetation - Acai Palm
metas.note:
Açai palms produce fruits that are popular globally. Most of these palms are found near Belem, but can be seen across the Amazon. They are distinct in the way the leaflets droop downward along with their unusually thin trunks.

Note by MB: They are very similar to the Jucara Palm (which grows in Southern Brazil). Tips for differentiation:

  • Acai Palms have more thick, robust leaves (comparatively)
  • Acai Palms like growing in bunches
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/brazil for more clues.

metas.name: Brazil - Vegetation - Acrocomia Totai (Paraguay Palm)
metas.note:
This palm is commonly mistaken to be a Macaw Palm (Acrocomia Aculeata). The key difference is that the trunk of the "Paraguay Palm" is often smoother and less irregular. The crown can also give some hints although it's difficult to catch the differences

  • Macaw Palm: More open and irregular, with leaves spreading in different directions.
  • "Paraguay Palm": Denser and more compact, sometimes looking neater and rounder.

The distribution is also a bit different, as this palm usually is closer to Paraguay than the Macaw Palm which stretches further.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Plant World - Palms by Zen

metas.name: Brazil - Vegetation - Babassu Palm
metas.note: Babassu palms have long, robust leaves comprised of many leaflets. Trunk length can vary from short to tall. They are found throughout the Amazon, or more rarely, down the east coast.

metas.name: Brazil - Vegetation - Carnauba Palm
metas.note: Carnaúba palms have short but strong, fan-like leaves and a trunk that is smooth at the top and spiked at the bottom. They are common in Ceará but are also in Piauí and Rio Grande do Norte.

metas.name: Brazil - Vegetation - Coconut Palm
metas.note: Coconut palm trees have long leaves, can grow very tall, and have thin trunks. They are common across the north eastern states and sometimes further west or south along the coast.

metas.name: Brazil - Vegetation - Jucara Palm
metas.note:
Closely related to the Açaí palm, they are really hard to distinguish apart from each other. However, the Açaí palm grows mostly in the northern flat regions of Brazil, while the Juçara grows in the mountainous south-east regions of Brazil anywhere from Espirito Santo down to Rio Grande do Sul.

Here some tips for differences:

  • The leaves of Jucara Palms are thinner
  • Jucara Palms have more space, they don't like growing close to each other.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Plant World - Palms by Zen

metas.name: Brazil - Vegetation - Macaw Palm
metas.note: Macaw palms, often called Paraguay palms, have thin leaves compared to other palms, and often have a visible spear shaped top. They are very common around Mato Grosso do Sul and the surrounding states, but can be seen much further out sometimes. These palms should be used with caution, and single trees are much less of an indicator than multiple trees.

metas.name: Brazil - Vegetation - Moriche Palm
metas.note: Moriche palms have leaves with a rounded fan shape. They are most common in Amazonas, Acre, and Roraima, but can be found in all of the Amazonian states.

metas.name: Brazil - Vegetation - Mysterious Northeastern Plant
metas.note: This species of plant, with long stems and many leaves growing up, are very common in Ceará, Rio Grande do Norte, and Paraíba. In the dry season, you can still make out the distinct long stems without leaves.

metas.name: Brazil - Vegetation - Parana Pine
metas.note: These distinct trees, called Paraná pines, have long horizontal branches with leaves only at the end. They grow mainly in the southern Brazilian states of Paraná, Santa Catarina, and Rio Grande do Sul.

metas.name: Brazil - Vegetation - Pine Trees
metas.note: Pine Trees are common in Southern Brazil, but are rarely ever found north of Belo Horizonte.

metas.name: Brazil - Vegetation - Queen Palm
metas.note:
Queen palms have leaf stems that point upwards on the trunk and then "bow down" again to the ground due to gravity. They are native to South America. In Brazil, they are mainly found along the coast between Rio de Janeiro and Porto Alegre.

Outside of South America, they're also found in Florida and East Coast Queensland.

metas.name: Brazil - Vegetation - Tocantins Grass
metas.note: Very tall grass can be often seen in the centre of the country, most notably in the Tocantins, Goiás, Bahia, and Minas Gerais states.

metas.name: Car Meta - 2 Zipties
metas.note: 2 clearly visible zip-ties can be found on a few roads in the southwest. Notably most of the 39 and its many sideroads, southeast of Ubar, southern 43, and the westernmost roads.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & The Oman Meta by @samuel8170

metas.name: Car Meta - Antenna facing camera
metas.note:
An antenna that is facing towards the camera is found all over the north.

Note by MB: This antenna can further be divided by the wire on the left side of the truck. BUT: If you're playing NMPZ and can't see the wire, it's still worth knowing where this antenna is found in general.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & The Oman Meta by @samuel8170

metas.name: Car Meta - Antenna facing camera - Big Wire Loop
metas.note:
The backwards-facing antenna can be further divided into smaller areas based on the type of wire present on the bar.

A wire that loops around the bar is found around Al Suwayq.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & The Oman Meta by @samuel8170

metas.name: Car Meta - Antenna facing camera - No Car
metas.note:
The backwards-facing antenna can be further divided into smaller areas based on the type of wire present on the bar.

If the car is mostly or entirely blurred, you are in

  • North Al Buraymi
  • North Al Dhahirah
  • South of Al Suwayq

metas.name: Car Meta - Antenna facing camera - No Wire
metas.note:
The backwards-facing antenna can be further divided into smaller areas based on the type of wire present on the bar.

No wire at all is found in the northwest.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & The Oman Meta by @samuel8170

metas.name: Car Meta - Antenna facing camera - Small Wire Loop
metas.note:
The backwards-facing antenna can be further divided into smaller areas based on the type of wire present on the bar.

A small looping wire in front of the bar is mainly in the east, starting in Muscat and Ad Dhakiliyah
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & The Oman Meta by @samuel8170

metas.name: Car Meta - Antenna facing camera - Wire on Bar
metas.note:
The backwards-facing antenna can be further divided into smaller areas based on the type of wire present on the bar.

A wire following the bar is found on the roads that make an A-shape on the map, and on the Al Batinah/Al Dhahirah border.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & The Oman Meta by @samuel8170

metas.name: Car Meta - Coiled Cable - Flat
metas.note:
Coiled Cable can be found in Coastal Al Batinah South, and in North Eastern Ash Sharqiyah South.

The cable can have several shapes but remains easy to identify.

Al Batinah South is very flat and more residential
metas.footer: Source: Oman Cable Guide by capitalos15

metas.name: Car Meta - Coiled Cable - Mountainous
metas.note:
Coiled Cable can be found in Coastal Al Batinah South, and in North Eastern Ash Sharqiyah South.

The cable can have several shapes but remains easy to identify.

Ash Sharqiyah South is more mountainous or flat with distant mountains
metas.footer: Source: Oman Cable Guide by capitalos15

metas.name: Car Meta - Double Laying Antenna
metas.note: Mostly found at the same places as single laying antenna but sometimes on different (sections of) roads.

metas.name: Car Meta - Forward Facing Antenna
metas.note: A forwards-facing antenna is only found in and around Muscat.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & The Oman Meta by @samuel8170

metas.name: Car Meta - Full Blurred Car
metas.note:
You might still be able to kind off make out the colour but there shouldn’t be any parts of the car fully visible except for (usually) the antenna.

In the North, it can be found West of Muscat. In the South, it can be found on the 31 in Al Wusta, on the 45 & 47 and around Salalah.

metas.name: Car Meta - Gen 3; Red Car; Long Antenna
metas.note: A red Generation 3 car with a long antenna can be seen in and east of Melbourne.

metas.name: Car Meta - Left Cut Ziptie
metas.note:
There are two visible zip ties, but the left one is cut.

Cannot be found in Musandam, Muscat, Al Dhahirah, Al Batinah South. In Al Buraimi, it's only found North of Al Ain. In Al Batinah North, it's only found in the eastern half.

metas.name: Car Meta - No Right Ziptie, Wire behind Bar
metas.note:
No right zip tie but the wire is arranged differently so that it passes behind the back of the metal bar.

Can be found West of Muscat.

metas.name: Car Meta - Right Tilted Antenna
metas.note: An antenna bent to the right is found all over the south, as well as a few pockets in the north, notably northeast of El Ain, west of Al Suwayq, and around Bidiyah.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & The Oman Meta by @samuel8170

metas.name: Car Meta - Semi-Blurred Car
metas.note:
Less blurred than the normal blurred. Parts of the car are still fully visible, usually the front but sometimes the sides too.

It can be found around Muscat.

metas.name: Car Meta - Straight Antenna
metas.note: A regular-looking antenna that faces upwards is mainly found around and west of Muscat, as well as on highways in the northwest. A few other pockets include Al Buraimi and Sohar.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & The Oman Meta by @samuel8170

metas.name: Chile - Agriculture - Vineyards
metas.note: Vineyards are commonly seen in Maule.

metas.name: Chile - Car Meta - Conguillo National Park
metas.note: Conguillio National Park can be recognized by this white truck with visible side mirrors and an antenna on the front right.

metas.name: Chile - Car Meta - Puerto Williams
metas.note:
Puerto Williams, the southernmost town covered by street view, can be recognized by this white pickup truck with visible side mirrors.

NOTE: The Puerto Williams coverage is located fairly far away from the normal car coverage in Chile. The nearest normal car coverage is in Fuerte Bulnes, near Punta Arenas.

metas.name: Chile - Car Meta - Toyota Hilux
metas.note: A grey Toyota Hilux, with various gear loaded and a snorkel on the front right, can be seen from around Baños Morales.

metas.name: Chile - Car Meta - Trailer
metas.note: The Google car can be seen towing a white and silver trailer with the word ‘Outback’ north of the Chilean National Zoo in Santiago.

metas.name: Chile - Coverage Meta - Autumn Coverage
metas.note: Southern Aysén can be recognised by autumn coverage, having orange and red coloured vegetation. Keep in mind that not all coverage in this region will have fall colours.

metas.name: Chile - Coverage Meta - B-710
metas.note:
More Generation 4 Sunset coverage can be seen on B-710 and Ruta 5.

On the B-710, a slight ridge can be seen to the west, while Ruta 5 is more open. Make sure to use the road angle or other clues before guessing.

metas.name: Chile - Coverage Meta - Ruta 5
metas.note:
More Generation 4 Sunset coverage can be seen on B-710 and Ruta 5.

On the B-710, a slight ridge can be seen to the west, while Ruta 5 is more open. Make sure to use the road angle or other clues before guessing.

metas.name: Chile - Infrastructure - Clay Brick Walls
metas.note: San Pedro de Atacama can be recognized by its clay brick walls, commonly with triangles at the top.

metas.name: Chile - Infrastructure - Concepcion Lamps
metas.note: Blue rectangular lamps with a yellow stripe can be found in Concepción.

metas.name: Chile - Infrastructure - Green Dome Lamps
metas.note: Lamps that look like green domes can be seen in Copiapo.

metas.name: Chile - Infrastructure - Letter Roads
metas.note: Chile uses a memorable regional road naming system, where the first letter increases between A and Y from north to south.

metas.name: Chile - Infrastructure - Orange Lamps
metas.note:
Orange lamps can most often be seen in Calama and Chañaral, and rarely in Antofagasta.

NOTE: Orange lamps can rarely be found in other smaller cities. Make sure to look out for other clues before guessing.

metas.name: Chile - Infrastructure - Orange Street Signs
metas.note: Orange street signs can be seen in the city of Lanco, present at almost every intersection.

metas.name: Chile - Infrastructure - Photocell Lamps
metas.note: Lamps in Santiago very commonly have photocells. You will rarely find them in other cities such as Valparaiso, Osorno and Loncoche.

metas.name: Chile - Infrastructure - Round Pole & Black Paint
metas.note: Round poles with black paint can be seen in the town of El Salvador.

metas.name: Chile - Infrastructure - Ruta 9
metas.note: All yellow lines on a concrete road are a good indicator that you are on the paved section of Ruta 9, in the very south of Chile. The landscape tends to be barren, grassy, and treeless.

metas.name: Chile - Infrastructure - Silver/Grey Lamp
metas.note: This lamp, with a silver top and grey bottom, can be found in Puerto Montt and Temuco.

metas.name: Chile - Infrastructure - Talca Lamps
metas.note: Grey lamps with a thin, flat top and a rounded underside can be found in Talca.

metas.name: Chile - Infrastructure - White Pole Paint in the Desert
metas.note: Poles in Arica feature white paint with a black number, while the other cities in the Atacama Desert feature poles with yellow paint. Keep in mind the paint may have faded, making it look white.

metas.name: Chile - Infrastructure - Yellow Pole Paint in the Desert
metas.note: Poles in Arica feature white paint with a black number, while the other cities in the Atacama Desert feature poles with yellow paint. Keep in mind the paint may have faded, making it look white.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - A-31
metas.note: The A-31 can be recognised by its high altitude, with a steep drop into a valley to the north. The road also has Gen 3 sunset coverage.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - A11 - Barren
metas.note:
After crossing the Lluta River at Poconchile, the Ruta 11 continues out of the valley and up into the mountains. The road is all newly paved (except for a few small segments with ongoing construction) and is generally quite wide. This section of Ruta 11 features:

  • Many concrete barriers (which are often painted yellow), double guardrails, and roadside drainage ways.
  • Maroon-colored asphalt in some places.
  • Mountains are made of light reddish sand with occasional exposed rock. Rounded protrusions are also common

The landscape is bare of vegetation until around Zapahuira, east of which the landscape becomes open and covered with small green bushes.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Chile by Palmerranian

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - A11 - Lluta River Valley
metas.note: Along the Lluta River, the Ruta 11 passes through a wide valley lined by sloping, sandy mountains that often feature distinctly round rock protrusions. The valley is home to a large amount of agriculture relative to other parts of the Atacama Desert. You’ll often see sizable green fields lined by bushes, trees, or wooden fences, as well as bunches of planted Mexican fan palms. A railroad track also follows the Lluta River on both sides, so if you’re in a green valley next to both a river and a railroad, you’re almost certainly on Ruta 11.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Chile by Palmerranian

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - A11 - Shrubby
metas.note: After crossing the Lluta River at Poconchile, the Ruta 11 continues out of the valley and up into the mountains. The road is all newly paved (except for a few small segments with ongoing construction) and is generally quite wide. The landscape is bare of vegetation until around Zapahuira, east of which the landscape becomes open and covered with small green bushes.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Chile by Palmerranian

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Alto Bio Bio National Reserve
metas.note: A vast, mostly treeless landscape combined with triple yellow lines are seen in Alto Bio Bio National Reserve. While the reserve may look dry, there is a distinct cold and high altitude feel.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Alto Bio Bio National Reserve - Monkey Puzzle Trees
metas.note: A vast, mostly treeless landscape combined with triple yellow lines are seen in Alto Bio Bio National Reserve. While the reserve may look dry, there is a distinct cold and high altitude feel. Monkey puzzles are also seen toward the east.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Alto Loa National Reserve
metas.note: Alto Loa National Reserve can be recognized by the vast, open landscape, followed by salt pans leading up to snow-capped volcanoes. The reserve does not have any paved roads.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Antofagasta Ridge
metas.note: A rockier, and more uneven ridge can be seen in Antofagasta.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Arica Mountains
metas.note: The province of Arica y Parinacota can be recognized by the smooth, sandy mountains that may look slightly eroded, or have bulbous formations. Valleys are also common, which are rarely seen in other parts of Chile.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Arica Ridge
metas.note: A slight, sandy ridge with a gradual incline can be seen in Arica.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Atacama Desert
metas.note:
The Atacama is an extremely arid desert covering the northern third of Chile. Some parts of it experience the lowest rainfall on the planet. As a result, many locations in this desert are almost completely devoid of any vegetation: you will often just see sand and bare rock without any plants in sight anywhere.

NOTE: The Atacama Desert also covers parts of southern Peru, western Bolivia and northwestern Argentina.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Atacama Mountains
metas.note: These rocky, uneven mountains are most commonly seen in Atacama and northern Coquimbo.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Brownish Red Soil (Gen 3)
metas.note:
This brownish red soil can sometimes be seen in Atacama province.

NOTE: This is most reliable in Generation 3. This soil can be seen in other provinces in Generation 4.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Chiloé Landscape
metas.note:
A rolling, agricultural landscape, comparable to New Zealand, can be seen on Isla Grande de Chiloé.

NOTE: Similar looking landscapes exist in some other parts of the country, but usually more level.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Dry Hills
metas.note: The region around Santiago can be recognized by its semi-arid climate, having dry hills and scattered vegetation.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Eucalyptus
metas.note: Eucalyptus plantations combined with a somewhat dry climate are a good indicator that you are in southwestern Valparaíso.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Iquique Ridge
metas.note: A large, towering ridge can be seen in Iquique.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Lauca National Park
metas.note:
East of Putre, Ruta 11 enters Lauca National Park which has a flatter landscape, with tall snow-capped mountains in the background, and features unique Andean Plateau vegetation like Peruvian feather grass and the recognizable cushion plant yareta (Azorella compacta). You can also find Chilean bollards lining the road, which are extremely rare.

Lauca can look very similar to other areas in the east Andes of northern Chile, but it’s recognizable for the iconic Volcán Parinacota, a tall snow-capped volcano that stands alone and away from other mountain ridges. It’s visible from basically every location in the park, though it can be shrouded by clouds.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Chile by Palmerranian

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Llanos de Challe National Park
metas.note: Llanos de Challe National Park can be recognized by the brown coloured dirt on the roadside, patches of light sand, juniper plants, and dark coloured mountains. The sky is overcast in most of the coverage.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Los Flamencos National Reserve
metas.note: Smooth mountains with a reddish tint are seen in Los Flamencos National Reserve. Salt pans are also a common sight. The reserve uses triple yellow lines.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Los FLamencos National Reserve - Short Dashes
metas.note: Smooth mountains with a reddish tint are seen in Los Flamencos National Reserve. Salt pans are also a common sight. The reserve uses triple yellow lines, with short dashes in the west.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Lush Green Valleys
metas.note: Lush green valleys, with rocky mountains and often overcast coverage, can be seen in southern Los Lagos and northern Aysén.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Maule Landscape
metas.note: Compared to the area around Santiago, the Maule province has a similar look. However, it has a Mediterranean climate, and is generally greener.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Narrow Roads & Trees
metas.note: Narrow roads with trees on both sides can commonly be seen in the provinces of Bio Bio and Araucania.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Nevado Tres Cruces National Park
metas.note: In the west, Nevado Tres Cruces National Park can be recognized by the vast, open landscape, followed by salt pans leading up to a line of mountains. The sand has a reddish tint.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Nevado Tres Cruces National Park - Snow
metas.note: In the east of this park, the Google Car drives up a mountain pass with views of lightly snow-capped volcanoes and snow on the side of the road. The roads in the National Park are paved.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Pampa del Tamarugal
metas.note: The northern section of Pampa del Tamarugal National Reserve can be recognized by the Tamarugo trees lining the road. The road itself is mediocre quality, and in a consistent north-west direction.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Pan de Azucar National Park
metas.note: Pan de Azucar National Park can be recognized by the brown coloured dirt on the roadside, patches of light sand, little vegetation, and dark coloured mountains. The sky is overcast in most of the coverage

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Puyehue National Park
metas.note: Puyehue National Park can be recognized by the dense vegetation surrounding the road. The pavement itself has triple yellow lines, and tar snakes are frequently seen.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Puyehue National Park - Dead Trees
metas.note: Puyehue National Park can be recognized by the dense vegetation surrounding the road. The pavement itself has triple yellow lines, and tar snakes are frequently seen. In the east, many dead trees can be seen with a lack of leaves.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Ruta 1
metas.note: Ruta 1 is a coastal road that is easily recognized by the wall of mountains to the east, and the Pacific Ocean to the west. This image shows the various weather conditions faced on the road to help you make closer guesses.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Ruta 181
metas.note: Ruta 181 leading up to Alto Bio Bio National Reserve has triple yellow lines, looks similar to the reserve but with more vegetation.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Ruta 41 - White Lines
metas.note: Part of Ruta 41 is located in a valley, with snowy mountains seen in the distance. Many trees and vineyards can commonly be seen toward the west. Triple white lines west of the middle between Balala and Miraflores.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Ruta 41 - Yellow Lines
metas.note: Part of Ruta 41 is located in a valley, with snowy mountains seen in the distance. Many trees and vineyards can commonly be seen toward the west. Triple yellow lines east of the middle between Balala and Miraflores.

metas.name: Chile - Landscape - Villa O'Higgins
metas.note: O’Higgins can be recognized by the large mountains to the east, often casting a shadow over the town. To the west, snow-capped mountains are seen further in the distance.

metas.name: Chile - Trekker - ACA
metas.note: ACA can be recognized by the many radio telescopes in a barren, snowy environment.

metas.name: Chile - Trekker - ALMA-OSF
metas.note: ALMA OSF can be recognized by the large radio telescopes and rural facilities.

metas.name: Chile - Trekker - Horse Trekker
metas.note:
This horse trekker can be seen to the northwest of San Filipe.

NOTE: A similar trekker can be found on the other side of the border in Argentina.

metas.name: Chile - Trekker - Torres Del Paine
metas.note: The Torres del Paine area can be recognized by the sharp peaked mountains, and the trekker walking on a glacier along with other people in orange helmets.

metas.name: Chile - Vegetation - Cactus Acido
metas.note: Eulychnia acida, commonly known as cactus ácido or copao, is a cactus species endemic to Chile, where it is primarily distributed in the semi-arid regions of the country. Its range includes: Atacama Region, Coquimbo Region,and Valparaíso Region.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Plant World - Cacti

metas.name: Chile - Vegetation - Chilean Rhubarb
metas.note: Chilean rhubarb can commonly be found on Isla Grande, and on the mainland east of it. Chilean rhubarb can be recognized by its large, cabbage-like appearance.

metas.name: Chile - Vegetation - Chilean Wine Palm
metas.note: It is endemic to a small area of central Chile between southern Coquimbo, Valparaíso, Santiago, O'Higgins, and northern Maule regions. They are highly concentrated around Viña del Mar.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Plant World - Palms by Zen

metas.name: Chile - Vegetation - Concepcion Pines
metas.note: Concepcion pines, scientifically named Pinus radiata, can be recognized by their puffy needles. They are most commonly found in Bio Bio, where the city of Concepcion is located, and less commonly in Ñuble and Araucania.

metas.name: Chile - Vegetation - Monkey Puzzle Tree
metas.note:
Monkey puzzles, scientifically named Araucaria araucana, are found in far eastern Araucania.

NOTE: Monkey puzzles can also be found on the other side of the Argentinian border.

metas.name: Chile - Vegetation - Purple Flowers
metas.note: These purple flowers, named Large-leaved Lupines, can commonly be found along Ruta 240.

metas.name: Colombia - Agriculture - Aracataca Cut Palms
metas.note: These palms where the crown has been cut, are very often found near Aracataca and some smaller towns North of it.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Agriculture - Banana
metas.note: In general, banana plantation can be found mostly in Quindio and Magdalena, sometimes in Northwest-Antioquia and Cordoba, and rarely in surrounding provinces of Quindio.
metas.footer: Colombia Guide for Geoguessr by vamponcrack

metas.name: Colombia - Agriculture - Banana - Cloudy Gen 3
metas.note:
Large amounts of banana plants in plantations are commonly found in different areas.

Paired with Cloudy Gen 3 Coverage, they're most common in Northwestern Antioquia.
metas.footer: Colombia Guide for Geoguessr by vamponcrack

metas.name: Colombia - Agriculture - Banana - Dry
metas.note: In Magdalena you will often see banana plantations in a dry sandy/dirty area with mountains to your east.
metas.footer: Source: Colombia Guide for Geoguessr by vamponcrack

metas.name: Colombia - Agriculture - Banana - Hedge
metas.note: In Quindio you will commonly find banana plantations behind hedges.
metas.footer: Source: Colombia Guide for Geoguessr by vamponcrack

metas.name: Colombia - Agriculture - Banana - Small Field / No Hedge
metas.note: In the states surrounding Quindio you will find smaller banana plantations along the road not behind hedges.
metas.footer: Source: Colombia Guide for Geoguessr by vamponcrack

metas.name: Colombia - Agriculture - Coffee
metas.note:
The coffee belt stretches in the valley between Medellin and Cali. In the North, you will only find it near the Venezuelan border.

Olives and Tea have a very similar distribution.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Agriculture - Common Guava
metas.note: Common Guava mostly appears in the valley between the western and the central mountain range in Colombia, but it can also appear in other valleys.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Agriculture - Guadua Bamboo
metas.note: Guadua Bamboo plantations are found mainly in Caldas, but also in the adjecent Tolima, Quindio and Risaralda.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Agriculture - Oil Palms
metas.note: Oilpalms can be found mainly in Meta and Casanare. They are also very common around the 45 near Fundacion and Aracataca. Sometimes, you can find them in Barrancabermeja.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Agriculture - Sugarcane
metas.note: Sugarcane will mainly be found in Cauca and Valle de Cauca.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Architecture - Guatape
metas.note: Bright Colored Houses & Unique Pavement.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Architecture - Straw/Thatched Roofs
metas.note: Houses with roofs like this are commonly found along the coast, especially near Cartagena and Barranquilla.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Car Meta - Gen 3 - white/blue striped car
metas.note: Gen 3 with the white-blue car follows a straight line between Cartagena and Medellín, has partial coverage along Route 80 west of Bosconia, as well as along Route 45 north of Bucaramanga and east of Medellín.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Car Meta - Gen 4 - Grey Car
metas.note: Gen 4 coverage with the grey car is not found north of Montería, has a gap between Bucaramanga and Bogotá, forms a 'staircase' pattern with right angles at Medellín and Bogotá, covers areas around Bucaramanga, and has a missing section around Popayán.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Car Meta - Gen 4 - White Car
metas.note: Gen 4 with the white car has no coverage south of Cali, very little around Medellín, and forms a curved pattern around Medellín.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Car Meta - Leticia
metas.note:
This unique vehicle can be found in and around Leticia, the Southernmost town in Colombia.

NOTE: The long concrete blocks seen in the bottom left corner are a reliable way of recognising the road North of Leticia.

metas.name: Colombia - Car Meta - Providencia
metas.note: The island of Providencia, located roughly 90 kilometres North of San Andrés, is home to this unique grey truck.

metas.name: Colombia - Car Meta - San Andres
metas.note: Coverage on the Caribbean island of San Andrés was taken by this distinct white car.

metas.name: Colombia - Coverage Meta - "Gen 5" Glitch
metas.note: A camera glitch that makes a part of the image look very saturated can be found in southern Colombia.

metas.name: Colombia - Coverage Meta - Arauca Rift
metas.note: On the road in Arauca and in the city of Arauca in northeastern Colombia, there is virtually only cloudy, bad weather coverage. Furthermore, there was a small camera glitch where you can see this small rift northeast of the driving direction.
metas.footer: Source: Tipp des Tages on the German Discord Server

metas.name: Colombia - Coverage Meta - Double Google Car
metas.note: A Second Google Car is visible in many random spots. The most prominent spots are the 26 in Cauca, Vda. Chontaduro (near Popoyan) and the road between Pital and Tarqui.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Coverage Meta - Double Google Car - Aguachica
metas.note: This instance of a second google car can be seen on Carrera 4, an offroad of the 45 near Aguachica.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Coverage Meta - Double Google Car - Villavicencio
metas.note: This instance of a second google car can be seen on the east-west road, directly south of Guayuriba River, which is south of Villavicencio.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Coverage Meta - Embalse Calima
metas.note: Large lake, mostly winter coverage. A small stretch also has summer coverage.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Coverage Meta - Foggy & Rainy Coverage
metas.note: If you see rainy coverage, combined with strong fog, you're on the 64.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Coverage Meta - Grey Car, 2023 copyright
metas.note: This constellation can be found on the 65 in Caqueta and the 45 in Putumayo.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Coverage Meta - La Florida
metas.note: Rainy coverage with very orange-brown soil can be found on this road to La Florida.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Coverage Meta - Rainy Coverage
metas.note: Rainy coverage is most common on the highways 20, 24, 50 and 64.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Coverage Meta - Sogamoso Lake
metas.note: If you see a lake, paired with an overexposed Gen 4 camera, you're probably on this lake south of Sogamoso.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Coverage Meta - Stick Meta
metas.note: This stick on the camera can be found between El Guio and El Boral (near the Cundinamarca-Meta border near Villavicencio)
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Coverage Meta - Unique Road - Tame to Arauca
metas.note: On this road, you can see a sunset through the clouds. It's not always easy to recognize, however.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Coverage Meta - Unique Road - Tame to Hato Corozal
metas.note: On this road, you can see a slight sunset through the clouds. It is pretty flat, with mountains in the Northwest.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Barichara Pavement
metas.note: This unique cobblestone pavement is found is the historic town of Barichara, Santander.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Barranquilla Roadbollard
metas.note: In Barranquilla, you can often find this bollard with roadnames on intersections.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Buenaventura Truck Spam Road
metas.note: The stretch of the 40 to Buenaventura is an important route for trucks, so if you see many trucks, it's worth a thought.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Caldas Polepaint
metas.note: orange & blue
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Cauca/Narino Polepaint
metas.note: Yellow with dark numbers
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Coastal Antioquia Polepaint
metas.note: Green paint with yellow numbers
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Electricity Counter - Oval
metas.note:
Usually pretty tall with oval windows, circle windows might not be as trustworthy.

Very common as there are few plastic counters in this region.
metas.footer: Source: The CoCo Document by Blinky

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - European Bollard
metas.note: This european-style (specifically spanish style bollard) is found in Cundinamarca, but also on the 40 towards Villavicencio.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - H-shaped lamp attachment
metas.note: H-shaped lamp attachment plates can be found in Bogota.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Huila Polepaint
metas.note: Orange paint with black numbers
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Ibague Lamp
metas.note:
This red lamp style is unique to Tolima province.

Note by MB: I only found it in Ibague, not in any other towns in Tolima. Also, the meta is more about the color and the shape of the lamp, not about the arrangement of the lights.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Megabus
metas.note: Green or yellow, modern bus. Often on a dedicated bus lane. Found in Pereira metropolitan area.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Pole Marking - Antioquia
metas.note: These pole markings with one short black strip on the top and bottom, and a longer yellow section in the middle, are most commonly found in the Antioquia department. Sometimes, you can find them in the Cordoba department as well.

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - QR-Code Sticker
metas.note: Found in Barranquilla and Santa Marta
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Rectangular lamp attachment
metas.note: Rectangular lamp attachment plates can be found mainly in Medellin, sometimes further North, especially in Monteria and Cucuta.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Risaralda/Choco Polepaint
metas.note: Yellow paint with red numbers. Found all over Risaralda and the towns of Istmina and Quibdo in Choco.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Sarawak Pole
metas.note: Asymmetrical poles with a "Sarawak" extension (a vertical stalk coming out the top), can often be found East of Andes. Note that this pole is not 100%, and has been spotted elsewhere.
metas.footer: Source: Meat of the Day on ScripterCord

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Spikes
metas.note: These spikes can be found on the 40 and the 62.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Street Lamps - Barranquilla
metas.note: The uniquely shaped supporting metal piece can be found in Barranquilla. (Similar to the Providencia design)

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Street Lamps - Providencia
metas.note: Providencia street lights are green and supported by a trapezoidal sheet of metal underneath. (The metal sheet without a green lamp can also be found in Barranquilla)

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Tinto Bus
metas.note: This red bus drives in the town (not the country) Armenia.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Tolima Poletag
metas.note: Orange tag with white numbers
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - TransLago vans
metas.note: TransLogo vans are common throughtout Boyaca Department. You will most often see them on the routes Tunja-Sogamoso and Tunja-Duitama.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Transmetro
metas.note: White Transmetro buses can be found in Barranquilla.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Tumaco
metas.note: If you see many puddles and a pavement out of '+' shaped stones, you're in Tumaco.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Valle de Cauca Pole
metas.note: If you see these poletops you will find yourself in Valle Del Cauca.
metas.footer: Source: Colombia Guide for Geoguessr by vamponcrack

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Valle de Cauca Polepaint
metas.note: Yellow, with black numbers. Several digits can be in one row.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Infrastructure - Villavicencio Bike Lane Road
metas.note: If you see a bike lane, and get East of Andes vibes, you're most likely on the road through Los Tobitos to Villavicencio.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Landscape - Deep grey & stony soil in Gen 3
metas.note: This type of soil can be found in towns near the pacific coast.

metas.name: Colombia - Landscape - East of Andes Landscape
metas.note:
East of the Andes lies a vast lowland called Llanos. It is characterised by open tropical grasslands, savannas with scattered trees, small areas of forest and seasonal flooding.

Since it's to the east of the Andes, you may see mountains in the west, but never in the east.

metas.name: Colombia - Landscape - Guatape Hill
metas.note: This striking cone-shaped mountain can often be seen from the surrounding area of Guatape.
metas.footer: Source: Tipp des Tages on the German Discord Server

metas.name: Colombia - Landscape - Guaviare Orange Road
metas.note: The only road in Guaviare goes from to Guaviare (city), and continues south up until Vda. El Trueno. It can be recognized by the orange-looking dust on the road.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Landscape - La Guajira
metas.note: This landscape is typical of the far Northern province of La Guajira: extreme dryness, low vegetation and occasional cacti.

metas.name: Colombia - Landscape - Northern Landscape
metas.note: The Northern part of the country is characterised by white, sandy soil and an arid landscape.

metas.name: Colombia - Landscape - Paramos
metas.note:
Paramos refers to alpine tundra ecosystems located in the mountains. These kinds of regions are easy to guess by how little vegetation grows here. The best clue is these odd looking pants. ( giant rosette plants ).

Note by MB: In my experience, this appears most commonly south of Bogota, still in the capital district.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Landscape - Pasto Hills
metas.note:
In southern Colombia, around the city of Pasto, there are hilly fields that are unique in that they are bordered by hedges. The hedges are very thick and form very distinctive lines on the hills. It almost gives off a “British” vibe. If you are sure that it is Colombia, this is a very good meta, but such fields with hedges also occur in Ecuador.

!! In very rare cases, such hedges on hills can also occur in other parts of Colombia. !!
metas.footer: Source: Tipp des Tages on the German Discord Server

metas.name: Colombia - Landscape - Santa Rosalia
metas.note: Santa Rosalia is the only town covered in Vichada. So if you see red/orange dirt in an urban Gen 4 loc, you should go there.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Landscape - Swamp Road + Extremely Sunny
metas.note: If you see a swamp road with extremely sunny coverage, you're probably on the 74 in Sucre.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Landscape - Swamp Roads
metas.note: The 74, the 78 and a few other roads more north have very swampy parts, you can see on the map where these are by zooming.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Landscape - Unique Road - 78 west of Pailitas
metas.note: This road is characterised by low clouds and a towering mountain in the east.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/colombia for more clues.

metas.name: Colombia - Landscape - Unique Road - Ruta 90 Landbridge
metas.note:
You can recognise the narrow Ruta 90 landbridge between Barranquilla and Cienaga thanks to the dashed yellow lines and shallow bodies of water next to the road. Open ocean can often be seen to the north.

NOTE: In the older Generation 3 coverage, you will also see tall mountains in the distance.

metas.name: Colombia - Landscape - Unique Road - Uribia to Puerto Boliviar
metas.note: You can often recognise the Uribia-Puerto Bolivar road because of La Guajira landscape (extreme dryness, low vegetation and occasional cacti), the straightness and the train track always present to the East.

metas.name: Colombia - Landscape - Vichada Red Dirt
metas.note: Vichada is characterize by hazy Gen 4 coverage and Red Dirt.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Misc - Afro-Colombians
metas.note: As a result of slave trade, the Pacific coast of Colombia is home to an overwhelming majority of Afro-Colombians.

metas.name: Colombia - Trekker - Trebal Resort Trekker
metas.note: This trekker can be recognized by the unique pavement and houses.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Vegetation - Cacti
metas.note: Cacti are most commonly found in the North near Valledupar. Sometimes they can appear in Huila, too.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Vegetation - Colombian Mahogany
metas.note: This tree is found mainly around Medellin, but it has been spotted in other random spots.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Vegetation - Kapok Tree
metas.note: The Kapok tree can be found throughout Colombia, but is most common between the central and eastern mountain range.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Vegetation - Quindio Wax Palm
metas.note: This palm is found in mountainous regions of Colombia, mainly in Quindio, as the name suggests.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Colombia - Vegetation - Veracruz Trees
metas.note: In Colombia you will most commonly find these trees that appear to have a knot on top of their trunk in the dark red areas. The province of Cordoba has the most gen 4 out of the others so if you see these in gen 4 consider Cordoba. (If the area is flat/semi hilly, You can find these trees in the mountains aswell everywhere)
metas.footer: Source: Colombia Guide for Geoguessr by vamponcrack

metas.name: Colombia - Vegetation - Wide Trees
metas.note: These wide trees, usually near fences, are found in Northern regions, especially near Monteria and Sincelejo.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Coverage Meta - 29 south of Ibri
metas.note: Road 29 south of Ibri features a fairly shrubby landscape, with low and jagged mountains on the eastern side of the road. The low-lying sun to the northwest is particularly distinct.

metas.name: Coverage Meta - 37 (Sunset Coverage)
metas.note: Road 37 travels in a generally northwest direction through a very generic, flat desert landscape. The angle is one of the best clues for this road. On the northern half, you can find distinct sunset coverage.

metas.name: Coverage Meta - 42 south of Shalim
metas.note: Just south of Shalim, you’ll find a stretch of overcast coverage, along with a power line to the west of the road.

metas.name: Coverage Meta - 43 south of Ubar
metas.note: Road 43, also south of Ubar, is unpaved and features sunset coverage along with a dust trail behind the car.

metas.name: Coverage Meta - 45
metas.note: Roads 45 and the western stretch of 39 both feature a similar slightly hilly desert landscape, sunny weather, and a general east-to-west direction. What makes them unique is the light-coloured shoulders the roads share, though it is most pronounced on Road 45. The roads also mostly have a faded white middle line. To tell the 45 and western 39 apart, look at the sun, which is overhead on the 39, but to the west on 45. The section north of Mudayy is also the 45, but unlabelled on Google Maps.

metas.name: Coverage Meta - Dirty Gen 2 Halo
metas.note: In some of New South Wales’ Generation 2, the halo looks very dirty. This is most common west of ACT and south of Barrington Tops.

metas.name: Coverage Meta - Hazy Adam
metas.note: In and close to Adam, the coverage is usually quite hazy, and the ridge and hills from the previous tip can be seen to the north. Though sometimes, only one or two are visible. Unlike north of Adam, you won’t see mountains in any other direction.

metas.name: Coverage Meta - Max South 32
metas.note: The southernmost section of Road 32 has a somewhat hilly landscape. The puffy cumulus clouds are what make this stretch recognisable. You can also look for the power line that runs west of the road for confirmation.

metas.name: Coverage Meta - Max West 39
metas.note: Roads 45 and the western stretch of 39 both feature a similar slightly hilly desert landscape, sunny weather, and a general east-to-west direction. What makes them unique is the light-coloured shoulders the roads share, though it is most pronounced on Road 45. The roads also mostly have a faded white middle line. To tell the 45 and western 39 apart, look at the sun, which is overhead on the 39, but to the west on 45. The section north of Mudayy is also the 45, but unlabelled on Google Maps.

metas.name: Coverage Meta - Ruta 21
metas.note: Generation 4 sunset coverage can be seen on Ruta 21 from Calama to San Francisco de Chiu Chiu. In the west near Calama, the sun has just started to set, causing a giant white dome in the sky. In the east, the sky has a warm gradient, and the tops of the volcanoes are seen glowing pink.

metas.name: Coverage Meta - Western 41 - Cloudy
metas.note: The western stretch of Road 41 has wide shoulders similar to Road 31, however, the more northwest-bound angle along with the reddish soil should tell them apart. The eastern half has cloudy coverage.

metas.name: France - Agriculture - Breeding
metas.note: It is not so rare to see cows, horses, or sheep in France in Geoguessr. If that ever happens, you should consider the West of the country (Brittany, Normandy), as well as the mountainous regions (Pyrenees and Alps). This is where you have the most chances to find animals in France in Google Street View.
metas.footer: Source: France Tips for Geoguessr by Guigz

metas.name: France - Agriculture - Corn
metas.note: Corn fields are mostly located in the Western part of the country, as well as in some areas in the East of Paris, and around Lyon and Strasbourg.
metas.footer: Source: France Tips for Geoguessr by Guigz

metas.name: France - Agriculture - Lavender Fields
metas.note: Lavender fields can be found in the southeast, appearing as small grey bushes when not fully grown.

metas.name: France - Agriculture - Salt Farms
metas.note: Salt farms, which appear as flooded trenches with grass medians, are unique to the west coastal islands of Île de Ré and Île d'Oléron as well as the nearby coast, as well as some very niche areas in the South of France (Camargue).
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & France Tips for Geoguessr by Guigz

metas.name: France - Agriculture - Sunflower
metas.note: Sunflowers are mostly found in the southwest of the country, particularly around Toulouse.

metas.name: France - Agriculture - Wine
metas.note: France is the second largest wine producer in the world, with many famed wine regions. The most common include the area around Bordeaux, southern coast and Champagne, East of Paris. Other regions include, but are not limited to, Loire Valley, Alsace and Corsica.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & France Tips for Geoguessr by Guigz

metas.name: France - Architecture - Alpine Architecture
metas.note:
Alpine architecture, unmistakable for its light coloured base and extensive wooden elements, is unsurprisingly found in the Alps.

NOTE: Similar houses can be found in the touristic parts of Pyrenees.

metas.name: France - Architecture - Basque Architecture
metas.note:
White houses with, often colourful, timber framing are a staple of Basque architecture that extends beyond the Basque speaking area. The timber frame colour (in this case red) will be consistent with other wooden elements, like window shutters and gates.

NOTE: They’re also common in parts of Northern Spain, where the timber frames are usually unpainted.

metas.name: France - Architecture - Belle-Île-en-Mer Architecture
metas.note:
On the Breton island Belle-Île-en-Mer you can find houses typical for Brittany combined with colourful façades and outlines, superficially similar to houses in Portugal.

NOTE: The entire island was only covered with an often oversaturated Generation 2 camera.

metas.name: France - Architecture - Black Shingle Roof
metas.note: Black shingle roofs are primarily found in the northwest, the rough cutoff being the Loire river. Other areas include near the Belgian border, the south-centre, and the Pyrenees, making black roofs a good clue for Alps-Pyrenees toss-ups.

metas.name: France - Architecture - Black Shingle Roofs with Mountains
metas.note: Black shingle roofs are often found in the Pyrenees, making black roofs a good clue for Alps-Pyrenees toss-ups.

metas.name: France - Architecture - Brick House / Black Roof
metas.note:
Found in the North (mostly Belgium border)

Note by MB: Brick Houses also often have Red Roofs. Houses with Black Roofs do not appear around Toulouse (unlike those with red roofs).

What I find more useful to differentiate the roof types is the materials. "Black Roofs" are shingles, while "Red Roofs" are actual tiles (which can also get very dark)
metas.footer: Source: France Tips for Geoguessr by Guigz

metas.name: France - Architecture - Brick House / Red Rooftiles
metas.note:
Brick roofs with red rooftiles can be found in the North mostly. Sometimes, they're also found around Toulouse.

Note by MB: With red tiles, Toulouse is an option, with black shingles, it isn't. What I find more useful to differentiate the roof types is the materials. "Black Roofs" are shingles, while "Red Roofs" are actual tiles (which can also get very dark)
metas.footer: Source: France Tips for Geoguessr by Guigz

metas.name: France - Architecture - Brittany Architecture
