metas.note: Brittany has one of the most recognizable and consistent architectures in the country. Common elements include, in addition to black roofs, edge chimneys, black slate walls and stones surrounding doors and windows. The walls will be either very light coloured or made of stone.

metas.name: France - Architecture - Germanic Architecture
metas.note:
Many elements of Germanic architecture are concentrated in Alsace, such as timber framing and half-hip roof. Furthermore, roofs with fish scale tiles are more common in this region.

Beware that these elements are sometimes incorporated into architecture in other parts of France, and are most reliable in conjunction with one another.

metas.name: France - Architecture - Ile de France Architecture
metas.note: Walls made of uneven cream coloured to orange stones, glued with mortar and often incorporating red brick details can be found in the towns surrounding Paris. Note that the city of Paris itself generally does not have this architecture.

metas.name: France - Architecture - Mansard Roof
metas.note:
Mansard roofs, also known as French windows, are a very common feature of Parisian architecture. They’re made up of steep black shingle roofs with inserted dormer windows. While not unique to Paris, it is a good clue in abundance and on wide boulevards.

On some occasions, they can also be found in the North of France.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & France Tips for Geoguessr by Guigz

metas.name: France - Architecture - Old Toulouse Architecture
metas.note: In and around Toulouse, mainly in old towns, you will commonly find bright orange brick buildings. They differ from brick houses near Belgium by the bricks being brighter, as well as somewhat Mediterranean looking architectural features, such as wooden shutters, being common.

metas.name: France - Architecture - Stone House / Black Shingle Roof
metas.note:
Found in Western France, mainly in Bretagne.

Note by MB: What I find more useful to differentiate the roof types is the materials. "Black Roofs" are shingles, while "Red Roofs" are actual tiles (which can also get very dark)
metas.footer: Source: France Tips for Geoguessr by Guigz

metas.name: France - Architecture - Stone House / Red Rooftiles
metas.note:
Can be found all over France, but mainly central and southern.

Note by MB: What I find more useful to differentiate the roof types is the materials. "Black Roofs" are shingles, while "Red Roofs" are actual tiles (which can also get very dark)
metas.footer: Source: France Tips for Geoguessr by Guigz

metas.name: France - Architecture - U-Tiles
metas.note: Roofs in the south of the country will often be made up of rounded tiles overlapping one another, often varying in colour.

metas.name: France - Architecture - West Coast Architecture
metas.note: The houses along the West Coast, from Nantes to Bayonne are usually low, with white walls, and red roofs.
metas.footer: Source: France Tips for Geoguessr by Guigz

metas.name: France - Car Meta - Rare Antenna - Black & White
metas.note:
On rare occasions, you may find a flag attached to the antenna in the generation 3 coverage. While much of the highlighted areas has been overwritten, learning the distribution of each antenna can yield very high scores.

The black/white flag can be found in Calvados, Orne, Eastern Bourgogne and Loire/Haut de Loire

metas.name: France - Car Meta - Rare Antenna - Blue
metas.note:
On rare occasions, you may find a flag attached to the antenna in the generation 3 coverage. While much of the highlighted areas has been overwritten, learning the distribution of each antenna can yield very high scores.

The blue flag can be found in Bas-Rhin, Aube and the Correze/Haute-Vienne/Dordogne Tristate

metas.name: France - Car Meta - Rare Antenna - Red
metas.note:
On rare occasions, you may find a flag attached to the antenna in the generation 3 coverage. While much of the highlighted areas has been overwritten, learning the distribution of each antenna can yield very high scores.

The red flag can be found in the eastern part of the Nord-Department

metas.name: France - Infrastructure - Azure Blue Signpost
metas.note:
On the French Riviera (Côte d'Azur in French, literally translated as Blue Coast), you can find regular traffic signposts painted azure blue. Uniquely, Cagnes-sur-mer, west of Nice, will feature lighter, powder blue infrastructure.

NOTE: Blue infrastructure can be found to a lesser extent all across France, particularly Brittany, so consider the landscape as well.

metas.name: France - Infrastructure - Bordeaux Signpost
metas.note:
In the outskirts of Bordeaux, you may find square traffic signposts with the Bordeaux shade of red, named after the wine grown in the region.

NOTE: Red posts by themselves are not unique to Bordeaux, so apply this meta with caution.

metas.name: France - Infrastructure - Bordeaux Streetsign
metas.note: Small tables with 'Arrᵗ' written on a small separate sign, are found in Bordeaux, despite being a city not divided into arrondissements.

metas.name: France - Infrastructure - Brown Signback
metas.note:
Road signs where both the post and back are painted brown are most commonly found in Seine-et-Marne, and rarely in Ille-et-Vilaine. It is more reliable when the post is square, however round signposts are equally common.

NOTE: Beware that this, and other colored infrastructure can rarely be found in other parts of the country.

metas.name: France - Infrastructure - Cityname Roadsign
metas.note:
Street signs in the metropolitan area of Paris often say the name of the city, which is generally atypical for street signs in France. The signs will often be made in a modern design, and many city names will be river based, notably named after Seine and Marne.

NOTE: This can be seen sporadically throughout the country, so consider other clues.

metas.name: France - Infrastructure - Cuboid Barrier
metas.note:
Cuboid barriers made of stones and mortar are commonly found on Corsica. While by no means unique to Corsica, it is good to consider the island when you see them in rounds with a plausible Mediterranean landscape.

NOTE: Stone barriers with a rounded top are not found on Corsica.

metas.name: France - Infrastructure - Dark Green Signpost
metas.note:
Dark green road signposts and backs are most commonly found in Brittany and around Paris, but also various southern regions in the country.

NOTE: Beware that this, and other colored infrastructure can rarely be found in other parts of the country.

metas.name: France - Infrastructure - Eure-et-Loir Sticker
metas.note: Signbacks in Eure-et-Loir may include a green sticker, the department’s logo. They’re usually placed on a dark green back, without a matching post.

metas.name: France - Infrastructure - Grey Signback / Green Signpost
metas.note:
A greyish green signback supported by a darker green post, is found in three areas: Brittany (Côtes-d'Armor and eastern half of Ille-et-Vilaine), Pyrénées-Atlantiques and rarely near the Alps.

NOTE: Beware that this, and other colored infrastructure can rarely be found in other parts of the country.

metas.name: France - Infrastructure - Lille Streetsign
metas.note: Street signs with a red slanted fleur-de-lis are unique to Lille.

metas.name: France - Infrastructure - Lyon Streetsign
metas.note:
Lyon’s street signs feature four corner bolts and an uninterrupted inner white border that cuts a notch for the arrondissement and each bolt.

NOTE: Outside Lyon proper, the street sign will display the name of the suburb instead.

metas.name: France - Infrastructure - Marseille Streetsign
metas.note: Marseille’s street signs will usually feature the city’s emblem, a variation of the Greek cross. The white border will usually be interrupted at the top, even when the cross is absent.

metas.name: France - Infrastructure - Montpellier Streetsign
metas.note: Montpellier street signs will typically contain a blue ‘M’ on a white background in the top left corner.

metas.name: France - Infrastructure - Paris Streetsign
metas.note:
Paris uses an iconic green & Prussian blue design with a top arch that has also been replicated in Bucharest, which is sometimes referred to as Paris of the east.

NOTE: The simple rectangular form of the sign can be found in the towns nearby and rarely in other cities.

metas.name: France - Infrastructure - Pas-de-Calais Sign
metas.note:
In the Pas-de-Calais department, you may find road signs with the following colour arrangement: a dark green post paired with a signback of a lighter shade of green, ranging from matcha green to greenish turquoise. The department’s logo, a green and blue triangle, is occasionally present on the signback.

NOTE: Under certain lighting, they can appear similar to the greyish road signs. Also, beware that this, and other colored infrastructure can rarely be found in other parts of the country.

metas.name: France - Infrastructure - Powder Blue Infrastructure
metas.note: Uniquely, Cagnes-sur-mer, west of Nice, will feature lighter, powder blue infrastructure.

metas.name: France - Infrastructure - Reddish Road
metas.note:
Roads with a significant red, purple or burgundy tint are most commonly found in an area between Paris and Dijon, with Normandy being a notable exception. The historical region of Burgundy, which gave the name to the shade of red, roughly corresponds to the highlighted area.

NOTE: Normal roads may deceptively look reddish under some lighting, so use this with caution.

metas.name: France - Infrastructure - Thin B-Type Guardrail
metas.note:
Thin B type guardrail, typical for Czechia and Slovakia, is sometimes found on highways in the northern half of the country, often coming from Le Mans, Tours, Paris, Reims and Metz.

NOTE: On the highlighted sections, thin B can be the minority guardrail, and short sections of any highway will have no guardrails at all. It is also more common on smaller roads in the North, but less consistent as a clue.

metas.name: France - Infrastructure - Wind Turbine
metas.note: Wind turbines are considerably more common in the north of the country.

metas.name: France - Infrastructure - Yellow Front License Plates
metas.note: France can sometimes have yellow back license plates, especially in old coverage. Should you see several yellow plates on the front, you're probably near Luxembourg.

metas.name: France - Landscape - British Hedges
metas.note:
Rural roads surrounded by hedges blocking the view, reminiscent of the British Isles, are primarily found in the northwest, particularly in Normandy.

NOTE: Hedges by themselves are not sufficient for recognizing this area and are common all over France.

metas.name: France - Landscape - Cote d'Azur
metas.note: The French Riviera (Cote d'Azur) will mirror many characteristics of Monaco. Rich areas with planted palms and light coloured multi story buildings with wide balconies are good indications you’re in this area, with the rest of the southern coast and Corsican Bastia sharing similar vibes.

metas.name: France - Landscape - La Beauce
metas.note:
La Beauce is one of the flattest regions of France, located South of Paris.

Apart from the flatness of the area, the important thing to notice about the fields in the Beauce region is that they are industrialized. You will not see hedges around the fields like you could see in the West of France. So, if you see very flat and industrialized fields with potatoes or cereals, you can be in this area. Still, the Paris hedge remains good because there are many fields North and East of Paris (but you will never get a 5K by guessing Paris out of fields).
metas.footer: Source: France Tips for Geoguessr by Guigz

metas.name: France - Landscape - Mountains
metas.note: The tallest mountains are found in the southeast and on the Spanish border.

metas.name: France - Language - Alsatian
metas.note: Alsatian, a dialect of German, is occasionally found in Alsace, a region that changed countries 4 times in modern history. Most bilingual street signs use some variation of gasse or strasse.

metas.name: France - Language - Basque
metas.note:
Bilingual signs in Basque, a language isolate, are concentrated In the western half of the Pyrénées-Atlantiques department, bordering the Basque speaking regions in Spain. Common letters include K, X and Z. On directional signs, it’s written with a thinner font, which is unique within all minority languages in France.

The word for street is karrika, in contrast to “kalea” in the Spanish Basque country.

metas.name: France - Language - Breton
metas.note: Breton is a Celtic language, visually most similar to Welsh. Common letters include d, k, w and the letter ñ, which is not found in French. It is commonly found on the Breton peninsula, with bilingual street signs as east as Rennes and rarely Nantes. The Breton word for street is straed.

metas.name: France - Language - Catalan
metas.note:
The far southern department Pyrénées-Orientales, also known as Catalunya Nord (Northern Catalonia), uses Catalan on their various signage.

It is closely related to both Spanish and French, with Ç being considerably more common than in French. The word for street is carrer.

metas.name: France - Language - Corsican
metas.note: On the island of Corsica, you may find bilingual signs in Corsican, a Romance language that utilises many features found in Italian, like words almost always ending in vowels. In particular, the endings u/iu/ju, changed from o/io, are common in Corsican. Moreover, placenames will usually have an Italian origin.

metas.name: France - Language - German Roadnames
metas.note: Streets containing German names are concentrated in Alsace.

metas.name: France - Language - Occitan
metas.note: Occitan is a Romance language closely related to Catalan that’s sparsely concentrated in the South of France, most often found on street signs in big cities, and very rarely on town entry signs. It can be divided into dialects, each using a slightly different word for street, all similar to Catalan “carrer”. For example, in Toulouse, you’ll find the Languedocian carrièra and in Avignon carriero, in the Provençal dialect

metas.name: France - Language - Occitan - Carriera
metas.note: Different dialects of Occitan use different words for 'road'. Carriera can be found in South Central France.

metas.name: France - Language - Occitan - Carriero
metas.note: Different dialects of Occitan use different words for 'road'. Carriero can be found in South-Eastern Coastal France.

metas.name: France - Language - Plou- Prefix
metas.note: Towns with the Plou- prefix are concentrated in Northwestern Brittany.

metas.name: France - Language - Town Suffix: -ac
metas.note: Knowing basic toponymy in France is crucial for regionguessing, particularly suffixes. -ac can be found in the Southwestern Quarter of France and in Brittany.

metas.name: France - Language - Town Suffix: -ach
metas.note: Knowing basic toponymy in France is crucial for regionguessing, particularly suffixes. -ach can be found in Alsace.

metas.name: France - Language - Town Suffix: -anjou
metas.note: Knowing basic toponymy in France is crucial for regionguessing, particularly suffixes. -anjou can be found in Maine-et-Loire.

metas.name: France - Language - Town Suffix: -as
metas.note: Knowing basic toponymy in France is crucial for regionguessing, particularly suffixes. -as can be found in the Southern half of France.

metas.name: France - Language - Town Suffix: -at
metas.note: Knowing basic toponymy in France is crucial for regionguessing, particularly suffixes. -at can be found in the Central South of France.

metas.name: France - Language - Town Suffix: -ay
metas.note: Knowing basic toponymy in France is crucial for regionguessing, particularly suffixes. -ay can be found in the Northern half of France.

metas.name: France - Language - Town Suffix: -bearn
metas.note: Knowing basic toponymy in France is crucial for regionguessing, particularly suffixes. -bearn can be found in Pyrenees Atlantique.

metas.name: France - Language - Town Suffix: -beauce
metas.note: Knowing basic toponymy in France is crucial for regionguessing, particularly suffixes. -beauce can be found between Essone and Vendome.

metas.name: France - Language - Town Suffix: -bresse
metas.note: Knowing basic toponymy in France is crucial for regionguessing, particularly suffixes. -bresse can be found on the border between Jura and Saone-et-Loire.

metas.name: France - Language - Town Suffix: -brie
metas.note: Knowing basic toponymy in France is crucial for regionguessing, particularly suffixes. -brie can be found in Seine-Et-Marne

metas.name: France - Language - Town Suffix: -caux
metas.note: Knowing basic toponymy in France is crucial for regionguessing, particularly suffixes. -caux can be found in Seine-Maritime

metas.name: France - Language - Town Suffix: -court
metas.note: Knowing basic toponymy in France is crucial for regionguessing, particularly suffixes. -court can be found in Hauts-de-France and Grand-Est

metas.name: France - Language - Town Suffix: -ey
metas.note: Knowing basic toponymy in France is crucial for regionguessing, particularly suffixes. -ey can be found on the eastern border, in Normandy and in the Southwest.

metas.name: France - Language - Town Suffix: -heim
metas.note: Knowing basic toponymy in France is crucial for regionguessing, particularly suffixes. -heim can be found in Alsace.

metas.name: France - Language - Town Suffix: -iller
metas.note: Knowing basic toponymy in France is crucial for regionguessing, particularly suffixes. -iller can be found in Alsace.

metas.name: France - Language - Town Suffix: -quercy
metas.note: Knowing basic toponymy in France is crucial for regionguessing, particularly suffixes. -quercy can be found in Lot and Tarn-et-Garonne

metas.name: France - Language - Town Suffix: -touraine
metas.note: Knowing basic toponymy in France is crucial for regionguessing, particularly suffixes. -touraine can be found in Indre-et-Loire.

metas.name: France - Language - Town Suffix: -ville
metas.note: Knowing basic toponymy in France is crucial for regionguessing, particularly suffixes. -ville can be found in Grand-Est and Normandy, and sometimes in between.

metas.name: France - Language - Water Town Name
metas.note:
Many French cities contain the name of the river they lay on, usually in the format -sur-[river]. On signage, sur are often shortened to ˢ/, in this case Chalonnes-sur-Loire (Chalonnes upon Loire). The picture shows five of the longest and therefore most common origins of river based names, but cities can bear the name of any river, regardless of length.

Similarly, city names containing -sur-mer (=on sea) or -plage (=beach) are found exclusively on the coast.

metas.name: France - Trekker - Boat Trekker
metas.note: Several cities along the Cote d'Azur host boat trekkers in their harbours.

metas.name: France - Vegetation - Maritime Pine Forest
metas.note: Forests made up entirely of Maritime pines (pinus pinaster) are found in the southwest of the country (Gironde and Landes departments). The whole area will be fairly flat, which is not typical of other areas with such pines.

metas.name: France - Vegetation - Meditteranean Vegetation
metas.note:
The vegetation near the South-East coast looks very Mediterranean.

Note by MB: This is more of a vibe thing tbh.
metas.footer: Source: France Tips for Geoguessr by Guigz

metas.name: France - Vegetation - Stone Pine
metas.note: Stone pines are commonly found along the southern coast, often planted alongside urban roads. You may however find them as north as Nantes.

metas.name: Germany - Agriculture - Hop
metas.note: Hop fields are mainly found between Ingolstadt and Landshut - an area called 'Hallertau/Holledau' in Bavaria. There are some minor regions in Thuringia, Saxony-Anhalt and Saxony as well.

metas.name: Germany - Agriculture - Vineyards
metas.note: There are 13 wine regions in Germany. They are mostly concentrated in the southwest of Germany. However, there are a couple regions further east as well, along the border between Thuringia and Saxony-Anhalt, as well as along the Elbe in Saxony.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt, Deutsches Weininstitut

metas.name: Germany - Architecture - Arches in Half-Timbered houses
metas.note: This type of half-timbered house with arches at the ground floor is very common in this region of Saxony.

metas.name: Germany - Architecture - Commie Blocks
metas.note: These large, utilitarian apartment buildings constructed during the socialist era, that are also known as 'Commie blocks' are common in all of former East Germany.

metas.name: Germany - Architecture - Fishscale Walls
metas.note: Houses with black slate walls, resembling fish scales, are commonly found in a large area of central Germany.

metas.name: Germany - Architecture - Frisian Architecture
metas.note: Thatched roofs and rock walls are most common on the North Frisian Islands, as well as mainland Schleswig-Holstein. You can also commonly find them in coastal resort towns in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern.

metas.name: Germany - Architecture - Red Brick
metas.note:
These brick houses are generally concentrated in northwestern Germany.

NOTE: This map is very approximate.

metas.name: Germany - Camera Meta - Low Cam
metas.note: Lowcam coverage can be found around Singen and near Switzerland.

metas.name: Germany - Car Meta - Gen 3 / Antenna
metas.note: This rare Generation 3 car coverage with an antenna can be found in central Hamburg (Speicherstadt). Note by MB: This is officially a trekker, so you won't find any copyright.

metas.name: Germany - Car Meta - Gen 3 Black Car
metas.note:
You can find a Generation 3 black car in this safari park southeast of Bielefeld.

You can commonly see 4x4s painted with a zebra pattern in the park.

NOTE: This car is unique to this park within all of Europe.

metas.name: Germany - Car Meta - White/Black Gen 4 Car
metas.note:
You can find this rare white and black Generation 4 car in Hamburg and around Frankfurt.

NOTE: You can also find the same car around London and in Ireland.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - ALDI Nord
metas.note: There are two regional Aldi chains, which have split Germany in two; Aldi Süd in the south, and Aldi Nord in the north.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - ALDI Süd
metas.note: There are two regional Aldi chains, which have split Germany in two; Aldi Süd in the south, and Aldi Nord in the north.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Black Disk Bollard
metas.note: Bollards standing on these black disks are commonly found in all of eastern Germany.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Bus Stop - Berlin
metas.note: Berlin uses segmented bus stops, with a yellow signpost.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Bus Stop - Bremen
metas.note: Bremen proper uses simple bus stops, which have the bus stop name within a red section. The edges can be rounded.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Bus Stop - Bremerhaven
metas.note: Bremerhaven, which is still part of Bremen, uses bus stops with a grey section on the opposite side of the signpost. And the bus stop name is red within a yellow section.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Bus Stop - Hamburg
metas.note: Hamburg bus stops have a red signpost, and the route numbers are within hexagons. Note that they can be found outside of Hamburg as well

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Capped Bollard
metas.note: Some bollards in North Rhine-Westphalia have a green bit at the top. The top can also be another colour.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Cologne Lamppost Plate
metas.note:
Lampposts in Cologne will often feature these bright yellow numbers on a black piece of plastic.

NOTE: Similar looking things can be found elsewhere as well.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Curved Poletop
metas.note: Pole tops which have a curved horizontal bar can be found in Bavaria, though they are rare.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Dark Reflector
metas.note: Bollards with darker reflectors than usual are commonly found in Schleswig-Holstein, Niedersachsen, Nordrhein-Westfalen, Bavaria. They can sometimes be found in Baden-Württemberg and rarely in Hesse.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Double Connector Signback
metas.note: The double connector signback is very common in Schleswig-Holstein and Mecklenburg-Vorpommern. It is also found in Brandenburg. Rarely, you may see it in Saxony, Rhineland-Palatinate or Hamburg.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Folded Sign
metas.note: Folded Signs are most common in Bremen, then Saxony-Anhalt and Saarland.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Grey Bollard Plate
metas.note: Baden-Württemberg is the only state where the plates on the bollards can be grey instead of white.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Lower Half Missing Bollard
metas.note: These irregular looking bollards, which do not have a white encasing on the bottom half, are found on K-roads in this region of Lower Saxony, around Lüneburg. K-Roads in this region will not have any other type of bollard.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Lower Saxony km Marker
metas.note: You can find these simple rectangular markers, with rounded edges in Lower Saxony.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - LVR Cap
metas.note: Some of the green caps will have the text ‘LVR’, along with a small coat of arms. These specific green caps are unique to southern North Rhine-Westphalia.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Metal Border km Marker - Lower Saxony
metas.note: These markers with a metallic border around the marker itself are found in Schleswig-Holstein and Lower Saxony. The numbers after the comma are usually smaller on the markers in Lower Saxony.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Metal Border km Marker - Schleswig-Holstein
metas.note: These markers with a metallic border around the marker itself are found in Schleswig-Holstein and Lower Saxony. The numbers after the comma are usually smaller on the markers in Lower Saxony (So if that's not the case go SchleHo)

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - No-Fold Signback
metas.note: Non-folded signbacks are most common in Schleswig-Holstein, Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, Hesse, Hamburg, Bremen, then Brandenburg, Saxony, Baden-Württemberg.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Orange Bollard Plate
metas.note: Rhineland-Palatinate is the only state where the plates on the bollards are orange instead of white.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Orange Posts
metas.note: These simple orange posts are most commonly found in Bavaria, and also in the other highlighted states.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Red Bicycle Sign
metas.note: Red bicycle signs can be found in Northrhine-Westphalia, Southern Lower Saxony and Hamburg.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Red Cap Bollard
metas.note: These white posts with a red cap are found in all of former East Germany, but most commonly in the state of Saxony-Anhalt.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Round Concrete Poles
metas.note: These round concrete poles are almost unique to Former Eastern Germany.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Saarland Bicycle Sign
metas.note: These dark-green designs can be found in Saarland only.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Schleswig-Holstein Bicycle Sign
metas.note: Schleswig-Holstein sometimes uses slightly different cycling sign designs. For the one with town-names, note the difference in the arrow. For the one without, the shape is different.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Streetsigns - Berlin
metas.note: Berlin uses white signs with a grey border, and a separate section for numbers under the street name. Also note how the letter ß looks.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Streetsigns - Darmstadt
metas.note: Streetsigns in Darmstadt are white and often are written in ALL CAPS, which is unique in Germany.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Streetsigns - Dortmund
metas.note: Dortmund uses blue signs with a white border and a grey frame. The signs also have a separate section for numbers under the street name.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Streetsigns - Dresden
metas.note: Dresden has blue signs with a unique font.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Streetsigns - Düsseldorf
metas.note: Düsseldorf has black signs with a white border, similar to Munich. The signs have a metallic frame.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Streetsigns - Essen
metas.note: Essen has blue signs with a very thick metallic frame.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Streetsigns - Frankfurt
metas.note: Frankfurt uses blue street signs with a metallic border around the sign, as well as the separate section for numbers under the street name.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Streetsigns - Hanover
metas.note: Hanover uses white signs with a wider than usual gap between the sign and metallic frame.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Streetsigns - Mainz
metas.note: Mainz has a mix of blue signs, and this unique red variant.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Streetsigns - Munich
metas.note: Munich has blue street signs with a white decorative border that does not touch the corners. Also note the unique font.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Streetsigns - Nuremberg
metas.note: Nuremberg has blue signs with a unique font. The signs also have a grey frame with a small gap between it and the sign.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Streetsigns - Stuttgart
metas.note: Stuttgart uses black signs without a border.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Streetsigns - Wuppertal
metas.note: Wuppertal uses white signs with a unique font and a white painted frame with a small gap between it and the sign.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - T-Signback
metas.note: The T-Signback is exclusive to Hamburg.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Thicc T Pole
metas.note: These pole tops where the middle of the horizontal bar is thicker can be found in all of former East Germany.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Three Section Road Marker
metas.note: Bavaria uses these white rectangular road markers, which are divided by black lines into three sections. The left section provides the road you are currently on.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Trashcan - Berlin
metas.note: Berlin uses bright orange bins that have white text on them.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Trashcan - Bremen
metas.note: Bremen has green and grey bins, with orange speech bubbles.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Trashcan - Hamburg
metas.note: Hamburg uses bright red bins, with white speech bubbles.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Tree Tag
metas.note: Many trees in Brandenburg and Mecklenburg-Vorpommern have these tiny green markers on them. You can very rarely find them in Lower Saxony.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Triangle Poletop
metas.note: Triangle pole tops are common in Western Germany.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Triangle Post - Grey
metas.note: Baden-Württemberg uses grey triangle posts.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Triangle Post - North Rhine-Westphalia
metas.note: North Rhine-Westphalia uses white posts without white plates on the sides. You can also find posts which go all the way to the ground.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Triangle Post - Thuringia
metas.note: The plates on the Thuringia Triangle Posts are unique, as they have sections which are seperated by a black line.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Triangle Post - Unpainted
metas.note: Rhineland-Palatinate and Saxony use unpainted, rocky looking posts, with white plates stuck on each side.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Triangle Post - White
metas.note: Saarland, Thuringia, and Baden-Württemberg use white posts, with the same white plates attached. Note by MB: PlonkIt says they're smaller in BaWü. From what I saw, this is fake though.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Trident Poles
metas.note: These trident-like pole tops can be found in Bavaria, Saxony-Anhalt, and Baden-Württemberg.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Type A Guardrail
metas.note: I'd avise to learn where this cannot be found, which is Easter Germany, Hesse, Baden-Württemberg and Saarland.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Type B Guardrail
metas.note: I'd avise to learn where this cannot be found, which is Schleswig-Holstein, Rhineland-Palatinate, Bremen and Hamburg.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - White Bollard Plate
metas.note: These basic white plates on bollards can be found in all states except for Bavaria, Saarland and the City States.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - White Tree Paint
metas.note:
You can spot trees that are painted white close to the bottom of the trunk in the northeast.

NOTE: You will rarely find them outside the shaded region.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Wooden Bollard
metas.note: These round wooden bollards, which have a painted top, are found in Bavaria.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Yellow Bollard - No Plate
metas.note: Fully yellow posts are found in the state of Brandenburg.

metas.name: Germany - Infrastructure - Yellow Bollard - Plate
metas.note:
Yellow posts with a white plate on them are found in Saxony-Anhalt.

NOTE: Sometimes there is only 1 plate, which can make it hard to tell apart from a Brandenburg post.

metas.name: Germany - Landscape - Alps
metas.note: The German Alps is the most mountainous region in Germany, it is mostly concentrated on the Austrian Border.

metas.name: Germany - Landscape - Flat Landscape
metas.note: The North and especially Northwest of Germany is very flat.

metas.name: Germany - Landscape - Hilliness
metas.note: Central Germany is hilly.

metas.name: Germany - Landscape - Regensburg Plains & Ridge
metas.note: The flat plains southeast of Regensburg can be recognised by the slight ridge often visible to the northeast. The plains themselves are flat, and quite agricultural.

metas.name: Germany - Landscape - Sylt
metas.note:
The shrub and sand covered hills are unique to the island of Sylt. And like the rest of the North Frisian Islands, rock walls, brick houses, and thatched roofs are common.

NOTE: Some parts of Sylt look more generic, but still very flat.

metas.name: Germany - Language - Sorbian
metas.note: Sorbian, a Slavic language, is spoken near the Polish and Czech border. You can find it on a variety of signs in this region between Cottbus and Bautzen.

metas.name: Germany - Language - Town Suffix: -a
metas.note: The suffix -a can be found in the Southern Half of Germany.

metas.name: Germany - Language - Town Suffix: -ach
metas.note: The suffix -ach can be found in the Southern Half of Germany.

metas.name: Germany - Language - Town Suffix: -itz
metas.note: The suffix -itz can be found in Eastern Germany.

metas.name: Germany - Language - Town Suffix: -itzsch
metas.note: The suffix -itzsch can be found in Eastern Germany.

metas.name: Germany - Language - Town Suffix: -ow
metas.note: The suffix -ow can be found in Mecklenburg-Vorpommern, Berlin and Brandenburg.

metas.name: Germany - Language - Town Suffix: -schütz
metas.note: The suffix -schütz can be found in Eastern Germany.

metas.name: Germany - Language - Town Suffix: -weier
metas.note: The suffix -weiler can mainly be found in Rhineland-Palatinate, Saarland and Baden-Württemberg.

metas.name: Germany - Language - Town Suffix: -weiler
metas.note: The suffix -weiler can mainly be found in Rhineland-Palatinate, Saarland and Baden-Württemberg.

metas.name: Germany - Vegetation - Baltic Pines
metas.note: Baltic Pines or Pinus sylvestris are generally more concentrated in the northeast of Germany. They can be recognized by their orange-tinged trunk.

metas.name: Hawaii - Agriculture - Eucalyptus Plantation
metas.note: The north east coast of Hawai'i Island is characterized by planted eucalyptus overlooking the ocean.
metas.footer: Source: Geoguessr Guide to Hawaii by pianoman

metas.name: Hawaii - Car Meta - Stubby Antenna
metas.note: This antenna can be found anywhere, but is most common Hawaii Island, then Kauai, then Oahu.
metas.footer: Source: Geoguessr Guide to Hawaii by pianoman

metas.name: Hawaii - Coverage Meta - Gen 2 Hawaii
metas.note: Generation 2 coverage can only be found on the islands of Hawaiʻi, Maui and Oʻahu.

metas.name: Hawaii - Coverage Meta - Gen 4 Hawaii
metas.note:
Generation 4 coverage can only be found on the islands of Hawaiʻi, Maui and Oʻahu.

Note by MB: This applies only to Gen 4, not to Smallcam, which can be found everywhere

metas.name: Hawaii - Coverage Meta - Green Blur
metas.note: Within Hawaii, a distinct green blur can only be seen on the island of Oʻahu.

metas.name: Hawaii - Infrastructure - Elevated Railway
metas.note: The only elevated railway in Hawaii is on Oahu island and runs along the HI-99 for the most part, merges into the H-1 interstate and continues to the airport.

metas.name: Hawaii - Infrastructure - Road Sign - No Tab / Arrow
metas.note: No tab above sign, arrow on the actual sign, unique to Oahu.
metas.footer: Source: Geoguessr Guide to Hawaii by pianoman

metas.name: Hawaii - Infrastructure - Road Sign - No Tab / No Arrow / Number
metas.note: Basic streetsigns, but with a number below the abbreviation (Rd/St/Pl/...), unique to Kauai.
metas.footer: Source: Geoguessr Guide to Hawaii by pianoman

metas.name: Hawaii - Infrastructure - Road Sign - No Tab / No Number
metas.note: Basic streetsign, with only the road name, mostly found in Hawaii, rare on Kauai and extremely rare on Oahu and Maui.
metas.footer: Source: Geoguessr Guide to Hawaii by pianoman

metas.name: Hawaii - Infrastructure - Road Sign - Tab (Empty)
metas.note: Tab above sign, but nothing in it, found in Maui district (which includes Maui, Lana'i and Moloka'i)
metas.footer: Source: Geoguessr Guide to Hawaii by pianoman

metas.name: Hawaii - Infrastructure - Road Sign - Tab / Long Arrow
metas.note: Tab above sign, containing a long arrow, found in Maui district (which includes Maui, Lana'i and Moloka'i)
metas.footer: Source: Geoguessr Guide to Hawaii by pianoman

metas.name: Hawaii - Infrastructure - Road Sign - Tab / Short Arrow
metas.note: Tab above sign, containing a short or very short arrow, almost unique to Oahu.
metas.footer: Source: Geoguessr Guide to Hawaii by pianoman

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Central Maui
metas.note: The Island of Maui sits southeast of Molokaʻi. In the centre of the island, you will find somewhat flat grasslands. It has the very recognizable West Maui Mountains to the west, and Haleakala to the east.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & Geoguessr Guide to Hawaii by pianoman

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Coastal Big Island
metas.note:
The coastal areas of the island of Hawai’i are where most of the towns and built-up areas on the island are located. These areas are typically more lush and have more trees and fern plants than the interior.

Note by MB: There is a similar road, the Hana Highway on Maui, which is more narrow and has narrower shoulders than the typical road on Hawai'i.

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Coastal Lana'i
metas.note: Towards the coasts of the island of Lānaʻi, hills dotted with dry grass and shrubby vegetation are commonly seen. These areas are very rural with few buildings.

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Coastal Maui
metas.note: Coastal areas of Maui are noticeably lush and green. Banana plants, palm trees, and views of the mountains are all common.

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - East Molokai Volcano
metas.note:
Rather flat and wide volcano, making it's shape quite unique.

As the name suggests, it's found in the East of Moloka'i island.

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Flat Forest
metas.note: Rural roads going through forests within a flat landscape are commonly found south of the city of Hilo, on the island of Hawaiʻi.

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Haleakala Foothills
metas.note: The area near Kula is at the foot of Haleakala and often looks over the rest of the island.
metas.footer: Source: Geoguessr Guide to Hawaii by pianoman

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Hana Highway (North)
metas.note:
The Hana Highway runs along the coast of Maui and is narrow and lush in the North.

Note by MB: Note that unlike in the picture, Hana Highway also has center lines on some parts. That creates a possible toss-up with Hawai'i island. However, Hana Highway is more narrow and has very narrow shoulders, unlike most roads on Hawai'i.
metas.footer: Source: Geoguessr Guide to Hawaii by pianoman

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Hana Highway (South)
metas.note:
The Hana Highway runs along the coast of Maui and is narrow. In the south, the landscape is fairly open and you can often see the southern coast, as no trees are in the way.

Note by MB: Note that unlike in the picture, Hana Highway also has center lines on some parts. That creates a possible toss-up with Hawai'i island. However, Hana Highway is more narrow and has very narrow shoulders, unlike most roads on Hawai'i.

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Hawaiian Lattice
metas.note: The infamous 'Hawaiian lattice' can be recognized by the volcanic soil and rocks that are abundant in the region. Volcanic vegetation can also be seen lining the roads. Note that the angle of the roads is a big clue for the area, and that this lattice was built on the slope of Mauna Loa.

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Hilo
metas.note:
Hilo fits nicely into the coastal Hawai'i landscape (lush and somewhat built up). What makes it unique is the grid format of many of its roads. You can also sometimes see Mauna Kea in the west.

Note by MB: Other grids also exist on Hawaii island (notably Hawaiian Lattice, and the area south of Hilo), but they look very different. Each has their own meta describing them.
metas.footer: Source: Geoguessr Guide to Hawaii by pianoman

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Honolulu
metas.note: Honolulu, located on southern Oʻahu, is by far the largest city and urban area in Hawaii. If you are in a dense urban area and can see tall buildings, you will always be in or near Honolulu.

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Houses on Hills
metas.note: In most of Hawaii, houses are built on flat plains. If you see Houses on hillsides, you are most likely around the Ko'olau range in eastern Oahu, often in suburbs of Honolulu.

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Hualalai
metas.note: Hualalaei (a large mountain) rises to the east of Kona.
metas.footer: Source: Geoguessr Guide to Hawaii by pianoman

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Interior Big Island
metas.note:
The Island of Hawai’i (also referred to as The Big Island) is both the largest and farthest southeast island with Street View coverage in the state. The interior areas feature rolling, grassy plains and volcanic rocks. You can typically see one or more of the island’s volcanoes from the road.

What sets apart the mountains on this island is that they are more sloping and gradual than on other islands.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & Geoguessr Guide to Hawaii by pianoman

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Kauai
metas.note:
The Island of Kauai is the furthest west island in Hawaii with official Google coverage. This island has deep red soil and has large rugged hills with lush, jungle-like vegetation. This island also has exclusively Generation 3 and Smallcam coverage.

NOTE: Other islands such as Maui and Molokaʻi have similar soil colours, but the hillsides on them will typically have less dense vegetation.

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Kaunakakai
metas.note: The town of Kaunakakai is the largest settlement on the Island of Molokaʻi. It is the only area on the island with an ‘urban’ vibe.

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Lana'i
metas.note: The Island of Lānaʻi is a small, yet distinct island that lies just south of Moloka’i. A volcano is found just east of the centre of the island, adjacent to the town of Lānaʻi. In this area, tall Cook pines are abundant. In addition, some main roads near the centre of the island are lined with younger Cook pines.

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Maui West Coast
metas.note: West Maui can often see Molokai and/or Lanai to the west. The northern part of the west coast has the West Maui Mountains rising to the east.
metas.footer: Source: Geoguessr Guide to Hawaii by pianoman

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Mauna Loa Observatory Road
metas.note:
This road "looks like Mars", and has large volcanic rocks on its sides.

Note by MB: Unlike the road on Red Hill, this road does not have center lines.
metas.footer: Source: Geoguessr Guide to Hawaii by pianoman

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Moloka'i
metas.note:
The Island of Molokaʻi is just southeast of the Island of Oʻahu. This island features deep red soil, dry-looking vegetation, and a prominent volcano on the eastern end of the island. Molokaʻi is also very sparsely populated. This island only has Generation 3 and Smallcam coverage.

Note by MB: In the newest smallcam coverage, the island doesn't look as dry as in Gen 3 (due to different season).

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - O'ahu
metas.note: The Island of Oʻahu lies southeast of Kauai. It is known for being home to the Honolulu urban area. It also is home to steep, lush hills, which can be commonly seen from all around the island, especially in Honolulu’s suburbs. Generation 4 coverage is common on Oʻahu.

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Red Hill
metas.note:
The Red Hill can easily be recognised by this unique barren, rocky landscape. Due to the high altitude, clouds are usually visible below you.

Note by MB: In newer smallcam coverage the hill looks not that red, but the coverage is still recognizable. Also, unlike the Mauna Lea observatory road on Hawai'i, this road has yellow center lines.

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Seaview Road
metas.note: The road around and east of Seaview (Hawai'i island) is very distinct, as it combines the volcanic rock landscape with water immediately to the South.

metas.name: Hawaii - Landscape - Volcanic Rock
metas.note: Hawaii island has the only currently active volcano and is the most recently formed island, so lots of volcanic rock is common.
metas.footer: Source: Geoguessr Guide to Hawaii by pianoman

metas.name: Hawaii - Misc - North-West Road Angle
metas.note: A weirdly good meta for the Kona area (western Hawai'i) is roads that are angled SE-NW.
metas.footer: Source: Geoguessr Guide to Hawaii by pianoman

metas.name: Hawaii - Misc - Oahu Area Codes
metas.note:
Signs on Oahu (and sometimes other places) often have a 2-digit number followed by a dash. These correspond to different tax zones.

They are not used in urban Honolulu. They start with 41 at the east coast, and increase counter-clockwise along the coast.
metas.footer: Source: Geoguessr Guide to Hawaii by pianoman

metas.name: Iceland - Car Meta - Red Truck
metas.note:
Iceland can be split in half depending on the colour of the pickup truck, with red being found in the southwest, and white being found in the northeast.

The Red Truck is found between Sudurland and Vesturland

metas.name: Iceland - Car Meta - White Truck
metas.note: Iceland can be split in half depending on the colour of the pickup truck, with red being found in the southwest, and white being found in the northeast.

metas.name: Iceland - Infrastructure - Divided Highway
metas.note: The 41 and 43 southwest of Reykjavík, as well as the 1 between Grundarhverfi and Selfoss are divided.

metas.name: Iceland - Infrastructure - Multi Lane Highway
metas.note: Both sides of the Hvalfjördur Tunnel have multiple lanes for one driving direction.

metas.name: Iceland - Landscape - Akureyri
metas.note: Akureyri is the second-biggest city in Iceland and is located in a North-South oriented valley, along the western edge of the bay. The city features mountains ranges to the east and west, making it recognisable.

metas.name: Iceland - Landscape - Akureyri Mountains
metas.note: The mountains west of Akureyri contain many valleys, sandwiched between tall, often slightly snowcapped peaks. Most of these valleys generally face north to northeast.

metas.name: Iceland - Landscape - Eiðar Valley
metas.note: The wide valley around Eiðar is slightly hilly and agricultural, with tall, snowy peaks visible in the distance on either side, to the east and northwest, respectively.

metas.name: Iceland - Landscape - Flat-Topped Mountains
metas.note: The Westfjords region features numerous narrow fjords, surrounded by moderately tall, and mostly flat-topped mountains.

metas.name: Iceland - Landscape - Fog
metas.note: Very foggy coverage can be found around the town of Bakkagerði, in northeastern Iceland. The fog can also be seen from a distance.

metas.name: Iceland - Landscape - Glaciers
metas.note: The southern coast of Iceland features some impressive glaciers visible from the ring road, spilling into the sea from the Vatnajökull ice cap.

metas.name: Iceland - Landscape - Hallormsstaður Valley
metas.note: The valley around Hallormsstaður has a distinct northeast/southwest angle with low-lying mountains on either side, a wide river flowing through it, and an unusual amount of trees for Iceland. Some of the sideroads are in the forests.

metas.name: Iceland - Landscape - Heimaey
metas.note: The Island of Heimaey can easily be recognised by seeing these ragged rocky cliffs overlooking the town of Vestmannaeyjabær. Similar cliffs can be seen on the islands off the coast.

metas.name: Iceland - Landscape - Inland Iceland
metas.note: Barren landscapes consisting mostly of dark volcanic gravel, with little to no vegetation or signs of life, are typical of the inland regions of Iceland. Most such covered roads are located in the east.

metas.name: Iceland - Landscape - Large Jagged Mountains
metas.note: The far east of the country is also home to several fjords. What distinguishes them from the Westfjords are the generally larger and more jagged mountains.

metas.name: Iceland - Landscape - Reykjavík
metas.note:
Reykjavík is the capital and by far the largest city in Iceland. The city is mostly flat with slight hills, and is located on the south side of a bay. It is most recognizable as it is significantly larger than other Icelandic cities, with a large urban area and “bigger city” feel.

NOTE: The city of Akureyri can feel urban in some places. You can distinguish it from Reykjavik as it has mountains to the east and west.

metas.name: Iceland - Landscape - Selfoss Mountain
metas.note: You can recognise the area near the town of Selfoss from its distinct flat-ridge mountain. Due to the otherwise flat landscape, this mountain can be seen from a wide area.

metas.name: Iceland - Landscape - Southwest Farmland
metas.note:
The Southwest agricultural area in Iceland can be identified by its relatively flat farmland landscape scattered with numerous farmsteads, fields, meadows and grasslands.

NOTE: Although there are other smaller agricultural areas in Iceland, mountains in this area tend to be quite distant, making it unique.

metas.name: India - Agriculture - Assam - Corn
metas.note: Within Assam, you can find corn between Guwahati and Nagaon, south of the river.

metas.name: India - Agriculture - Assam - Sugarcane
metas.note: Within Assam, sugarcane is mainly found around Lanka

metas.name: India - Agriculture - Bihar - Tea
metas.note: Within Bihar, tea plantations can be found in the far Northeast.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Agriculture - Canola
metas.note: Canola is mostly found in and around Rajasthan.

metas.name: India - Agriculture - Cotton
metas.note: Cotton is commonly found in the western parts of India, particularly in Gujarat and Maharashtra.

metas.name: India - Agriculture - Grape
metas.note: Maharashtra is by far the state with the highest grape production in India.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Agriculture - Madhya Pradesh - Sugarcane
metas.note: Within Madhya Pradesh, sugar cane can commonly be found southwest and northeast of the Satpura National Park.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Agriculture - Maharashtra - Cotton
metas.note:
Cotton (within) is mostly found around Nanded, more generally in the middle/eastern part of Maharashtra.

Note by MB: Very unreliable in my experience
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Agriculture - Maharashtra - Sugarcane
metas.note: Sugarcane in Maharashtra is mostly central from what I saw.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Agriculture - Oil Palm
metas.note: Oil palm plantations are almost exclusive to Andhra Pradesh and are mostly located around Eluru.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Agriculture - Pineapple
metas.note: Pineapple is very uncommon in India, but if you see it, it's in Bihar in the corridor between Nepal and Bangladesh.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Agriculture - Sugarcane
metas.note: Sugarcane is most commonly found in the north in and around Uttar Pradesh, and in the southwest.

metas.name: India - Agriculture - Sugarcane - Tamil Nadu
metas.note:
Sugar cane can be found in several areas, the two main ones being near Erode and Thiruvanamalai.

It is also findable in smaller areas between those two big areas, but it is still mainly a northern Tamil Nadu thing.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Agriculture - Tea - Assam
metas.note: Within Assam, Tea is mostly planted in the eastern and in the southern regions. There are also some patches in Western Assam.
metas.footer: Source: Northeast India by Cassa, Alok and the GeoGuessr India community

metas.name: India - Agriculture - Tea - Tamil Nadu
metas.note: Tea plantations in India are mostly located in the northeast and in Kerala, but it spills in one particular area in Tamil Nadu northwest of Coimbatore
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Agriculture - Tea - Tripura
metas.note: Within Tripura, Tea is found along the Bangladeshi border, and along the Assamese border.
metas.footer: Source: Northeast India by Cassa, Alok and the GeoGuessr India community

metas.name: India - Agriculture - Tea - West Bengal
metas.note: Within West Bengal, tea plantations are found near the northern border to Bhutan.
metas.footer: Source: Northeast India by Cassa, Alok and the GeoGuessr India community

metas.name: India - Agriculture - Tea Plantation
metas.note:
Tea plantations can be found in the northeast and the far south.

NOTE: If you find tea plantations in a flat area, you are likely in Assam or northeastern West Bengal, near the Assam border.

metas.name: India - Agriculture - Telangana - Cotton
metas.note:
Cotton fields in Telangana are logically next to the big area that produces the most of it in Maharashtra, so it is gonna be found mostly north-west of the state. You can click in Nizamabad for a good score.

Note by MB: In my experience, it's more common North of Nizamabad.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Andhra Pradesh - Thatched Roofs
metas.note:
Within Andhra Pradesh, thatched roofs can commonly be found in three places.

  • Mainly south east of Guntur
  • Secondarily south of Nellore, where a rare red car can be found.
  • Sparsely around Srikakulam
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Assam - Thatched Roofs
metas.note: Within Assam, you can find thatched roofs all the way north east in the state.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Assam - Woven Walls
metas.note: In Assam, you can find houses with woven walls along the border to Arunachal Pradesh, north of Tinsukia.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Bihar - Tin Hip Roof
metas.note: If you see these hip roofs made out of tin - which are usually found in West Bengal - in Bihar, you're in the Northeastern Quarter of Bihar.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Bihar - Wide W Tiles
metas.note:
Within Bihar, you can find regular Wide W Tiles around Katihar.

Reminder: This type of tile is like a larger kind of W tile. Another way to tell it apart is the small pike in the middle of the tile.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Blue Walls & Tiles
metas.note: Houses with tiled roofs and blue painted walls are very common in Jharkhand and Chhattisgarh, a little less in Madhya Pradesh
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Brick Kiln
metas.note: In poorer parts of the Ganges Valley it is common for villages to construct their own large chimneys to fire clay into bricks. These can be seen from far away and are a good clue for the Ganges Valley specifically, especially UP and Bihar. Note that they are also fairly common in the poorer eastern parts of Tamil Nadu.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Clay House
metas.note: Houses made out of clay are most common in Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand. There's some spill in far southwestern Bihar.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Clay House
metas.note: Clay houses exist a lot in Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand, and some spill can be seen in southwestern Bihar.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Clay Huts
metas.note: White painted clay huts are found in northwestern Bihar, northwest of Muzaffapur.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt, India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Colorful Walls
metas.note: Houses with colorful, particularly blue painted walls, can be found in the areas around Eastern Madhya, Chhattisgarh and Jharkhand.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Corrugated Hip Roof
metas.note: Large hip roofs made of corrugated sheet metal are found in West Bengal and adjacent areas in Bihar and Odisha.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Dravidian Temple
metas.note:
- Shorter and "pyramidal" towers (Vimana) - most easily recognizable

  • Monumental and ornate gate (Gopuram)
  • Door Guardian Statues (Dvarapala)

Found in the South of India.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Dumka House
metas.note: Houses between Dumka and Pakur have long tiled roofs and walls are painted in two colors (green/blue with an orange/brown color at the bottom
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Elevated Bengali Roof
metas.note:
Found mostly in the main, southern part of West Bengal, but more in the west. Sometimes also found in Bihar at the border to eastern Nepal.

Note by MB: This meta is not sufficiently researched, but it's still good to know
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Flat Gooner (actually Guna) Tiles
metas.note: Flat Guna tiles is just a tiled roof full of staple-shaped tiles. It can be found around Prayagraj, south east of the state.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Flat Tiles
metas.note: Flat tiles seem to be the worst type of tile by their appearance. They are mainly found in Madhya Pradesh and southern Uttar pradesh.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Gooner (actually Guna) Tiles
metas.note:
It has a “U” shape but there is a flatter shaped tile connecting tiles to each other.

It’s very common in southeastern Uttar Pradesh, western Bihar and rarely in northeastern Madhya Pradesh and Jharkhand.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Green House
metas.note: Houses in Odisha are often painted green.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Hay Hut
metas.note: These huts that are made entirely out of hay, and have thatched roofs are found in Southwestern Bihar, mainly between Patna and Gaya.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Jammu Architecture
metas.note:
Jammu looks like a fairly developed state compared to most places in India. The architecture looks richer and overall way nicer. Punjab has a similar architecture.

50/50 Tip ! It can be hard to differentiate Punjab and Jammu in urban rounds due to the similarity of their architecture. If you see rich looking houses, look at the car to know whether you are in Punjab or in Jammu. If you don’t see one of the two Jammu cars (boxy with top right thread or central strap, see image 3&4), click Punjab.

Note by MB: This 50/50 tip is not 100% reliable, so look at other clues (like Punjabi language) too.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Jharkhand - Wide W Tiles
metas.note: In the eastern parts of Jharkhand, you can find some West Bengal wide W tiles spill
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Madhya Pradesh - Flat Tiles
metas.note: Flat tiles can be spotted in random places in Madhya Pradesh, but mainly around Guna, Chhatarpur and Sagar in the center of the state.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Madhya Pradesh - Slate Roofs
metas.note: Slate roofs in Madhya Pradesh can be found west of Sagar
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Madhya Pradesh - U Tiles
metas.note: U tiles are more common in the eastern half of Madhya Pradesh.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Madhya Pradesh - W Tiles
metas.note: W tiles are quite rare in Madhya Pradesh but can still be seen west of Jabalpur and south of Guna
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Nalukettu
metas.note: Nallukettu architecture has distinct roofs, which are often very high and red. This style is often found around Kerala Backwaters.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Odisha - Thatched Roofs
metas.note:
Thatched roofs can be found pretty much all over the eastern coast of India. In the state of Odisha, they can mostly be seen between Balasore and Puri, but also more inland and in the southwest of the state.

If you see only thatched, the coast is more likely.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Odisha - U-Tiles
metas.note: U tiles are commonly found on the northwest of the state, on the borders with Jharkhand and Chhattsgarh.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Odisha - U-Tiles & Thatched Roofs
metas.note: When mixed with thatched roofs, U Tiles are most commonly found around Umerkote.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Odisha - W-Tiles
metas.note:
W tiled roofs can be found in two areas in Odisha:

  • corridor north of Bhubaneswar
  • Southwestern Odisha, southwest of Bhawanipatna
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Odisha - W-Tiles & Thatched Roofs
metas.note:
W tiled roofs combined with Thatched Roofs can be found in two areas in Odisha:

  • corridor north of Bhubaneswar
  • Southwestern Odisha, southwest of Bhawanipatna

Note by MB: This is also true if you just see W-Tiles, without Thatched Roofs.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Odisha - W-Tiles & U-Tiles
metas.note: When mixed with W-Tiles, U-Tiles are most commonly found around Umerkote.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Orange/Black Wide W Tiles
metas.note:
If you see orange/black wide W tiles, you're probably around Madhubani (BR).

Reminder: This type of tile is like a larger kind of W tile. Another way to tell it apart is the small pike in the middle of the tile.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Plastered Woven Wall
metas.note: Woven walls, plastered with clay are found on the western half of the Bihar-Nepal border.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Red Brick
metas.note: While Red Brick can be found anywhere in India, there is a notable concentration in the Ganges River Valley, especially towards the West.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Shimla Vibes
metas.note:
Shimla is definitely the place in the Himalayas with the biggest amount of bright green and bright red roofs (and architecture in general).

Note by MB: It also spams Himalayan Cedars.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Sikhism
metas.note: Gurdwaras, which can typically be recognised by their white domes and ornate walls, are most common in Punjab. You can also sometimes recognise them by the Sikh Khanda symbol, which represents the religion.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Sikkim Roof
metas.note: Roofs in Sikkim often have this short "curtain" hanging down on the side of the roof.
metas.footer: Source: Northeast India by Cassa, Alok and the GeoGuessr India community

metas.name: India - Architecture - Slate Roof - Karnataka/Telangana
metas.note:
Slate roofs can be found in a very specific area between Kalaburagi and Hyderabad in Telangana.

Note by MB: This is the same area where they use the thin grey stones (see thin grey stones meta), and thus you can often see them in combination
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Square Panel Houses
metas.note: Houses made of square panels separated by thin beams are found in Northeast India, mainly in Sikkim, Arunachal Pradesh, Manipur.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Stick Huts
metas.note: Wooden huts with sticks around can be found in the western half of Bihar, at a latitude between Patna and Muzaffarpur..
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt, India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Tamil Nadu Colors
metas.note: Houses with very "strong colors", such as dark yellow, pink, purple, are often found in Tamil Nadu, and sometimes in Kerala and Andhra Pradesh
metas.footer: Source: India GeoGuessr Guide - 2024 Edition by duskden2

metas.name: India - Architecture - Tamil Nadu House
metas.note:
In Tamil Nadu, you will often come across quite good looking houses, the most recognizable are the ones with W tiled roofs and blueish paint. The combination of the color and the tiles should be 95% Tamil Nadu, the remaining 5% being spill in bordering states.

W tiled roofs are pretty much everywhere but somewhat less common in the northeast and on the eastern coast, where U tiles can be found more commonly.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Thatched Hay Roofs
metas.note: Houses or huts with thatched roofs are mainly found along the east coast and northern plains. Large hay mounds are also generally more common in this region. Thatched roofs from Uttar Pradesh to Odisha tend to be made of fine pieces of hay.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Thatched Palm Roofs
metas.note: Houses or huts with thatched roofs are mainly found along the east coast and northern plains. Large hay mounds are also generally more common in this region. Thatched roofs from Odisha to Tamil Nadu tend to be made of dried palm fans.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Thatched Roofs - Tamil Nadu
metas.note: In Tamil Nadu, thatched roofs are more common south east of Thanjavur.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Thin Grey Stones
metas.note: The area on the border of Telangana and Karnataka often have houses with roofs made out of distinctly thin grey bricks. These grey bricks and similar coloured rocks are sometimes also seen in walls and scattered on the ground in stockyards.

metas.name: India - Architecture - Triangle Metal Roofs
metas.note: Metal roofs, with a small triangle near the top, are common in Northeast India.

metas.name: India - Architecture - U-Tiles
metas.note:
These rounded tiles are found mostly in

  • Chhattisgarh
  • Jharkhand
  • Bihar
  • Eastern Madhya

You can also find them in

  • Eastern Gujarat
  • Eastern Tamil Nadu
  • North-Western Telangana
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - U-Tiles - Tamil Nadu
metas.note:
U tiled roofs are quite rare in Tamil Nadu, but if you come across such roofs, it should be in the northeast.

It is possible to find some further down near Thanjavur, but it will more likely come with the combination of thatched roofs.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - W-Tiles
metas.note: W-Tiles are mostly found on the western coast and in Tamil Nadu, but it also goes further inland in western Madhya Pradesh and in Telangana.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - W-Tiles - Karnataka
metas.note: If you come across a W tiled roof in Karnataka, you can basically go in the western/southwestern part
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - W-Tiles - Telangana
metas.note:
The only type of tile in Telangana is the W tile type.

As you can see, it doesn’t go in the south of the state.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Wealthy & Modern Homes
metas.note: Goa and Kerala are two of the most developed states in India and often have very wealthy and modern homes.

metas.name: India - Architecture - West Bengal - Dumka House
metas.note: In West Bengal, houses with walls painted in two colors (green/blue with an orange/brown color at the bottom, are usually found near the Jharkhand border.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Architecture - Wide W-Tiles
metas.note:
This type of tile is like a larger kind of W tile. Another way to tell it apart is the small pike in the middle of the tile.

It is very common in West Bengal, eastern Jharkhand and eastern Bihar, but doesn’t go further north than Purnia, Bihar.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Camera Meta - High Quality Shitcam
metas.note: The coverage on road NH326 (labelled 326) west of Brahmapur in Odisha has a thin grey antenna. The images are generally very high-quality for shitcam, with an especially high quality near the Harabhangi Reservoir.

metas.name: India - Car - Kuno National Park Car
metas.note: This car has a back curving bar, but is mostly blurred. It can be found east of Kuno National Park
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Andaman Car
metas.note: This is the most common, though not only car on Andaman.

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Arunachal Pradesh - Back Antenna
metas.note: Within Arunachal Pradesh, a back antenna can be found around Chowkam and East of Namsai.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Arunachal Pradesh - White Car with Mirrors
metas.note: Within Arunachal Pradesh, a white car with mirrors can be found on the road west of Itanagar.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Assam - Back Antenna
metas.note: If you see a back antenna in Assam, you're in the far east of the state.

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Black Car
metas.note: This is not something you will come across very often, but if you have a black car and don’t really know where to go/want to confirm your guess, black car is more common in Telangana/Andhra Pradesh, especially in Northern Telangana and Coastal AP.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Black Goa Car
metas.note: This black car, uniquely characterized through the black bars on each the side, is only found in Goa.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Boxy Car
metas.note: Large visible, square shaped cars can be found in all states northwest of Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh, except for Madhya Pradesh. It can also be found in and around Hyderabad, Bengaluru and Chennai.

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Boxy Car - 5 Indents
metas.note: A boxy car with 5 indents can be found near the river mouth of the Subarnarekha river near the Odisha/WB border.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Boxy Car - 6 Indents
metas.note: A boxy car with 6 indents is found near Malkangiri, Odisha.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Boxy Car - Karnataka
metas.note: Boxy car in Karnataka is only found in and around Bengaluru.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Boxy Car - Odisha
metas.note: A boxy car with an extra step at the front is found in Odisha.

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Flower Car
metas.note: A car with flowers on the front can be found around Keonjhar, on the 49 and the 20.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Goa/Daman Car
metas.note: This car (note the antenna!) can be found in Goa, and in the Union Territory of Daman.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Haryal Car
metas.note: This car is unique to Haryal, PB. It looks similar to the boxy car, but with a rounded front.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Himachal Pradesh - Boxy Car
metas.note: Shimla is the only city in Himachal Pradesh to have a boxy car, which is this car with the top right corner visible with a thread (sometimes not visible).
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Jammu/Kashmir Car
metas.note:
White car, box car with bars and the central strap leaning right.

It can be found mainly in Jammu/Kashmir but sometimes in Sultanpur, UP.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Ladakh Car
metas.note: All roads in Ladakh have this white car with visible front.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Lakshadweep - Adidas Car
metas.note:
The "Adidas Car" is characterized by the black stripes on the white car front. Sometimes it has a visible side mirror. It also often has a visible bar at the back.

It is exclusive to the island of Amini

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Lakshadweep - Big Blur
metas.note: A big circular blur (either full blurred or transparently blurred) is very common in Retrocam. On Lakshadweep, however, it is only found on Andrott and Kalpeni (both also have a car that's unique for these islands respectively).
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Lakshadweep - Blurred Black Front
metas.note:
This car with the subtle black blur at the front is found in Kalpeni. The blur can be very subtle sometimes, and is confusable with the blurred white edges on Agatti.

Sometimes the same car has a slightly different blur, where the edges are exposed.

Kalpeni can also have a big circular blur, so don't rule out Kalpeni if you don't see this car.

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Lakshadweep - Blurred White Edges
metas.note: This car is mostly blurred and has subtle white edges at the front. It's found on the island of Agatti. Sometimes the edges are so subtle that you can overlook them and confuse it with the Kalpeni car (which has a subtle black blur)

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Lakshadweep - Exposed Black
metas.note: This car with an exposed black front is unique to Kiltan. Note that the front is always exposed on Kiltan, if it's blurred (even partly), it's not the Kiltan car.

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Lakshadweep - Red Car
metas.note:
The red front blur can be found on Andrott. Sometimes, the same car has a bit different blur, where there's some exposed red visible.

Note that Andrott can also have the big circular blur where you see no car.

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Lakshadweep - White Car with Mirror
metas.note: This car is the most likely to encounter if you get Lakshadweep. It has a white front and always a bit of mirror visible on the left. Sometimes a part of the mirror is blurred, but you can always see at least a bit of it exposed. This car is so common because it's on the main island of Lakshadweep, Kavaratti.

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Lakshadweep - White Exposed Front
metas.note: This car with an exposed white front is found of Kadmat. This car can be confused with others: It's not the Kadmat car if it has a visible side mirror. It's also not the Kadmat car if the front is blurred.

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Mechuka Car
metas.note: Mechuka features a unique car in Arunachal. It can be found in the valley and on the road leading to it from Along on the NH13.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Mizoram - Double Mirror Car
metas.note: In Mizoram, a grey car with double mirrors appears in the southernmost coverage, near the NH502.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Mizoram - Long Antenna
metas.note:
If you see a long antenna, combined with a black car front in Mizoram, you're on the NH6 north of Serkhan.

Keep in mind this car is not unique to Mizoram.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Mizoram - Stubby Antenna
metas.note: A car with a black front and a stubby antenna within Mizoram can be found on the roads west of Aizawi.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Car Meta - NH179B Car
metas.note: This car has an antenna with some kind of a spring. It basically goes from Salem to Chennai.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Open Trunk
metas.note: In the eastern parts of Ajmer, RJ, you can sometimes see an open trunk in Smallcam. It can be found north of Shrinagar/west of Circular Rd.
metas.footer: Discovered by TheRealWoly, shared on GeoGuessr India Discord, extent researched by Major Bajor.

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Orange Flag Car
metas.note: A car with an orange flag can be found in the Jharkhand north-east panhandle.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Punjab - Black Boxy Car
metas.note: Within Punjab, the black boxy car can be found on the Pakistani border between Firozpur and Amritsar.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Punjab - Dasuya Forest Car
metas.note: Within Punjab, this car is is unique to Dasuya Forest. Beware that this car is not unique to Punjab though.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh
