metas.name: India - Car Meta - Punjab - Red Boxy Car
metas.note: Within Punjab, the red boxy car can be found in Ludhiana, Chandigarh, and a bit north between them. The coverage forms a reverse 'v'.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Racecar
metas.note: This cool car with a spoiler at the back can be found in Max-North Andaman, near Daglipur.

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Rewa Car
metas.note: This car has a back curving bar at the front and white bars on the side. It's found mostly around Rewa, but also around Raipura.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Roing Car
metas.note: Within Arunachal Pradesh, both this black and this red car are exclusively found in Roing. The black car appears mainly on the NH313 and east. The red car appears mainly west of the main road.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh; self-researched

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Satpura National Park Car
metas.note: This car has a back-curving bar and a singular black bar. It's found mainly east of Satpura National Park, and sometimes around Raipura.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Tezu-Lohitpur Road
metas.note: If you see this white, boxy-looking car in Arunachal Pradesh, you're on the road between Tezu and Lohitpur.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Western Meghalaya Antenna
metas.note: In the very far western part of the Meghalaya, on the roads north of Purakhasia, you can find a particular car with an antenna on the top left. It can be quite hard to see so be aware it exists so you know what to look for
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Car Meta - White Goa Car with bar
metas.note: This white car, uniquely characterized through the bar on the side, which is black and grey, is only found in Goa.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Car Meta - Yellow Car
metas.note:
While the car is blurred most of the time, Sikkim features a noticeable car that gives the western part of Sikkim, starting at Rangpo.

It can have an antenna, be blurred, almost invisible, but as long as you see a yellow car, you know it’s here.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Coverage Meta - Andaman Vibes
metas.note:
Andaman Islands are remote Islands that have their own distinct vegetation. It is covered in areca palm forests and the roads are often very thin.

Andaman has been covered using a camera with maxed out saturation somehow. The result is these very bright/white colors.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Coverage Meta - Kerala Construction Meta
metas.note:
In 2025, a large part of the NH-66 in Kerala is under construction, making it very recognizable.

If you see a long, straight highway with construction in Smallcam, you're likely to be on the NH-66.

metas.name: India - Coverage Meta - Tripura Cam
metas.note: Many locations in Tripura have a pretty low brightness, despite the sun being out and not setting.
metas.footer: Source: Northeast India by Cassa, Alok and the GeoGuessr India community

metas.name: India - Coverage Meta - Yawal Double Smudge
metas.note: This double smudge can be found in the central-northern parts of the Yawal Wildlife Sanctuary in Madhya Pradesh.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - ∀-Poletop
metas.note:
Poles in Madhya Pradesh often have a metal bar shaped like an upside down A (∀) slightly below the top of the pole.

94% Madhya Pradesh 2% Jharkhand 1% each: Chhattisgarh, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - <-Poletop
metas.note: Poles with two diagonal bars forming a ‘<’ shape are common in Meghalaya (75%) and Arunachal Pradesh (20%) and occasionally found in Assam (2%).
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - 1 1/2 Trapezoids
metas.note: This pole configuraiton is mainly found in Tripura and Arunachal Pradesh.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - ACC Cement
metas.note: Found everywhere except for North-East.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Ambuja Cement
metas.note: Commonly found everywhere, except for North East. Within North-East, it is sometimes found in Assam.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Andaman Black Sticker
metas.note:
These black paint can be circular or square, features 2 letters, an arrow beneath, and some numbers beneath that and can be on metal/concrete poles.

They're found mostly near the capital (Port Blair/Sri Vijaya Puram) (95%) and rarely near Diglipur (5%)
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Andaman Horizontal Bar Poletop
metas.note: Pole tops in Andaman mostly consist of horizontal bars perpendicular to the pole. They are not 100% unique to Andaman, but are very common there.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Antioquia Pole
metas.note: This black-yellow-black pole painting (which is famous for appearing in Antioquia in Colo), can also be found in Eastern Bihar along the Ganges.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Arunachal Pradesh - Black & White Bollard
metas.note:
These bollards are rarer and not unique to Arunachal Pradesh, but if you think you are here, these are the areas these bollards are most commonly found

  • In Max West Arunachal Pradesh
  • North of Deed
  • North of Aalo
  • on the 319 in the East
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Arunachal Pradesh - Divided Road
metas.note: The only divided road in Arunachal Pradesh is the NH415 south of Itanagar
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Arunachal Pradesh - Pole Band
metas.note: A section of the NH13 west of Roing has poles marked with white numbers on blue, red or black paint.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Assam / West Bengal vans
metas.note: These vans (can be white, red, or orange) with specifically yellow plates, in NE India are found only within West Bengal and Assam. Doesn’t count with a white plate.
metas.footer: Source: Northeast India by Cassa, Alok and the GeoGuessr India community

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Assam Pavement
metas.note: Many roads in Assam are paved with these tiles. What makes it stand out is that it is also found on very rural roads.
metas.footer: Source: Northeast India by Cassa, Alok and the GeoGuessr India community

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Assam Trident Poles
metas.note: Trident poletops with the tip of the middle bar bent at a 90° angle can be found in Assam (98%).
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Bangur Cement
metas.note:
Bangur Cement is found in large parts of India.

It is only sometimes found in Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana and Delhi (where Bangur Power Cement) is more prevalent.

It is never found in

  • Kerala + Tamil Nadu
  • North East India
  • Gujarat
  • Anything North of Himachal Pradesh
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Bangur Power Cement
metas.note:
Found in Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana and Delhi, and sometimes also in Uttar Pradesh or Madhya Pradesh.

Don't confuse this with Bangur Cement, which has a different distribution.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Bar underneath Generic Pole
metas.note:
Metal crossbar with no insulators

Most common in Maharahstra (50%)

Also occasionally found in other northern states.

Within the Northeast, it's exclusive to Tripura.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Big Ring Pole
metas.note:
Big rectangular metal ring around the pole.

Most common in Uttarakhand + Himachal Pradesh and Mizoram + Tripura.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Bihar Pole + Mountains
metas.note: In Uttarakhand, the Bihar pole (yellow and black stripes) can be found on the NH109 North and a small road South of Dwarahat. Since Uttarakhand is mountainous, you shouldn't mistake it for Bihar.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Bihar stripes
metas.note: Pole paint consisting of exactly four thicker black and yellow stripes can be found in Bihar.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Bihar/Jharkhand Guy
metas.note:
In Bihar and Jharkhand you will see many ads with this man with a turban and a beard. He's usually accompanied by a hexagonal company logo and a yellow background.

Note by MB: This sounds ridiculous but he seems to be so popular that there are copycats of him with the same Turban/beard style. So if you see a different company logo, don't trust this.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Black Tuk-Tuks
metas.note: Black Tuk-Tuks are most common in Maharashtra (maybe fake meta)

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Blue & White Bridge
metas.note: The bridges in West Bengal frequently feature blue and white concrete blocks. It is also rarely found in Bihar around the city of Gaya.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Blue Pole Stickers
metas.note: These blue stickers on metal poles can be found on the NH109 near Lohali (UK)
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Buddhism
metas.note:
Buddhist prayer flags and other Buddhist signals are mostly found in the Himalayas. Sometimes you can also find them in the Northeast, around Bangladesh, especially in Western Meghalaya, Western Mizoram and Southern Tripura. Rarely you can find it in central-eastern Maharashtra around Nagpur.

Note by MB: The colors in the map don't exactly match the text. The text is right though (for Geoguessr), not the map.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Flag Metas by Atomo MC

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Chandigarh - Lampe Circles
metas.note:
The City of Chandigarh is a planned industrial city. As a result, the city features a lot of unique infrastructure, such as round yellow markings on street lights.

NOTE: The nearby cities of Sahibzada Ajit Singh Nagar and Panchkula are also planned industrial cities, which feature somewhat similar signs.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Chandigarh - Large Blue Signs
metas.note:
The City of Chandigarh is a planned industrial city. As a result, the city features a lot of unique infrastructure, such as blue signs mentioning sectors and industrial areas.

NOTE: The nearby cities of Sahibzada Ajit Singh Nagar and Panchkula are also planned industrial cities, which feature somewhat similar signs.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Chandigarh - Streetsign
metas.note:
The City of Chandigarh is a planned industrial city. As a result, the city features a lot of unique infrastructure, such as street signs which will typically feature several numbers rather than street names.

NOTE: The nearby cities of Sahibzada Ajit Singh Nagar and Panchkula are also planned industrial cities, which feature somewhat similar signs.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Chandigarh Poletop
metas.note:
Trident poletop, V-shaped bars underneath and Punjab Poletop.

Very hyperspecific for some roads in Chandigarh.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Chennai Wall
metas.note: This wall pattern can be found in and around Chennai (but it is rare).
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Chettinad Cement
metas.note: Recognizable by the C-Logo Found in South India, and sometimes in Goa and Maharashtra.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Combination of Even and Uneven Poletop
metas.note: In the northeast you may find poles with a combination of an even and uneven poletop.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Complicated Dark Metal Pole
metas.note:
Overly complicated, usually dark metal.

90% in West Bengal.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Concrete Blocks
metas.note: Concrete blocks, similar to those you see in Bhutan, are commonly found in (but not limited to) North-East India
metas.footer: Source: India GeoGuessr Guide - 2024 Edition by duskden2

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Concrete Holey Poles
metas.note:
Concrete holey poles are unique to Gujarat and the Union territory of Daman and Diu, and Dadra and Nagar Haveli. Gujarat uses a variety of poletops, some of which can be used to identify other states. Beware that holey poles generally take precedence over poletop metas.

NOTE: They are rarely found in other states:

  • Maharashtra (2%)
  • Madhya Pradesh (1%)
  • Chhattisgarh (1%)
  • Odisha (0.5%)
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Concrete Road / Yellow Lines
metas.note: From the city of Sukma to the border with Andra Pradesh, the NH30 has yellow road lines and is made of concrete. (Kinda similar to the famous Ruta 9 in Chile)
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Concreto Cement
metas.note: Found in East India (i.e. Bihar, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Odisha)
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Dark Rock Walls
metas.note: Dark Rock Walls are commonly found around Udaipur, RJ.
metas.footer: Source: India GeoGuessr Guide - 2024 Edition by duskden2

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Dehradun Sticker
metas.note: These round white stickers can be found all over Dehradun (UK)
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Delhi Bus
metas.note: Orange and bright green buses are typically found in Delhi.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Delhi stripes
metas.note:
Pole paint consisting of five or more thin black and yellow stripes can be found in Delhi.

#1 clue for rural Delhi (98%)

Has to be the exact order and color.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Delhi Yellow Sticker
metas.note: Besides Kerala and Uttarakhand, Delhi can also rarely have yellow stickers. All of these regions look very different.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Double Bull Cement
metas.note: Found in Central and East India, in Haryana and Delhi, and sometimes in Gujarat.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Duraguard Cement
metas.note:
Found in Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh and Chattisgarh, sometimes in Odisha.

Don't confuse with Duraton Cement.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Duraton Cement
metas.note:
Only found in Punjab and Jammu / Kashmir.

Don't confuse with Duraguard Cement.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Elevated Jharkhand Structures
metas.note: These elevated structures are found a lot of them between Hazaribagh and Ranchi in Jharkhand.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Extended Vertical Bar
metas.note:
Extra vertical bar at the top of the pole, extends significantly over the pole.

85% West Bengal 12% Chhattisgarh
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Generic Poletop
metas.note: Typically not south of Maharashtra-Chhattisgarh-Odisha except in Kerala. Generic pole does NOT include any bars on the top of pole
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Generic Poletop with Grey Crossbar
metas.note:
If the generic poletop has a grey crossbar, you're most likely in Uttar Pradesh. It's less commonly found in Odisha, Bihar, and more rarely in Haryan and Jharkhand.

If it's in South India, it's 98% Kerala.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Goa Poletops
metas.note:
This poletop has two crossbars, the top one is short with 2 insulators, the bottom one is long with 4 insulators.

It's mostly found in Goa (95%) and rarely in Kerala (2%), Maharashtra (1%) and Karnataka (1%)
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Green Pole Stripes
metas.note: Green pole stripes are commonly found in the far western roads of Arunachal Pradesh. They are often combined with yellow or white stripes.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Gujarat - Non-Holey Pole
metas.note: Almost all poles in Gujarat are holey poles. Generic poles are only found sometimes in very far west Gujarat, near the border with Pakistan
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Harsil Road
metas.note: On the road south of Harsil (UK), you will find a large amount of poles with red/yellow stripes and black bollards with stripes (see UK/JH bollard)
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - HiBond Cement
metas.note: Recognizable by the wavy triangle logo. Found only in Gujarat.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Himachal Pradesh - Double Guardrail
metas.note: The NH5 near Sarahan ist the only road in Himachal Pradesh with a double guardrail.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Hollow Metal Pole
metas.note:
This means, it has an indent that runs through the whole pole. If you look at it from the top, it looks like a C.

Most common in Mizoram, seen in Himachal Pradesh as well.

Note by MB: Seen this in central states too, but still useful together with landscape ig.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Hyderabad Mesh Pole
metas.note:
Mesh pole with three wires on one or both sides, that are connected to the pole in a "pyramid shaped" extension on the side.

Note that it has to be a pole, not a cellphone tower (which would be a lot larger).

Found around Hyderabad, TG
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - JK Lakshmi Cement
metas.note:
Found in North and Central India, plus Jharkhand, Odisha and Gujarat. Sometimes also in Maharashtra.

Don't confuse with JK Power Cement (which hasn't been researched yet).
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - JSW Cement
metas.note: Found in South India, Goa + Maharashtra, and Bihar, West Bengal and Odisha.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Karnataka Pole
metas.note:
In Karnataka (85%), and sometimes in Haryana (6%), Western Andhra Pradesh (6%) and rarely Uttar Pradesh (1%), you can find trident poletops on concrete poles where the central insulator is attached directly to the top of the pole, while the other two are attached to a horizontal crossbar positioned slightly further down. There are different variants of this poletop that increase the likelihood for Karnataka.

Note by MB: Make sure not to confuse it with the trident with a small bar at the top (see images).
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Karnataka Pole - Karnataka Insulator
metas.note:
If a trident pole has these insulators with three circles and air between them, it is found 98% in Karnataka.

The other versions of this poletop have lower certainties for Karnataka.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Kerala "Weird" Poletop
metas.note: Made of metal, has a "generic" crossbar, but additionally a very long bar that extends into one direction at the top, which holds the actual insulators.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Kerala Bollard
metas.note: What makes these bollards unique is the red reflector on a stone bollard.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Kerala Bridge
metas.note: Blue and white bridges can commonly be found all over Kerala. They can sometimes be painted in green.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Kerala Yellow Marker
metas.note:
Small yellow pole markings are commonly found in Kerala.

Can also be used to rule out Kerala since 80-90% of all poles have it.

Can also be found in Goa (2-3%)
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Konark Cement
metas.note: Found in Bihar, West Bengal and Odisha.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Large Rectangle
metas.note: In West Bengal you may also find poletops containing two crossbars which are connected to each other with thin vertical supports on either side. The lower bar is connected on either side to the pole with diagonal supports.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - License Plates - Andhra Pradesh
metas.note:
Sometimes, unblurred license plates can be seen (particularly often on trucks). The first two letters give the state. The next two numbers give the district (really not worth learning)

AP stands for Andhra Pradesh.

The exception is license plates that do not start with letters or with T0. Those rarer license plates are national.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - License Plates - Karnataka
metas.note:
Sometimes, unblurred license plates can be seen (particularly often on trucks). The first two letters give the state. The next two numbers give the district (really not worth learning)

KA stands for Karnataka.

The exception is license plates that do not start with letters or with T0. Those rarer license plates are national.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - License Plates - Kerala
metas.note:
Sometimes, unblurred license plates can be seen (particularly often on trucks). The first two letters give the state. The next two numbers give the district (really not worth learning)

KL stands for Kerala.

The exception is license plates that do not start with letters or with T0. Those rarer license plates are national.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Madhya Pradesh - Rock Walls
metas.note: In Madhya Pradesh, rock walls are very common around two national parks : Kuno National Park and Panna National Park
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Maharashtra Pole
metas.note:
This pole is either metal or concrete (but more skinny than a generic pole). It has one or two small bars near the poletop.

It's not exclusive to Maharashtra, but very common there.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Manipur Poletop
metas.note: In Manipur you can often find trident poletops on poles made entirely out of metal. They sometimes have small bars on the top of the trident.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Max Cement
metas.note: Found only in North-East India, but not in Nagaland or Arunachal Pradesh.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Meghalaya - Divided Road
metas.note:
The NH6 north of Shillong is the only divided highway in Meghalaya.

Note by MB: A good way to tell you're in Meghalaya is the lack of non-latin scripts.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Metal Holey Poles
metas.note: Metal holey poles are common in Kerala.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Metal Mesh Poles
metas.note: Metal poles with a mesh pattern are commonly found in Sikkim (93%) and rarely in Arunachal Pradesh (5%)
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Mycem Cement
metas.note: Found only in Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Nagaland Auto
metas.note: Auto Rickshaws with a Black Body and a Yellow Roof (i.e. reverse to the Andhra Pradesh / Telangana variant) are commonly found in Nagaland.
metas.footer: Source: Northeast India by Cassa, Alok and the GeoGuessr India community

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - NH51 / Gujarat
metas.note: The NH51 in Gujarat is unique because it is lined with many dark metal poles (unlike most of Gujarat which has concrete holey poles). It is also divided and paved with concrete.
metas.footer: Source: bibberbang1234 on the LearnableMeta Discord + additional self research

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Odisha Bridge
metas.note: Some bridges in Odisha are made of green and white concrete blocks as guardrails
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Orange Pole Paint
metas.note: This Orange Pole Paint is found on the NH15 in Arunachal Pradesh
metas.footer: Source: Northeast India by Cassa, Alok and the GeoGuessr India community

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Orange Pole Stickers
metas.note: These orange stickers on metal poles can be found in Uttarakhand, mostly in the East.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Painted Stripes
metas.note: Metal poles in Uttarakhand sometimes have those red or yellow stripes painted on them.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Pole with Black/White bottom
metas.note:
White and black stripes on the bottom of a pole are found in both Meghalaya and Tripura.

Note by MB: Don't confuse this with the Tamil Nadu polepainting, which is always white-black-white and further up on the pole.
metas.footer: Source: Northeast India by Cassa, Alok and the GeoGuessr India community

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Pole with Red Paint
metas.note:
Silver painted poles with a red or brown top.

Common in Uttarakhand and Uttar Pradesh, sometimes Tripura & Mizoram.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Punjabi Electricity Counters
metas.note: Electricity counters in Punjab are usually mint green with small window-like squares. They can rarely be seen in Haryana.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Pure Metal in Uttarakhand
metas.note: In the Himalayas, pure metal poles are usually more common in the North-East. If you see them in the Northwest, it's most likely Uttarakhand.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Rajasthan - Rock Walls / Flat Landscape
metas.note: Rock walls are not unique to Rajasthan, but if you know or have a feeling you’re in Rajasthan, it is most common south of Udaipur (hilly) and southeast of Kota (flat). This can be used combined with the elevation to get the precise area.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Rajasthan - Rock Walls / Flat Landscape
metas.note: Rock walls are not unique to Rajasthan, but if you know or have a feeling you’re in Rajasthan, it is most common south of Udaipur (hilly) and southeast of Kota (flat). This can be used combined with the elevation to get the precise area.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Rajasthan Mesh Pole
metas.note:
Found 90% in Rajasthan.

Sikkim and Telangana also have Mesh poles, but they're different.

The Sikkim pole is slimmer, while the Telangana pole has "triangles" at the top.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Ramco Cement
metas.note: Found in South India, however less common in Karnataka. Sometimes also found in West Bengal.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Red & White Bollard
metas.note: It is quite rare to see red and white bollards, but they are mostly found in far west Arunachal Pradesh
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Red&White Tree Paint
metas.note: In Bihar, and less commonly Jharkhand, you may find trees with four red and white stripes painted near the bottom.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Rusted Hollow Pole
metas.note: Thin rusted Poles that are hollow, i.e. have an indent going from the bottom to the top, are found in Maharashtra, and sometimes in Chhattisgarh.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Sanghi Cement
metas.note: Recognizable by the Lion Logo. Found only in Gujarat.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Seperated Bus Lane
metas.note: On large roads in Ahmedabad and Surat you can find separated middle lanes for buses. Beware that people will still often drive in these lanes.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Shree Cement
metas.note: Found everywhere, except for Himalayan states, North Eastern States, Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Sikkim Taxis
metas.note: Taxis in Sikkim often have a painted yellow hood or a small yellow circle on it.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Simple Black Sticker
metas.note:
This black sticker usually just has few characters, often just a number.

35% Tamil Nadu 35% Andhra Pradesh 20% Telangana

Note that it's a weak meta for Andhra over Telangana.

Do not confuse for Andaman & Nicobar Islands.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Small Extra Bar
metas.note:
Short bar at the top of the pole.

Mostly in Rajasthan and Telangana Sometimes Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra Rarely Jharkhand.

In the Northeast, it can be found in Tripura or rarely in Arunachal Pradesh
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Small Ring Pole
metas.note:
Very similar to a second vertical bar, but it is attached to the pole on its ends, rather than in the middle, giving it a ring shape. What differentiates it from the big ring pole is that the bar isn't far away from the pole.

35% Maharashtra 35% Madhya Pradesh 20% Chhattisgarh 2% Rajasthan & Mizoram 1% Tripura
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Small Trapezoid
metas.note:
Trapezoid poletop, but the diagonal bars do not reach the end of the crossbar.

Most common in flat Arunachal Pradesh Sometimes in Tripura
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Square Stick Fences
metas.note:
In the northeast you will commonly see fences made of thin wooden sticks in a square pattern.

They can also sometimes be seen in Odisha, which has a very different landscape, making it useful to distinguish Odisha from other eastern states.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Star Cement
metas.note: Found in North-East India, West Bengal and sometimes Bihar.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Symmetric Trident / Asymmetric Insulators
metas.note:
60% Tamil Nadu 20% Telangana 15% Andhra Pradesh

Important that the crossbar is symmetric, if it's asymmetric, it's usually TG.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - T-shaped Pole Extension
metas.note:
This pole extensions (above the pole) with 3 insulators

45% Andhra Pradesh 45% Telangana 9% Tamil Nadu
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Tall, Narrow Rectangle Poletop
metas.note: A variety of poletops attached to the pole with two vertical bars forming a tall and narrow rectangle can be found in West Bengal.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Tamil Nadu Pole
metas.note:
3 insulators in a horizontal line, or middle insulator slightly above others

88% Tamil Nadu 5% Bihar 3% Haryana 2% Uttar Pradesh 1.5% Andhra Pradesh
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Telephone Speaker Pole
metas.note: In Assam, Meghalaya and Mizoram you commonly see metal poles where the poletops look like "telephone speakers". There are different variants of it, but it can generally be found in Meghalaya, Assam and Mizoram.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Telephone Speaker Pole - Bars in different directions
metas.note:
In Assam, Meghalaya and Mizoram you commonly see metal poles where the poletops look like "telephone speakers". There are different variants of it, but it can generally be found in Meghalaya, Assam and Mizoram.

If the bars point in different directions, it's often in Meghalaya.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Telephone Speaker Pole - Dark Metal / Single Bar
metas.note:
In Assam, Meghalaya and Mizoram you commonly see metal poles where the poletops look like "telephone speakers". There are different variants of it, but it can generally be found in Meghalaya, Assam and Mizoram.

If it's a single bar, with dark metal, it's 80% Meghalaya 15% Assam
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Telephone Speaker Pole - Grey Metal
metas.note:
In Assam, Meghalaya and Mizoram you commonly see metal poles where the poletops look like "telephone speakers". There are different variants of it, but it can generally be found in Meghalaya, Assam and Mizoram.

If the pole is made out of bright/grey metal, it's 45% Meghalaya 45% Assam
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Telephone Speaker Poles - Dark Metal / Double Bar
metas.note:
In Assam, Meghalaya and Mizoram you commonly see metal poles where the poletops look like "telephone speakers". There are different variants of it, but it can generally be found in Meghalaya, Assam and Mizoram.

If it's dark metal and has two bars, it's 65% Meghalaya 15% Assam 15% Mizoram
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - TG/AP Bridge
metas.note: Bridges in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh are often recognizable by the color of their guardrails. It is often made of vertical red/pink/orange concrete blocks with horizontal white/light yellow blocks.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Thai Bollards
metas.note: "Thai" bollards (white-black-white) are found in Odisha.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Thick Grey Trapezoid
metas.note:
Commonly found in Kerala (especially with yellow stickers).

Note that there's also a version with the two indents, which is not found in Kerala, but in Andhra Pradesh.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Thick Trapezoid - Two Indents
metas.note:
Thick gray trapezoid, with two indents in the pole material.

97% Andhra Pradesh
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Thin Grey Metal Poles
metas.note: Thin grey metal poles are seen all over northeastern India and in the Himalayan region of Uttarakhand and Himachal Pradesh. You will commonly see two of these poles in close proximity.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Tiny Crossbar
metas.note: A pole with no poletop except for this tiny bar, is often found in Odisha (70-80%)
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Toothbrush + Horizontal Bar
metas.note:
Insulators at the top, directly attached to the concrete, pointing in one direction. Below, there is a metal crossbar with no insulators.

70% Maharashtra 10% Chhattisgarh 5% Himachal Pradesh
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Trapezoid - Dark Metal
metas.note:
Trapezoid poletops with poles completely made out of dark metal, are found in Chhattisgarh 95% of the time.

If it's not made out of dark metal, it's less certain.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Trapezoid Pole (Concrete)
metas.note:
A connector on the pole which looks like an upside down trapezoid.

80% Chhattisgarh 10% Maharashtra 3% Karnataka 2% Odisha 1% each: Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Assam

NOTE: They can also be paired with Holey Poles in Gujarat and Ladder Poles in Andhra Pradesh, thus only use the trapezoid when no other pole meta is present. Northeast India also has some trapezoid poletops that look a bit different.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Triangle Poletop
metas.note: Upside down triangle poletops placed below the top of the pole are commonly found in Maharashtra, Chhattisgarh, and less commonly in Madhya Pradesh.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Triangle Poletop / Dumbbell Insulators
metas.note: 32% Maharashtra 32% Madhya Pradesh 32% Chattisgarh 1% Andhra Pradesh 1% Telangana
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Triangle Poletop & Three Insulators
metas.note:
Triangle poletops with three insulators on top can be found in Jammu and Kashmir, sometimes in Himachal Pradesh.

Note: Do not confuse this with the regular triangle poletops which can be found elsewhere. Also even these poletops are not 100% unique to J&K
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Triangle Window
metas.note:
Triangle-shaped window insulators on a crossbar.

90% Jharkhand 2% Chhattisgarh 1% Bihar
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Trident / Asymmetric Bar
metas.note:
This pole has an asymmetric crossbar, with one side double the length of the other, and two insulators on the longer side, and one on the shorter side.

Research is not conclusive due to its rarity, but it's estimated to be 95% Telangana.

Note by MB: It's important that the bar is asymmetric, if it's symmetric, and the insulators are asymmetric, it's a different pole.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Triple Karnataka Poletop
metas.note:
Concrete Trident pole with three crossbars.

Do not confuse it with the North-Eastern Triple Poletop, which has shorter crossbars and is made out of metal instead of concrete.

Found 98% in Karnataka 0.5% in Gujarat
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Tripura Pole
metas.note: Tripura Poles often tend to have an extra bar underneath as well as the small crossbar on top.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Two Section Pole - High Bar
metas.note:
Two-section poles can sometimes be regionguessed by looking at the bar above the crossbar (which doesn't always exist).

If it's high on the pole (meaning you can barely see the concrete above it), it's 80% Telangana, 20% Andhra Pradesh (especially western)

Sometimes it's hard to tell though, so it can be a bit of a cope
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Two Section Pole - Low Bar
metas.note:
Two-section poles can sometimes be regionguessed by looking at the bar above the crossbar (which doesn't always exist).

If it's lower on the pole (meaning you can see a bit of concrete over the bar), it's 85% Andhra Pradesh, 15% Telangana

Sometimes it's hard to tell though, so it can be a bit of a cope
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Two Section Poles
metas.note: Poles divided in two sections, in a similar fashion to Brazilian poles, are common in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - UK/JH Bollard
metas.note: This black bollard with stripes (usually at least one of the colors: red, white, orange) can be found in Jharkhand and Uttarakhand.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Ultra Tech Cement
metas.note: Can be found anywhere except for North-East India.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Uttarakhand - Red/white pole paint
metas.note: In Uttarakhand, you can find these red-white stripes on poles on random roads around Dwarahat.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Vertical Bar
metas.note:
Vertical bar at the poletop. It is attached to the pole with two short bars. Note that those bars are not at the end of the vertical bar, which would make it a ring pole (and change the distribution)

50% Chhattisgarh 30% Madhya Pradesh 15% Maharashtra 10% West Bengal
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Vertical Insulators
metas.note:
3-5 Insulators pointing upwards, attached to the pole.

Common in Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, sometimes Bihar.
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - West Bengal E-Rickshaw
metas.note: West Bengal only has E-Rickshaws. They have a unique shape and are often blue.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - White Metal Plate
metas.note:
Can sometimes be rusted and a bit more brown.

Found in Northern States: Uttar Pradesh, Haryana, Bihar, sometimes Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - White-Black-White Paint
metas.note:
Markings on poles and trees, consisting of one black stripe in-between two white ones, are common in Tamil Nadu.

Note by MB: This only counts if it's black, not with other colors.

99.3% Tamil Nadu 0.02% Andhra Pradesh 0.01% Madhya Pradesh
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt &India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Windfarms
metas.note:
The places with the most wind farms are indeed Gujarat, Karnataka, Maharashtra and Tamil Nadu. This is pretty advanced knowledge, but region guessing states can be possible by learning where wind farms are:

  • Gujarat: Southwestern half
  • Karnataka: Davanagere to Hubballi
  • Tamil Nadu: Max South; Around Coimbatore
  • Maharashtra: Tristate to Madhya and Gujarat; Around Jath (southern)
  • Rajasthan: Jodhpur to Jaisalmer
  • Madhya Pradesh: West & North of Indore
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Window Poletop
metas.note: Small metal poletops in the shape of a window are found in Punjab and Haryana. 93% Punjab 4% Haryana 1% Delhi & Jammu (on Punjabi border) 0.5% Rajasthan 0.2% Ladakh
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Wonder Cement
metas.note: Found Northwest of Madhya Pradesh, however not in Himachal Pradesh or further North.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Yellow Outer Lines
metas.note:
Parts of roads NH6 and NH206 southeast of Shillong can be recognised by the presence of khasi pines with distinct yellow outer road lines and fresh dark pavement.

NOTE: This is the only road in Meghalaya that uses yellow outer road lines, but these lines exist in other states as well.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Yellow Pole Bands
metas.note: Between Aizawl and Champhai on the NH6, poles will have yellow bands.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Yellow Pole Stickers
metas.note: These orange stickers on metal poles can be found in Uttarakhand, mostly in the East.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Yellow Tuk Tuk / Black Roof
metas.note:
Yellow tuk tuks with black roofs are common in the southern Indian states of Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, and Tamil Nadu.

NOTE: They can also rarely be found elsewhere.

metas.name: India - Infrastructure - Zuari Cement
metas.note: Found in South India, especially in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Cement Company Meta by atomomc3904

metas.name: India - Infrasturcutre - Karnataka Symmetrical Poletop
metas.note:
2 insulators on each side, with the top of the pole sticking out.

Found in Karnataka (94%) and rarely in Tamil Nadu (4%) or Kerala (1%)
metas.footer: Source: India Poles by Duskron & Indiacord

metas.name: India - Landscape - Amygdaloidal Basalt
metas.note:
This is a volcanic rock, which is recognizable by it's dark color with white mineral patches on it.

It is mostly found between Pune and Jalgaon.

It's important to note that this rock alone, without the mineral patches is more widely spread.
metas.footer: Source: posted by unfazed on The Real Meta Research Group (RMRG) Discord

metas.name: India - Landscape - Andhra Pradesh - Red Soil
metas.note:
Andhra Pradesh has a long coast along the bay of Bengal and it is fairly recognizable because of the red soil combined with overall flatness. This is the area in which you fill find red soil in Andhra Pradesh.

Flat landscape with red soil and lots of Palmyra should pretty much always give the eastern India coast.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Landscape - Anisun River Valley
metas.note: A rocky desert can be found in this valley southwest of Nandyala, AP.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Landscape - Assam - Hilliness
metas.note: Hilliness in Assam is found mostly South or East of Nagaon.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Assam - North Mountains
metas.note: If you see Mountains to the North in Assam, you're on the border to Arunachal Pradesh. In my experience, this is a particularly common sight on the border east of Itanagar.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Badvel Valley
metas.note:
Wind turbines aligned on top of mountain ranges are very common in these mountain ranges valleys I would say. (I know there are some in RJ as well)

Even without wind turbines, you can click in this valley if you have a good north/south angle. I would even say that it is the only place in India with such big N/S dry ranges to the west AND to the east.

Differentiations:

  • Western ghats mountains in Maharashtra (Pune-Nashik area) have different angles
  • The other Mountain Range in Andhra Pradesh (near Odisha border) is less dry.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Landscape - Chaukhamba
metas.note: Chaukhamba, located near the town of Ukhimath, is a mountain massif covered in snow which can be recognised by its three distinct peaks, with the centre peak being the tallest.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Coastal Andhra Pradesh
metas.note:
Coastal Andhra Pradesh is characterized by a flat, agricultural landscape with coastal bushes

50/50 Tip ! Similar bushes can also be found in Gujarat, but Gujarat will often have distinct holey poles or have a boxy car. Also, Gujarat will primarily have date palms whereas Andhra will have palmyra palms as the main occurrence in palm trees.

The harder rounds in Andhra are the coastal, agricultural ones without any Palmyra or any pole. This basically becomes a 50/50 with any other flat & agricultural state.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Landscape - Dark Soil
metas.note: Distinctly dark soil is mainly found in Maharashtra and adjacent regions.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Dark Soil - Karnataka
metas.note:
Dark soil in India is usually found in and around Maharashtra.

In many cases you can see trident poles together with this dark soil, which will put you in Northern Karnataka, usually near the Maha border (free 4.5k+)

metas.name: India - Landscape - Dry Ganges River Valley
metas.note: Southern Haryana and Southern Uttar Pradesh are very agricultural, but often still look dry. These areas look like a mix of Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Landscape - Dry Mountains
metas.note: In Ladakh and northern Himachal Pradesh you can find an extremely dry landscape with little to no vegetation within the Himalayan mountains.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Dry TG/AP
metas.note: If you have a Telangana/Andra pole or Telugu with a dry landscape, you are likely in the area between Anantapur, AP and Shadnagar, TG (see image)
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Landscape - Elevated Dry Road
metas.note: Elevated Roads (similar to Bangladesh), with a dry landscape, are common in and around Jharkhand.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Elevated Jammu & Kashmir
metas.note: While a lot of the coverage in Jammu is located in flat parts, there are some areas north and northeast of the city of Jammu with elevation, where you will be able to see a lot of pines.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Landscape - Ganges River Valley
metas.note:
The northern plains, also known as the Ganges River Valley, of India are very fertile with extremely flat and open agricultural fields.

Note by MB: Agriculture can be found in many parts of India. I think what sets apart these Northern Plains is the lack of palm trees (except for the occasional date palms and the Palmyra palm spam in Bihar).

metas.name: India - Landscape - Gujarat - Dead Landscape
metas.note:
Salt flats and coastal marshes with nearly no vegetation, other than short yellow or brown grass, can be found in parts of Gujarat. Shallow bodies of water can often be seen around these areas.

NOTE: The soil in western Rajasthan will be a lot more sandy and you’ll typically be able to see short desert shrubs.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Guntur Landscape
metas.note:
Around Guntur in Andhra Pradesh, you can find a landscape that combines the Andhra Pradesh Panhandle and the agricultural east coast further south.

You will have lots of agriculture (more than in Panhandle) and also many palm trees (more than in the coastal region further south).

metas.name: India - Landscape - Haryana - North Haryana vibes
metas.note:
The northern part of Haryana is very green and agricultural.

Note by MB: Ganges River Valley in general looks like this, but I feel like this area is even greener and lusher, and it also has more sugarcane.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Landscape - Himachal Pradesh - North/South Valley
metas.note:
The city of Manali is fairly recognizable due to it being one of the two areas with coverage in a recognizable north-south valley. The other is from Kullu to Nagwain 50 km south of it.

The only way I came up with to tell the 2 apart is the vegetation but this is kinda fake since both cities are located in the same valley.

According to me, Manali has poplar trees and pines within the city whereas the other area doesn’t have much of those and mostly consists of random trees.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Landscape - Himalayas
metas.note: The by far tallest mountains in India are found in the Himalayas.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Ladakh - Snow Coverage
metas.note: Coverage extends to roads that are very high in altitude, so snow can be visible on the end of the streetview east of Leh.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Landscape - Madhya - Elevated
metas.note: There are a few places where you can have elevation in Madhya Pradesh. The main elevation areas are around Yawal and satpura park, as well as south of Indore
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Landscape - Madhya Pradesh - Red Soil
metas.note: Within Madhya Pradesh, a reddish or pinkish soil is generally more common towards the East.
metas.footer: Source: self-researched by Jayden and me

metas.name: India - Landscape - Maharashtra West Coast
metas.note: The landscape west of the Western Ghatts in Maharashtra is quite unique. It has a lot of forests, and a dark brown soil. It's mostly a vibe thing, but it looks kinda like Kerala but with less palms.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Mechuka Valley
metas.note: The Mechuka valley is the only place in Northeast India where snowy mountains are visible. The valley contains brownish grass and a plethora of Bhutan white pine. North of Mechuka the coverage gradually becomes overcast and somewhat dark.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Meghalaya Hills
metas.note: The landscape in Mizoram mainly consists of lush, green valleys with fairly low vegetation with eroded, smooth hillsides with a flat top.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Mizoram Hills
metas.note: The landscape in Mizoram mainly consists of lush, green valleys with fairly low vegetation with eroded hillsides having many small peaks scattered around.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Monoliths
metas.note: Near the southern tip of Tamil Nadu, you can find these large monolithic mountains, with huge exposed rocks. Several of these mountains can be seen from afar, especially the Magenthiragiri hills.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Mountains in Tamil Nadu
metas.note: Mountains in Tamil Nadu can be found along the western border. Additionally, there's a lot of mountains west of Madurai and some east of Salem.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Landscape - NH3 between Gramphu and Dalang
metas.note: This section of road features huge mountains, with a little bit more **green on their slopes. **
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Landscape - Panhandle Andhra Pradesh
metas.note:
The panhandle of Andhra Pradesh looks quite different than the rest of the state. It is much greener (and has an arguably "darker greener" tone). There are also A LOT more coconut palms here than anywhere else in AP.

Other parts of Andhra Pradesh do have Palmyra Palms, but Coconut palms are kinda rare outside of the panhandle.

The area south of Tirupati in Andhra Pradesh can also look extremely similar, but it has a lot less coverage.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Punjab - Elevated
metas.note: Punjab is generally a very flat state. If you know you're in Punjab, but it's hilly or mountains, you're on the border to Himachal Pradesh
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Landscape - Rajasthan - Mountains
metas.note: The biggest mountainous areas in Rajasthan are around Alwar max northeast and Udaipur - Mount Abu area
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Landscape - Rajasthan - NorthEast Ridge
metas.note: In Rajasthan, there is a North-east angled ridge going from Mount Abu area to New Delhi
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Landscape - Rajasthan - Rolling Hills
metas.note: In Rajasthan, rolling hills are common for the area south of Udaipur
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Landscape - Rajasthan Vibes
metas.note: Rajasthan is a state that is drier than its surrounding states. It's difficult to explain, but many locs in Rajasthan just have a certain 'drier' vibe. If you saw this loc and thought 'This looks like Rajasthan', pat yourself on the back :)

metas.name: India - Landscape - Red soil
metas.note: Red soil can be found in several regions, but mainly near the southern west coast and in and around Chhattisgarh and western Odisha.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Rewa Ridge
metas.note: A pretty straight east-west range with a slight north east angle can be found near Rewa. It is fairly easy to recognize.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Landscape - Rockiness
metas.note:
Telangana and Andra Pradesh have a lot of “rockiness”. It can be rocks on the side of the road, boulders or even rocky hill slopes but they share that in common.

I found it to be more in Telangana so the meta is here, but note that it can extend to surrounding states of Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh.

Note by MB: In my experience, in AP, rockiness is very common west of the ridge from Tirupati to Nallamala Forest.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Landscape - Rural Manipur Landscape
metas.note:
Since Imphal is located in a valley, it is fairly simple to recognize it after a few games.

The landscape around the city consists of agricultural fields surrounded by mountains, so it is pretty easy to know you are in Imphal.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Landscape - Snow Coverage in the Mountains
metas.note:
This coverage can be found on the 3 in Himachal Pradesh near the Ladakh border.

The coverange extends from Zing Zing Bar to Killingsarai

metas.name: India - Landscape - Southern Tamil Nadu Red Soil
metas.note: A flat, bushy landscape with very red soil can be found in southern Tamil Nadu.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Spiti River Valley
metas.note:
The shape of the mountains iin this valley are truly unique : very dry, very high in elevation and sparsely green.

If you have trouble making the difference between this road and the NH3 to the west because it looks roughly similar, just know that the NH3 is paved whilst the Spiti river valley roads usually are not.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Landscape - Tirupati
metas.note: The city of Tirupati, AP can easily be recognized by the huge ridge in the North. Other metas, like black&yellow Tuk-Tuks, two-indent poles or simply Telugu language, can help confirm.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Western Ganges River Valley
metas.note: The western Ganges River Valley (Punjab/Haryana/Western UP) usually looks wetter and greener than the general Ganges River Valley. You can often see rice and sugarcane. Note that areas like this can still be found in other parts of the river valley, this is not a 100% meta

metas.name: India - Landscape - Western Ghats
metas.note:
The Western Ghats Mountains in the western part of Maharashtra can be recognised by their distinct ridgelines, often having plateaus rather than peaks. The northern part is drier while the southern part has more vegetation.

NOTE: During the rainy season the mountains will turn green and appear quite different.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Western Meghalaya Landscape
metas.note:
The western part of Meghalaya basically looks like bangladesh with hills. There are a lot of areca palms, banana trees and palms.

“Hilly forests with areca palms surrounding flat agricultural fields” is how I would best describe this part of Meghalaya.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Landscape - Western Rajasthan Landscape
metas.note: The western parts of Rajasthan can commonly be recognised by the dry landscape with sandy soil.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Western Uttarakhand Landscape
metas.note: The western half of Uttarakhand is typically far more barren than the other Himalayan regions, due to logging and erosion. The coverage northwest of Dehradun on the Himachal Pradesh Border has some especially barren hills full of brown grass and small roads next to cliffs.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Wonky Hills
metas.note: The Odisha Hills are very "wonky", i.e. they're undulating and can also very greatly in height.

metas.name: India - Landscape - Yawal Wildlife Sanctuary
metas.note: Unique hilly landscape with dead trees. Note that not all coverage in this park looks like this.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Language - Assamese
metas.note: Assamese, mainly found in Assam, also uses the Bengali script, with the addition of some characters, most notably ৰ and ৱ.

metas.name: India - Language - Bengali
metas.note:
Bengali is found in northeastern India and has a similar look to Devanagari (Hindi), however it can usually be recognised by the many letters featuring left-facing triangular shapes.

NOTE: This is also the language found in Bangladesh.

metas.name: India - Language - Devanagari Script
metas.note:
Hindi is the most common language in India and can be found in many central and northern regions. It uses the Devanagari script, which can be recognised by the line going through the top of each word and the straight vertical lines found in the majority of all letters.

Note by MB: Maharashtra has a different language that uses the same script.

metas.name: India - Language - Gujarati
metas.note: Gujarati, found in Gujarat, has a script with several similarities to the Hindi script, however it notably lacks the horizontal line at the top of every word.

metas.name: India - Language - Kannada
metas.note: Kannada is found in Karnataka and has a script with a lot of smooth curves and small circles. It is very similar to the Telugu script, with Telugu having one additional feature described in the next tip. Many characters also feature a distinct squiggly tail in the top right corner, which is less common in Telugu.

metas.name: India - Language - Malayalam
metas.note: The Malayalam script can be found in Kerala and mostly consists of somewhat simple-looking curvy letters, often containing upside-down U-shapes.

metas.name: India - Language - Marathi
metas.note:
Marathi, found in Maharashtra, also uses the Devanagari script, however it sometimes uses the letter ळ which is not found in Hindi.

Further differences, analyzed by MB:

  • Vowels with this symbol on top (ऍ) are exclusive to Marathi
  • Marathi uses Western Full Stops '.' , while Hindi uses Devanagari full stops '।'
  • This letter: ण is more common in Marathi (but not exclusive)
  • Marathi does NOT use those dots (nukta) on the bottom left of a character: ज़

metas.name: India - Language - Meitei
metas.note: Manipuri, also called Meitei, is the official language of Manipur. It is written using the Meitei script, which can be recognised by its many vertical lines and right angles.

metas.name: India - Language - Mizo
metas.note: Mizo, found in Mizoram, is the language most commonly found on the Indian coverage other than English, which uses the Latin script.

metas.name: India - Language - Only English
metas.note: The state of Meghalaya uses English primarily and no other scripts. Thus if you see a lot of signs and no non-english language, you are most likely in Meghalaya.

metas.name: India - Language - Oriya
metas.note: The Oriya script is found in Odisha and has a curvy look, with many letters having wide semi-circles covering the top. Many letters have a distinct diacritic in the shape of a wide curve above the top of the letter. A useful mnemonic is that the shape of the characters resembles a skull emoji .

metas.name: India - Language - Punjabi
metas.note: Punjabi can be found in Punjab in northwestern India. While the script looks somewhat similar to Hindi, it can generally be differentiated by the softer shape of the letters and the horizontal bar being broken over certain letters. It also has some distinctly different features, such as the letters ਨ, ਲ and ਅ as well as a diacritic in the shape of a soft curve beneath a letter.

metas.name: India - Language - Tamil
metas.note:
The Tamil script is found in Tamil Nadu and has a distinct combination of curves, straight lines and 90° angles. Some letters also have diacritics shaped like dots.

NOTE: Tamil is also commonly found in Sri Lanka.

metas.name: India - Language - Telugu
metas.note: Telugu, found in Telangana and Andhra Pradesh, has a script very similar to Kannada, but you’ll often see diacritics resembling checkmarks at the top of letters.

metas.name: India - Misc - AGP
metas.note:
The AGP's flag is an elephant on the dutch flag.

It operates only in Assam.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Flag Metas by Atomo MC

metas.name: India - Misc - BGPM
metas.note:
Yellow - Grey - Dark Red Flag with a nice landscape in the middle and some Devanagari (!) text at the top.

Found in West Bengal near the Sikkim border.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Flag Metas by Atomo MC

metas.name: India - Misc - BJP
metas.note:
BJP is one of the most popular national parties in India. You can find its flags basically everywhere. However, they are less popular in Tamil Nadu and Kerala, meaning their flags are rare there.

Their symbol is a lotus flower.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Flag Metas by Atomo MC

metas.name: India - Misc - BJP Spam
metas.note:
The BJP is a popular national party, and thus it's flags can be found everywhere. Their symbol is a lotus flower.

It is most popular in Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh and Odisha, so if you see a lot of BJP flags in one pano, you are likely to be in this belt.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Flag Metas by Atomo MC

metas.name: India - Misc - Black & Yellow Taxis
metas.note: Black Taxis with yellow roofs are found in Meghalaya and Mumbai.

metas.name: India - Misc - Bodoland People's Front
metas.note: This flag with this tool on an Indian background is found in Bodoland, which consists of the districts in Assam bordering Bhutan.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Flag Metas by Atomo MC

metas.name: India - Misc - Communism
metas.note:
Communist symbolism is mostly found in Kerala. Second mostly, but significantly less, it's found in Tamil Nadu. Sometimes, it's also found in Tripura, Bihar, Jharkhand, Odisha and Chhattisgarh. You can rarely spot it in Maharashtra, West Bengal, Assam and Manipur.

The communist party has a youth organisation, the DYFI, with the same distribution.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Flag Metas by Atomo MC

metas.name: India - Misc - DMK
metas.note: Black and red colored flag. Other objects in this colors are also commonly found in the state of Tamil Nadu.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Flag Metas by Atomo MC

metas.name: India - Misc - Donyi Polo
metas.note: This flag that resembles the Japanese flag stands for Donyi Polo, a religion found in Arunachal Pradesh between Ziro and Anini.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Flag Metas by Atomo MC

metas.name: India - Misc - Gandhi Topi
metas.note:
This hat is called the Gandhi Topi is almost unique to Maharashtra. Note the shape which resembles a boat.

Note by MB: White hats in general are a common attire for Muslims in India, so make sure it's the boat shape.
metas.footer: Source: posted by unfazed on the GeoGuessr India discord

metas.name: India - Misc - Gorkha Seperatist Flag
metas.note: The flag is green-white-yellow and can be found in West Bengal near the Sikkim Border.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Flag Metas by Atomo MC

metas.name: India - Misc - IELTS
metas.note:
Advertisements for IELTS-exams are relatively often seen between Punjab and Western Uttar Pradesh

Note by MB: Of course, advertisements like this can theoretically be found everywhere.
metas.footer: Source: India GeoGuessr Guide - 2024 Edition by duskden2

metas.name: India - Misc - INC
metas.note:
INC is a popular national party, and found almost everywhere. The notable exceptions are West Bengal and Andhra Pradesh, where the INC has regional versions, meaning you won't find any INC imagery there.

Their symbol is a flat hand facing you, on the background of the Indian tricolor.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Flag Metas by Atomo MC

metas.name: India - Misc - India Union Muslim League
metas.note:
Green flag with half moon and star, pointing at the top left corner.

This party is almost exclusively active in Kerala. Mostly in the districts of Kozhikode and Malappuram.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Flag Metas by Atomo MC

metas.name: India - Misc - Jainism
metas.note: Jainism is a pretty rare minority religion. Jainist symbols are found mostly in Maharashtra, then Gujarat and Rajasthan, then Madhya Pradesh and Karnataka.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Flag Metas by Atomo MC

metas.name: India - Misc - Janata Dal
metas.note:
Flag is green-white-green, the symbol is an arrow.

Found only in Bihar.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Flag Metas by Atomo MC

metas.name: India - Misc - Karbi Colors
metas.note:
The Karbi are an ethnic group that inhabit two districts in Assam, Karbi Anglong and West Karbi Anglong.

Their flag is rarely shown, but you can often find Karbi colors (dark red, black and white) in those districts.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Flag Metas by Atomo MC

metas.name: India - Misc - Karnataka Flag
metas.note: This is an unofficial flag of Karnataka.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Flag Metas by Atomo MC

metas.name: India - Misc - Kongunadu Makkal Desia Katchi
metas.note: Flag of a political party active only in Tamil Nadu
metas.footer: Source: Indian Flag Metas by Atomo MC

metas.name: India - Misc - Lungi
metas.note: People wearing a Lungi, which looks like a towel wrapped around the waist, are more common in South India.
metas.footer: Source: posted by unfazed on the GeoGuessr India discord

metas.name: India - Misc - Manithaneya Makkal Katchi
metas.note: Flag of a political party only active in Tamil Nadu.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Flag Metas by Atomo MC

metas.name: India - Misc - Meitei Flag
metas.note: The Meitei people inhabit Manipur state, especially Imphal. Their flag is commonly found in and around that city.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Flag Metas by Atomo MC

metas.name: India - Misc - Naam Tamilar Katchi
metas.note:
Flag of a political party only active in Tamil Nadu.

The tiger symbol can sometimes be found without the flag.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Flag Metas by Atomo MC

metas.name: India - Misc - Navayana Buddhism
metas.note: This blue flag with this symbol in the middle is specific for Navayana Buddhism, the branch of Buddhism common in Central-Eastern Maharashtra.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Flag Metas by Atomo MC

metas.name: India - Misc - Odisha Shell (Political Party)
metas.note: This shell is the symbol of a Odisha specific political party: Biju Janata Dal
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Misc - Samajwadi Party
metas.note: Exclusive to Uttar Pradesh, their symbol is a bicycle.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Flag Metas by Atomo MC

metas.name: India - Misc - Sarnaism
metas.note: This flag and this symbol stand for Sarnaism. They are very localized, found in Ranchi and in Southern Jharkhand.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Flag Metas by Atomo MC

metas.name: India - Misc - Scarfs
metas.note: People wearing colorful scarfs are generally found in the north of India.

metas.name: India - Misc - Shivaji
metas.note: Shivaji is a person often depicted on statues in Maharashtra. He is always riding a horse, and is often accompanied by an orange flag.

metas.name: India - Misc - SKM
metas.note: This party has an orange-red-green flag and a table lamp as a symbol. It operates exclusively in Sikkim.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Flag Metas by Atomo MC

metas.name: India - Misc - Trinamool Congress / CMT
metas.note:
The flag of this party often has these flowers on some grass with the Indian flag as background.

It can be found mainly in West Bengal, however less commonly in the Northern Parts. Sometimes it's also found in Western Meghalaya
metas.footer: Source: Indian Flag Metas by Atomo MC

metas.name: India - Misc - Tripra Mothi
metas.note:
Tripra Mothi is a Tripura-specific party. Its flag has two vertical stripes, yellow and red.

Don't confuse it with the Karnataka flag, where the stripes are horizontal.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Flag Metas by Atomo MC

metas.name: India - Misc - UPPL
metas.note:
The flag of UPPL is yellow white green with a farmer on a tractor on it. Found in Bodoland, which consists of the Assamese districts bordering Bhutan.

Don't confuse this with the Gorkha seperatist flag, which is green-white-yellow.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Flag Metas by Atomo MC

metas.name: India - Misc - VCK
metas.note: Blue and red flag with a Myanmar-style star, found only in Tamil Nadu.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Flag Metas by Atomo MC

metas.name: India - Misc - YSR Congress
metas.note: This party is exclusive to Andhra Pradesh, and most popular in the South. Their symbol is a ceiling fan.
metas.footer: Source: Indian Flag Metas by Atomo MC

metas.name: India - Vegetation - Agave
metas.note:
Agaves are mostly found in Karnataka

Note by MB: This is generally a fake meta, Agaves can be found in many different places throughout India. But if you have really nothing else to go off, Karnataka is definitely a place to conside.r
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Vegetation - Areca Palm
metas.note:
Areca Palms can be recognised by their very thin trunk and a small crown.

They are most common in Assam, but also in other northeastern areas, stretiching to coastal Odisha. A second common region is Kerala and coastal Karnataka
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & India Palms by Duskron

metas.name: India - Vegetation - Assam - White Flowers
metas.note: In Assam, these white flowers can often be seen along the road in three areas: - The border to West Bengal - The border to Eastern Bhutan - West of Nagaon.

metas.name: India - Vegetation - Bhutan Cypress
metas.note:
Recognition (most visible when you look at the bottom of the crown):

  • symmetrical pattern of needles on twigs
  • thin twigs
  • twigs draping down

Found in:

  • mostly Western Sikkim and Sangti, Manda La, Salari (Arunachal Pradesh)
  • often in Khellong, Rupa (Arunachal Pradesh)
  • sometimes Rest of Sikkim, and Arunachal, west of Jamiri
  • rarely in West Bengal near Sikkim Border.
metas.footer: Source: Himalayas Conifers Tree Guide by Duskron

metas.name: India - Vegetation - Bhutan White Pine
metas.note:
Recognition:

  • whiteish-greyish tinge
  • Short needles
  • long slender cones
  • two rows of hanging needles
  • many branches, little space between them

Found in:

  • Max West Arunachal, Mechuka
  • sometimes Ziro, Neora Valley National Park (West Bengal)
  • very rarely Sikkim
metas.footer: Source: Himalayas Conifers Tree Guide by Duskron

metas.name: India - Vegetation - Blue Pine
metas.note:
Recognition:

  • individual branches well visible
  • edges of branches have thin brush of new needles
  • in higher elevation, the crown will be conical
  • needles drape down in all directions

Found in:

  • mostly: Max West Arunachal; Road south of Harsil
  • sometimes: Dharamshala, Manali, Kullu, Shimla, Sarahan, Southern Uttarakhand Mountains
  • rarely: Further inside the Uttarakhand mountains
metas.footer: Source: Himalayas Conifers Tree Guide by Duskron

metas.name: India - Vegetation - Calotropis Procera
metas.note: Calotropis Procera is found all over Rajasthan and less in surrounding states so it is a good clue for Rajasthan if you have a lot of it.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Vegetation - Chir Pines
metas.note:
Recognition

  • round crown
  • young pines: conical crown, thick brush for new needles Found in
  • Mountainous Uttarakhand; Shimla, Dalhousie (Himachal Pradesh); Elevated Jammu / Kashmir
  • Sometimes Dharamshala (Himachal Pradesh)
  • Rarely low elevation dry valleys in Western Arunachal Pradesh
metas.footer: Source: Himalayas Conifers Tree Guide by Duskron

metas.name: India - Vegetation - Coconut Palms
metas.note: Coconut palms are most common in Kerala, the Western Half of Karnataka and Southern Coastal Maharashtra In general, they appear near Coasts, near the border to Bangladesh, and anywhere South of Central Telangana

metas.name: India - Vegetation - Combination of Date Palm & Palmyra Palm
metas.note: In Jharkhand, you will very often see the combination of date palms (a lot of them) and palmyra palms. I think it is one of the best clues for getting Jharkhand because it’s pretty unique. I also saw a lot of that combination of palms in Telangana so be careful and look for text before guessing.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Vegetation - Date Palm
metas.note: Date palms can be found in Central India. They appear North of the Latitude of Chhattisgarh, except for Himalayan states, the Northeast and Western Gujarat/RJ.

metas.name: India - Vegetation - Date Palm - Tamil Nadu
metas.note: Within Tamil Nadu, date palms can be found in the North-East.

metas.name: India - Vegetation - Dead Trees
metas.note: These 'dead'-looking trees are a very strong point to go to Rajasthan. They are concentrated mostly southwest of Sikar.
metas.footer: Research by prizrak and Unassumed, shared on GeoGuessr India Discord

metas.name: India - Vegetation - Doum Palm
metas.note: Doum palms, which appear similar to Palmyra palms but with multiple branches, are almost exclusive to the union territory of Diu.

metas.name: India - Vegetation - Eucalyptus
metas.note: Eucalyptus trees are a good clue for the Uttarakhand foothills and nearby areas in Uttar Pradesh.

metas.name: India - Vegetation - Euphorbia Neriifolia
metas.note: This type of cacti (Euphorbia neriifolia) can commonly be seen as part of fences throughout Gujarat, western Maharashtra and the southern half of Rajasthan.

metas.name: India - Vegetation - Euphorbia Neriifolia (Hilly Landcape)
metas.note: South of Udaipur, you can find a very distinct landscape with narrow hills and a lot of this type of cactus (Euphorbia).
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Vegetation - Himalayan Cedar
metas.note:
Recognition:

  • downward bending branches
  • very short needles

Found in

  • Shimla, Dalhousie, Dharamshala, Palampur, Kasol, Jibhi, South of Kullu, South of Manali (HP); Road from Harsil to Gangotri (UK) and Southwestern UK in general
  • sometimes in Kangra, Solan, Manali-Dalang road (HP) and around Rudrapayag (UK)
  • rarely in eastern Uttarakhand
metas.footer: Source: Himalayas Conifers Tree Guide by Duskron

metas.name: India - Vegetation - Himalayan Hemlock
metas.note:
Recognition:

  • twig with two symmetrical rows of short needles
  • downward bending twigs
  • crowns look a bit disorganized

Found in:
