  • South of Senge and South of Dirang (Western Arunachal Pradesh)
metas.footer: Source: Himalayas Conifers Tree Guide by Duskron

metas.name: India - Vegetation - Indian Pitcher Plant
metas.note: The endangered Indian pitcher plant is exclusive to the Khasi Hills, which are mainly in Meghalaya. They can occasionally be spotted on road sides, especially on the NH206 north of Umlārem.

metas.name: India - Vegetation - Jand Tree
metas.note:
This tree, often called Jand by Indians, can be recognized by the clusters of leaves at the end of thick branches.

It is found in Northern Rajasthan and Southern Haryana/Punjab.

metas.name: India - Vegetation - Japanese Cedar
metas.note:
Recognition:

  • puffy, conical crown
  • smooth reddish bark with parallel vertical indents
  • "sea grass twigs" (look at picture #3)
  • twigs growing in all directions

Found in:

  • Sikkim/WB Border
  • Meghalaya Hills
  • Dirang, Khellong, Bomdila (Arunachal)
  • sometimes more north in Sikkim and west of Jamiri (Arunachal)
  • rarely east of Jamiri (AR)
metas.footer: Source: Himalayas Conifers Tree Guide by Duskron

metas.name: India - Vegetation - Khasi Pines
metas.note:
Recognition:

  • disorganized crowns, neither conical nor round
  • younger pines can appear round, but have shorter needles

Found in:

  • Meghalaya Hills
  • Raga & South of Ziro Junction (Arunachal Pradesh)
  • Imphal (Manipur)
  • Champhai, Darlawn (Mizoram) Less commonly:
  • Road from Ziro to Raga
  • North Vanlaiphai (Mizoram) Rarely:
  • Rest of Meghalaya and Mizoram
  • Arunachal Pradesh / Nagaland border
metas.footer: Source: Himalayas Conifers Tree Guide by Duskron

metas.name: India - Vegetation - Macaranga Peltata
metas.note: Parasol leaf tree (Macaranga peltata) is common along the southwestern coast anywhere south of Mumbai and seems to be virtually exclusive to that area, I have yet to find it anywhere else in India. To identify it, look for the teardrop shape of the leaves and the spot where the leaf stem connects to the inner part of the leaf blade.
metas.footer: Posted on Plantcord(Invite) by Avetixz

metas.name: India - Vegetation - Morinda Spruce
metas.note:
Recognition:

  • Dense Foliage
  • Shoots drape downwards

Found in:

  • Shimla, Kullu, Manali (Himachal Pradesh)
  • Uttarkashi, Dehradun, Ukhimath (Uttarakhand)
  • to a lesser extent: general area between Dehradun and Ukhimath
  • rarely in Eastern Uttarakhand
metas.footer: Source: Himalayas Conifers Tree Guide by Duskron

metas.name: India - Vegetation - Palmyra Palms
metas.note:
Palmyra Palms have a round crown with fan shaped leaves and a trunk with consistent thickness, giving them a lollipop shape.

They appear mostly in 3 areas:

  • Central Bihar
  • Coastal Pondicherry towards Andhra Pradesh/Odisha border + Telangana
  • Around Mumbai

They are also common in

  • coastal states from Tamil Nadu to West Bengal
  • Bihar & Eastern UP
  • Telangana
  • Eastern Gujarat

metas.name: India - Vegetation - Pindrow
metas.note:
Recognition:

  • Symmetrical Branches
  • Layered Clusters
  • Clusters shaped like an "inverse function" (see images)
  • narrow, conical, dense foliage

Found in:

  • Jibhi (HP), Chinyalisour, Ukhimath (UK)
  • sometimes Shimla (HP), Range from Dehradun to Rishikesh (UK)
  • rarely remaining UK Mountains; Dharamshala, Palampur, Kullu, Kasol, Manali (HP)
metas.footer: Source: Himalayas Conifers Tree Guide by Duskron

metas.name: India - Vegetation - Prickly Pear Cactus
metas.note: Found in Gujarat, mainly at the southern peninsula (could be fake)
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Vegetation - Rajasthan - Euphorbia Neriifolia (Flat)
metas.note: West of Mount Abu, you can find a lot of Euphorbia cacti with flat landscape. Note that this meta is only specific for Rajasthan, Euphorbia appears in other states, like Gujarat, too.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: India - Vegetation - Sikkim Fir
metas.note:
Recognition:

  • Symmetrical Shoots
  • Longer Needles
  • Small shoots make triangular shape
  • Seperated clusteres at different hights

Found in

  • Senge, Manda La (AR)
metas.footer: Source: Himalayas Conifers Tree Guide by Duskron

metas.name: India - Vegetation - Sikkim Larch
metas.note:
Recognition:

  • no needles in winter (which is currently all coverage in India with this tree)
  • Conical structure that resembles a christmas tree
  • lighter needles (if present)

Found in:

  • around Senge
  • sometimes around Manda La (both Arunachal Pradesh)
metas.footer: Source: Himalayas Conifers Tree Guide by Duskron

metas.name: India - Vegetation - Sikkim Spruce
metas.note:
Recognition:

  • needles organized in seperated clumps
  • darker than pines
  • individual branches visible (on high trees)
  • new shoots & many buds often visible from afar
  • Unique branch structure

Extremely rare in India, so far only a singular tree has been found in Manda La.
metas.footer: Source: Himalayas Conifers Tree Guide by Duskron

metas.name: India - Vegetation - Teak Forest
metas.note: Teak forests in wet season with boxy car can be found around the Gujarat-Maharashtra border between Surat and Nashik. The trees are quite distinctive, tall and narrow.

metas.name: India - Vegetation - Telangana - Coconut Palms
metas.note: If you see a Coconut, hedge in the south eastern half towards Andhra Pradesh, it has more of them.
metas.footer: Source: India region guessing doc by bzhbzhbzh

metas.name: Indonesia - Agriculture - Cassava
metas.note: Cassava (Manihot esculenta) can be recognised by its small, hand-shaped leaves. It can be found both in plantations as well as semi-wild in residential areas. It is most commonly seen in Lampung and Java with Lampung being the main hot spot.
metas.footer: Source: Real Meta Research Group

metas.name: Indonesia - Agriculture - Oil Palms
metas.note: Within Indonesia, oil palm plantations are mostly concentrated in Sumatra and Kalimantan. Palm plantations can rarely be seen in Sulawesi.

metas.name: Indonesia - Agriculture - Rice
metas.note: The majority of rice production is concentrated in Java, but can sometimes be found in other provinces, namely South Sulawesi and South Sumatra. They can rarely be found in other provinces as well.

metas.name: Indonesia - Architecture - Andesite
metas.note: Andesite, a dark, volcanic rock, is a common building material in Bali. You can often see gates, walls, and other intricately carved ornaments built from this material.

metas.name: Indonesia - Architecture - Bali Architecture
metas.note: Architecture in Bali is unique because it was influenced by old Balinese culture and Hinduism. The most important thing to look for are these crown-like roof pinnacles, found everywhere in Bali. Guardian statues and slit-drum towers are common too.

metas.name: Indonesia - Architecture - Boat Roof - Not Spiky
metas.note:
North Sumatra features similarly distinct boat-shaped roofs, however the roofs are less angled upward and they do not feature spires.

NOTE: These roofs are most commonly found near Lake Toba, due to its sacred history.

metas.name: Indonesia - Architecture - Boat Roof - Spiky
metas.note: West Sumatra features these distinct boat-shaped roofs.

metas.name: Indonesia - Architecture - Flat Tiles
metas.note: The tiles on roofs in South Kalimantan and Jambi look slightly different. The tiles are usually less rounded but flatter.

metas.name: Indonesia - Architecture - Horny Roof
metas.note:
Roofs with gable horns can be found most commonly in South Sulawesi, Riau and Central and South Kalimantan.

NOTE: Horned roofs are often found with Bugis roofs in South Sulawesi. Use this tip along with other clues to determine which region you are in.

metas.name: Indonesia - Architecture - Java Roof
metas.note:
Tiled roofs are most commonly found on the island of Java, and sometimes nearby regions such as southern Sumatra, the Lesser Sunda Islands, and South Kalimantan.

NOTE: The tiles on roofs in South Kalimantan and Jambi look slightly different. The tiles are usually less rounded but flatter.

metas.name: Indonesia - Architecture - Malay Canopies
metas.note: In the regions of Sumatra and Kalimantan that lie opposite Malaysia, many buildings have metal canopies with curved ends. These canopies are often blue or red.
metas.footer: Source: Real Meta Research Group

metas.name: Indonesia - Architecture - Nias Roof
metas.note: Steeply pitched roofs made of palm tree leaves can sometimes be seen on Nias Island, south west of North Sumatra.

metas.name: Indonesia - Architecture - Sheet Roofs
metas.note: Plain sheet metal roofs are more commonly found toward the north, where tiled roofs are not found. They are most commonly found on Kalimantan, Sulawesi and Sumatra.

metas.name: Indonesia - Architecture - South Sula House
metas.note:
These horizontal slots inside the triangles of the roofs are almost unique to Southern Sulawesi.

NOTE: They can rarely be found in East Kalimantan and West Nusa.

metas.name: Indonesia - Architecture - Sumba Roof
metas.note: You can find these distinct roofs with uniquely high-pitched peaks on Sumba.

metas.name: Indonesia - Architecture - Tongkonan
metas.note: A small region of South Sulawesi, around the city of Rante Pao, features these very unique houses, called Tongkonan, that have saddle-shaped roofs. The houses themselves are also elevated from the ground.

metas.name: Indonesia - Architecture - Wooden Chips Roof
metas.note: On Kalimantan, you can find these unique roofs made out of wooden chips.

metas.name: Indonesia - Car Meta - Gen 3 Antenna
metas.note: Generation 3 antenna coverage is most commonly found on Java, but can very rarely be seen on Bali in and around Denpasar. It is most commonly seen in East Java, as most of the antenna coverage in the west has been overwritten by Generation 4.

metas.name: Indonesia - Car Meta - Gen 3 Black
metas.note: Black Generation 3 coverage can be found almost everywhere in Indonesia, but is most common in Sulawesi.

metas.name: Indonesia - Car Meta - Jagasatru Car
metas.note: A black cab with men sitting in the truck bed can be seen near Jagasatru on Bali.

metas.name: Indonesia - Car Meta - Wooden Plank Car
metas.note: A white SUV with black bars and a wooden plank on the roof can rarely be seen in eastern Bali.

metas.name: Indonesia - Coverage Meta - Pink Air
metas.note: In some of the Generation 4 coverage in the city of Batam, a purple tint and a black blurred object can be seen. Although this camera glitch is most commonly found in Batam, you may spot it in nearby regions such as North Sumatra, around Medan. Make sure to look out for other clues before guessing.

metas.name: Indonesia - Infrastructure - Cigarette Blocks
metas.note: Central Sulawesi features these unique bollards that are painted black on the bottom, white in the middle, and yellow on the top.

metas.name: Indonesia - Infrastructure - Even Pole
metas.note: Indonesia uses two types of pole tops: even and uneven. This refers to the bar that holds the insulators and whether it is symmetrical to the pole itself. Knowing where even and uneven poles are most commonly found is useful for region guessing.

metas.name: Indonesia - Infrastructure - Green Bridge
metas.note: Green paint can often be seen on the side of bridges in South and Central Kalimantan.

metas.name: Indonesia - Infrastructure - Indented Pole
metas.note: Poles with an indent on both sides are found in West Java, Jakarta, and Banten.

metas.name: Indonesia - Infrastructure - North Sumatra Pole
metas.note: These poles are almost exclusive to North Sumatra. The bar which holds the insulators is even, but features uneven insulators with one on one side and two on the other.

metas.name: Indonesia - Infrastructure - Nusa Pole
metas.note: On the Lesser Sunda Islands ('Nusas'), you can find poles with an extra long support on the pole top. Sometimes, two supports can be present.

metas.name: Indonesia - Infrastructure - Pole Tape
metas.note: You can often see thin, black poles next to regular poles near the East Peninsula of Central Sulawesi. Two pieces of tape can be seen near the top of the poles, usually light blue and green. These can rarely be seen in northern South East Sulawesi.

metas.name: Indonesia - Infrastructure - Rectangle Attachment
metas.note: Bali features both even and uneven poles, as well as the Lesser Sunda island variants. You can also find this unique rectangle attachment on the pole tops in Bali.

metas.name: Indonesia - Infrastructure - Sulawesi Fences
metas.note: These painted fences are typically found on Sulawesi. They will be mostly painted white with blue or red.

metas.name: Indonesia - Infrastructure - Surabaya Pavement
metas.note: Pavement made out of bricks like this is found in East Java, particularly around Surabaya

metas.name: Indonesia - Infrastructure - Trapezoid Pole
metas.note: Pole tops in North and Central Sulawesi, and Gorontalo commonly feature an extra attachment right under the horizontal bar.

metas.name: Indonesia - Infrastructure - Triangle Attachment
metas.note:
You can find these poles with a triangle attachment under the horizontal bar in the following regions.

NOTE: This does not apply to stacked poles.

metas.name: Indonesia - Infrastructure - Trident Pole
metas.note: Trident style pole tops are most commonly found in Central Java and Yogyakarta, and rarely in South and West Kalimantan, and North Sumatra and Riau.

metas.name: Indonesia - Infrastructure - Uneven Pole
metas.note: Indonesia uses two types of pole tops: even and uneven. This refers to the bar that holds the insulators and whether it is symmetrical to the pole itself. Knowing where even and uneven poles are most commonly found is useful for region guessing.

metas.name: Indonesia - Landscape - Dryness
metas.note:
The Nusas typically look drier than other regions in Indonesia. The islands get especially dry towards the east, especially in Generation 3. Vegetation tends to look less tropical, but instead more brown with a lack of leaves. Sumba Island is also the driest of the Nusas.

NOTE: While less common, other regions such as Java can look similarly dry. Make sure to look out for other clues before guessing.

metas.name: Indonesia - Landscape - Lake Toba
metas.note: The region around Lake Toba, in North Sumatra, can be recognized by mountains surrounding the lake and Samosir Island in the middle. Overcast coverage is also common for the region.

metas.name: Indonesia - Landscape - Palu Bay
metas.note: Palu Bay is a unique slightly north-west facing bay just north of Palu city, which features mountains to the west of the bay, and a flat, more urbanised landscape to the east.

metas.name: Indonesia - Landscape - Red Soil
metas.note: Red soil can often be found on Batam and the Bangka Belitung islands, located east of mainland Sumatra.

metas.name: Indonesia - Landscape - Savannah
metas.note:
This savannah landscape is occasionally seen on North Sumba.

NOTE: In Generation 3, you will always see a white car.

metas.name: Indonesia - Misc - Christianity
metas.note: Indonesia is religiously a Muslim majority country, so seeing churches, and other Christian signs, is a good clue for these regions.

metas.name: Indonesia - Vegetation - Areca
metas.note: Areca palms (Areca catechu) are most prominent in western Sumatra; however they can also be seen elsewhere less commonly. They can be recognised by their relatively short and thick leaves.
metas.footer: Source: Real Meta Research Group

metas.name: Indonesia - Vegetation - Coastal She-Oak
metas.note: Coastal she-oak (Casuarina equisetifolia) can be found along the coast throughout much of the country, but particularly in Sumatra, Kalimantan and Java. Their leaves resemble the needles of pine trees, but are noticeably longer. Another species of she-oak can be found in mountainous regions throughout the country.
metas.footer: Source: Real Meta Research Group

metas.name: Indonesia - Vegetation - Coconut
metas.note: Coconut palms (Cocos nucifera) can be found in many regions throughout Indonesia, but are most abundant along the coast, especially in western Sumatra, southern Java, northern Sulawesi and North Maluku.
metas.footer: Source: Real Meta Research Group

metas.name: Indonesia - Vegetation - Footstool Palm
metas.note: Footstool palm (Saribus rotundifolius) has fan-shaped leaves similar to those of Palmyra palm; however the crown is more open, the leaves are thinner and the palm itself is usually taller. It can be found most notably in Sulawesi and more rarely in other parts of the country.
metas.footer: Source: Real Meta Research Group

metas.name: Indonesia - Vegetation - Gebang Palm
metas.note: Gebang palm (Corypha utan) can at first glance look similar to both Palmyra and footstool palm due to its fan-shaped leaves, however the leaves are noticeably larger, stiffer and more upright in contrast to the round crown shape of both Palmyra and footstool palm. Unlike most palms, the gebang palm will only flower once at the end of its life in a dramatic gesture where the leaves wither away and it shoots one large inflorescence into the heavens before it dies. It is found mainly in the east of the country, namely Sulawesi and the Nusas.
metas.footer: Source: Real Meta Research Group

metas.name: Indonesia - Vegetation - Milkweed
metas.note: Giant milkweed (Calotropis gigantea) is a small shrub with thick round leaves and pale flowers. It can be found in dry regions of Indonesia, namely the Nusas and parts of Java and Sulawesi.
metas.footer: Source: Real Meta Research Group

metas.name: Indonesia - Vegetation - Palmyra
metas.note: Palmyra palms (Borassus flabellifer) can be recognised by their fan-shaped leaves and dense round crowns. Compared to footstool palm, the crown is more dense, the leaves are heavier and the palm itself is usually shorter. It is found in dry parts of the country, namely the Nusas and South Sulawesi.
metas.footer: Source: Real Meta Research Group

metas.name: Indonesia - Vegetation - Sumatran Pine
metas.note: Sumatran pines (Pinus merkusii) in Indonesia can be found in a few pockets across the country, notable areas include North Sumatra and Java. They can be recognised by having long needles for leaves, but be careful not to confuse them with she-oak, which has even longer leaves.
metas.footer: Source: Real Meta Research Group

metas.name: Indonesia - Vegetation - White Leadtree
metas.note: White leadtree (Leucaena leucocephala) can be recognised by its delicate featherlike (bipinnate) leaves. Fruits are often also visible in the form of legume pods. It can be found mainly in the Nusas as well as a few other dry areas of the country.
metas.footer: Source: Real Meta Research Group

metas.name: Infrastructure - 29 in Ad Dhakhiliyah
metas.note: The southern section of Road 29 only has a middle white line, which along with the greyish and sandy desert landscape makes this road unique.

metas.name: Infrastructure - 31 (divided)
metas.note: The divided section of Road 31 is the only divided road going through a flat desert landscape.

metas.name: Infrastructure - 31 (single lane)
metas.note: This long stretch of Road 31 can be recognised by the light-coloured flat desert landscape along with the wide shoulders and the often faded road lines. The weather is usually somewhat cloudy.

metas.name: Infrastructure - 37 (Powerline)
metas.note: Road 37 travels in a generally northwest direction through a very generic, flat desert landscape. The angle is one of the best clues for this road. On the southern half, a big power line is visible to the northeast.

metas.name: Infrastructure - 39 (flat)
metas.note: Road 39 is also one of the more generic roads. Probably the best way to recognise it are the narrow, or even non-existent shoulders.

metas.name: Infrastructure - 39 (hilly)
metas.note: Road 39 is also one of the more generic roads. Probably the best way to recognise it are the narrow, or even non-existent shoulders. The western parts can get quite hilly

metas.name: Infrastructure - 42 north of Shalim
metas.note: North of Shalim Road 42 turns into a very wide unpaved road, with the soil being quite light in colour. You’ll sometimes see oil drills in the distance along this stretch.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Bin Color - Black
metas.note:
Black Bins can be found everywhere except for Batina North. They're also rarely found in South-Dhakiliyah.

NOTE: Even the dark blue and red regions are not 100% a certain colour.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Bin Color - Grey
metas.note:
Grey Bins can be found in Dharihar, South Dhakhiliyah, Dhofar, Bathina North and west of Muscat.

NOTE: Even the dark blue and red regions are not 100% a certain colour.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Black Bin / Black Sticker
metas.note: Black bins with a black sticker on the front can be found in Al Buraimi, Ash Sharqiyah North, and Muscat Governorates.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Black Bin / No Sticker
metas.note:
Black bins without stickers are mainly found in Al Batinah South Governorate and north of Al Khaburah in Al Batinah North Governorate.

NOTE: Black bins throughout Oman may appear like they lack stickers, so use this with caution.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Black Bin / White Sticker
metas.note: Black bins with a white sticker are found in Ad Dakhiliyah Governorate, southern Dhofar Governorate, and Muscat Governorate.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Black Western Bin
metas.note: Western-style small black bins are found in Muscat and eastern Al Batinah North Governorate.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Chevron Bin
metas.note:
Bins in Muscat governorate often have white-and-red chevron-like stickers on the sides.

Note by MB: 'often' really is an overstatement, definitely don't rule Muscat out if you don't have those stickers.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Fahud Road
metas.note: The road west of Fahud goes through a flat desert with pink-greyish soil. The road itself is in poor shape and without roadlines as well as the direction of the road being southeast.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Grey Bin / Black Sticker
metas.note: Grey bins with a black sticker on the front are found in Ad Dhahirah Governorate.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Grey Bin / No Sticker
metas.note:
Grey bins without a sticker on the front are found in Al Batinah North Governorate.

NOTE: They can have a sticker on the side.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Grey Bin / White Sticker
metas.note: Grey bins with a white sticker are commonly found in Ad Dakhiliyah Governorate, and sometimes in Dhofar Governorate.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Ibri Road
metas.note: The road going to Saudi Arabia from Ibri can be recognised by the completely flat desert landscape with bright pink-greyish soil along with the road having very wide shoulders and the overall great road condition. The southern portion goes in a straight northeast direction, and the northern section curves more and can have more shrubs.

metas.name: Infrastructure - License Plates - Assam
metas.note:
Sometimes, unblurred license plates can be seen (particularly often on trucks). The first two letters give the state. The next two numbers give the district (really not worth learning)

AS stands for Assam.

The exception is license plates that do not start with letters or with T0. Those rarer license plates are national.

metas.name: Infrastructure - License Plates - Maharashtra
metas.note:
Sometimes, unblurred license plates can be seen (particularly often on trucks). The first two letters give the state. The next two numbers give the district (really not worth learning)

MH stands for Maharashtra.

The exception is license plates that do not start with letters or with T0. Those rarer license plates are national.

metas.name: Infrastructure - North of Ubar Road
metas.note: The unlabelled road northwest of Ubar can be recognised by the small white markings between the dashes.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Oil Drills
metas.note: Oil drills are common around Amal and sometimes seen along Road 39.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Road to Yemen
metas.note: Just west of ميتان, only labelled in Arabic on Google Maps, literally translating to methane, there is a stretch of road, which has a uniquely light-coloured pavement. To the north, you can see sand dunes.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Road west of Ubar
metas.note: West of Ubar, the 43 and the unlabelled road west of it are still unpaved but now have a power line to the north. The desert landscape has an orange tint to it.

metas.name: Infrastructure - Side Sticker
metas.note: Regardless of colour, if the bins have a sticker on the side, you should be in one of the North Coast governorates.

metas.name: Infrastructure - signpost with yellow sticker
metas.note: Signposts in the Northern Territory can feature these yellow stickers.

metas.name: Infrastructure - South-East of Ubar Road
metas.note:
The road southeast of Ubar has a general northwest bound angle, along with a power line to the left of the road. You will often see signs of life in the form of farms or buildings on this road.

NOTE: Don’t mix this up with the 37, which has a similar angle, but is more desolate and can have sunset coverage.

metas.name: Infrastructure - State Flag - Arizona
metas.note: Each of the 50 states has its own state flag. These appear frequently enough that they are worth learning.

metas.name: Infrastructure - State Flags
metas.note: Each of the 50 states has its own state flag. These appear frequently enough that they are worth learning.

metas.name: Japan - Agriculture - Red Fields
metas.note: Agricultural fields with red soil are commonly found on several southern islands, most notably on the islands of Miyakojima and Ishigaki in southern Okinawa.

metas.name: Japan - Agriculture - Rice
metas.note:
Rice is mainly produced north of Tokyo. During growth, it resembles straws of grass. And when ready for harvest, brown husks are visible. They are also commonly planted in beds of water.

The regions of Chubu (21%), Kanto (15%), Tohoku (27%), and Hokkaido (7%) make up the majority of production.

metas.name: Japan - Agriculture - Sugarcane
metas.note: Sugarcane is almost exclusively found on the islands in southern Kyushu and Okinawa.

metas.name: Japan - Agriculture - Tea
metas.note:
Green tea plants are often grown in hedged rows. You will often see these fans mounted on poles, which serve the purpose of preventing frost from falling on the plants.

The prefectures of Shizuoka (36%) and Kagoshima (34%) make up the majority of the production, with Mie (7%), Miyazaki (4%), and other prefectures (17%) making up the minority.

metas.name: Japan - Architecture - Northern Roofs
metas.note:
The further you are north, roofs generally transition from tiled to level or flat sloped in order to compensate for heavy snowfall. Northern houses often have ladders attached to the side, giving roof access to clear snow.

NOTE: In addition to north to south, high-elevation mountainous regions or high snowfall areas often use such roofs, even in more central or southern prefectures.

metas.name: Japan - Architecture - Okinawa House
metas.note: Okinawa can often be recognised by the white concrete buildings with flat roofs.

metas.name: Japan - Architecture - Red Tiled Roof
metas.note: These unique red-tiled roofs are most commonly found in Chugoku, especially in the prefectures of Hiroshima and Shimane.

metas.name: Japan - Architecture - Shisa
metas.note: You can find these ‘Shisa’ guardian lions and house plaques with these specific characters in Okinawa. The colour and shapes of both can vary.

metas.name: Japan - Coverage Meta - Hokkaido Winter
metas.note: Hokkaido has very limited winter and snow coverage. Unless you are certain, it is often better not to guess this prefecture. Though, if you do find yourself in Hokkaido, these regions are most likely. Other low amounts of miscellaneous coverage is primarily in the southern half of the island.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Arrow
metas.note: This infrastructural arrow informs drivers of where the shoulder line is when under snow, and is located almost exclusively in Hokkaido.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Arrow - Bolts
metas.note: This arrow, found in the Aomori prefecture (or more rarely Hokkaido), has distinct silver bolts around the border.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Arrow - Long
metas.note: This variation, found in the Gifu prefecture, is long and thin.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Arrow - Northern 275
metas.note: This alternate yellow and black design can often be found on the northern part of National Highway 275 in Hokkaido.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Arrow - Yellow/Black
metas.note: This yellow and black arrow can be found on Hokkaido.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Arrow - Yellow/Green
metas.note: This yellow and green arrow is found southwest of Sapporo.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Birch Poles
metas.note: These artistically painted poles, made to resemble birch trees, are unique to the city of Date in Hokkaido.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Bollard - Akita
metas.note: This bollard, much like Tohoku, will be a thick, white bollard with an octagonal reflector. However, this Akita prefecture variation will have two yellow stripes underneath the reflector.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Bollard - Aomori
metas.note: This bollard, found in the Aomori prefecture, has two yellow stripes, a single circular reflector, and is extendable. Sometimes, only one thicker stripe near the top may be present.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Bollard - Black Stripe
metas.note: Some bollards on the island of Shikoku can have a black stripe just under the reflector. They can be found normally, attached to guardrails or walls.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Bollard - Extendable
metas.note: In the northern parts of the Chugoku region, you can primarily find these basic snow poles, with either a thin extended, or thin contracted top. They can also sometimes be found in Iwate.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Bollard - Okoyama
metas.note: This bollard, with an octagonal reflector, and red stripe underneath it, is exclusive to the Okayama prefecture. Additionally, there will be a sloped connection where the base meets the reflector.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Bollard - Orange Reflector
metas.note:
This flat, white bollard, found on the island of Kyushu and in Yamaguchi Prefecture, will have a series of separated orange reflectors on one side, and the same white on the opposite.

NOTE: Rarely, you may find similar bollards in Hokkaido. However, both sides will have orange reflectors.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Bollard - Striped / No Reflector
metas.note: These striped bollards (which cover over the original) have a thinner top half, and no reflectors, and are common to the Tohoku region. They are especially common in Akita prefecture.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Bollard - Tohoku
metas.note: This thick, white bollard, found in the Tohoku region, will have an octagonal reflector, and yellow stripe just underneath. In addition, you can find the same bollard, but with a rectangular top.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Bollard - Tohoku (Black Variant)
metas.note: Additionally to regular Tohoku bollards, there are two other variations. You can find a black octagonal, and rectangular version. They are often found on National Highways or Expressways and can have the number printed on them.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Bollard - Toyama
metas.note:
The Toyama prefecture bollard has one reflector, is extendable and has a red stripe underneath the reflector.

NOTE: Be careful: if there is either a second reflector, or a yellow stripe instead of a red one, these are different bollards. These are more common variations found across many prefectures.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Claymore
metas.note: Kerosine tanks, otherwise known as “Claymores”, can be found more commonly the further north you go. They are abundant in Hokkaido, but can be found in prefectures south of it, or in high elevation mountainous areas.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Ehime Cycling Route
metas.note:
Cycling routes in Ehime use an outside white, with an inside blue line. They are more commonly found along the coast but may be found further inland too.

While exceptions do exist, and can be found in other prefectures, they are the extreme minority.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Gas Tank
metas.note:
Hot water, gas and propane tanks can be found more frequently in northern prefectures or high elevation mountainous areas. Here are a few common variations you can find:

  • The standard hot water tank.

  • Covered propane tanks.

  • Exposed propane tanks.

  • These cylindrical tanks.

  • And finally, these circular tripod tanks.

Moreover, these are even more common in rural towns or villages, where major water or gas lines are unavailable.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Guardrail - Green Band
metas.note: Green bands on guardrails are most commonly found in Oita and Miyazaki, but can be found on all of Kyushu.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Guardrail - Hokkaido Sticker
metas.note:
You can find these chevron-like stickers, or more rarely orange ones, on guardrails in Hokkaido.

  • On the end or side of a guardrail.

  • Stuck to metal posts between wire fences, which are often found in Hokkaido.

  • On railings, which are often found on bridges, underneath the inside of the railing.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Guardrail - Red-Yellow Stripes
metas.note: Guardrail endings with these red and yellow striped stickers can commonly be found across Chugoku, except in Yamaguchi. They can also rarely be found in Niigata.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Guardrail - Yellow
metas.note: These distinctive yellow guardrails can be found in the Yamaguchi Prefecture.

metas.note: Tokyo City features a nice manhole design, with a 5 petal flower and many small circles on the outside.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Transformer - 2 or 3 Insulators
metas.note:
The transformers in Kanto, which can have three or two insulators, are often mounted on a wooden plate and two bars, or a round plate and a T-shaped bar.

NOTE: While the Hokkaido transformer may also be mounted on two bars, it will never have a wooden plate. Kanto ones can also be mounted without a wooden plate.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Transformer - Black Tap Connector
metas.note: The transformers in Chubu, which often have painted yellow numbers and black “tap” connectors, are either attached with large triangle and horizontal bars, or these thin metal brackets.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Transformer - Cross (Chugoku Variant)
metas.note: The transformers in Chugoku, which have a cross-shaped bar attached in the middle of the pole, mounted by a full triangle, will have a long horizontal or short vertical insulator(s) at the end.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Transformer - Cross (Hat Insulator)
metas.note: The transformers in Shikoku, which also have a cross-shaped bar attached in the middle of the pole, mounted by a half triangle, will have “hat shaped” short horizontal insulators at the end.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Transformer - Insulator Box
metas.note: These grey “insulator-esque” blocks, which wires are fed through, can be found in the regions of Chubu, Kansai, Chugoku, Shikoku, and very rarely in Hokkaido.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Transformer - Kyushu
metas.note: The transformers in Kyushu, which have a straight bar attached on the side of the pole with three insulators at the end, will have transformers mounted 180-degrees from one another.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Transformer - Lamp-Shaped Insulator
metas.note:
The transformers in Hokuriku, which are attached with thin metal bars, often have these small “lamp” shaped insulators. There will never be a bar present except for the attachment mentioned above.

NOTE: The prefecture of Niigata will have the Tohoku transformer design, as opposed to Hokuriku one.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Transformer - Metal Bracket
metas.note: The transformers in Chubu, which often have painted yellow numbers and black “tap” connectors, are either attached with large triangle and horizontal bars, or these thin metal brackets.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Transformer - Okinawa
metas.note: Transformers in Okinawa, which have a T-shaped bar attached on the side of the pole, will have transformers mounted on opposite sides of the pole.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Transformer - One on Square
metas.note:
In Tohoku, you may also find transformers mounted on the side of a square, with a straight bar mounted on the top of the square. Rarely, you may find a square without a bar.

NOTE: While Kansai may have a square attachment as well, the bar will be mounted on the bottom rather than the top.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Transformer - Plus-Shaped Bar
metas.note: The electrical poles in Hokkaido either have this plus-shaped bar attached to the side of the pole, or one transformer mounted on two bars.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Transformer - Red Number
metas.note: In Chugoku, a white sticker will often be stuck to the bottom of the transformer with red numbers. They may also be painted on the side.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Transformer - Round Plate / T-Bar
metas.note:
The transformers in Kanto, which can have three or two insulators, are often mounted on a wooden plate and two bars, or a round plate and a T-shaped bar.

NOTE: While the Hokkaido transformer may also be mounted on two bars, it will never have a wooden plate. Kanto ones can also be mounted without a wooden plate.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Transformer - Round Plate / Zigzag Bar
metas.note: The transformers in Tohoku, which often have additional square holding brackets and the logo of the Tohoku Electrical Company, are sometimes mounted on a round plate with a zigzag bar.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Transformer - Square / Bottom Bar
metas.note:
The transformers in Kansai have either a straight or zigzag bar mounted on the bottom of a square. The transformer(s) will be mounted on the sides of that same square.

While this is uncommon, the bar and transformer(s) may be mounted on a vertical bar, rather than a square.

NOTE: While Tohoku may have a square attachment as well, the bar will be mounted on the top rather than the bottom

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Transformer - Triangle
metas.note: The transformers in Chubu, which often have painted yellow numbers and black “tap” connectors, are either attached with large triangle and horizontal bars, or these thin metal brackets.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Transformer - Two Bars
metas.note: The electrical poles in Hokkaido either have this plus-shaped bar attached to the side of the pole, or one transformer mounted on two bars. The Kanto Transformer may also be mounted on two bars.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Transformer - Two on Square
metas.note: In Hokkaido, if there is more than one transformer, they will often be mounted on the sides of a square.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Transformer - White Sticker
metas.note: A white sticker will often be stuck to the bottom of the transformer with black numbers.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Transformer - Wooden Plate
metas.note:
The transformers in Kanto, which can have three or two insulators, are often mounted on a wooden plate and two bars, or a round plate and a T-shaped bar.

NOTE: While the Hokkaido transformer may also be mounted on two bars, it will never have a wooden plate. Kanto ones can also be mounted without a wooden plate.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Tuning Fork - Chubu
metas.note: This tuning fork pole top, with a short top bar and horizontal bar below, is found the majority of the time in the Chubu region.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Tuning Fork - Kansai
metas.note: This tuning fork pole top, with a thin wire and horizontal bar below, is common in the Kansai region.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Tuning Fork - Kanto
metas.note: This tuning fork pole top, with a long top bar that sticks out each end and horizontal bar(s) below, is found the majority of the time in the Kanto region.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Vertical Traffic Light
metas.note: Vertical traffic lights can be found in Hokkaido, and along the northwestern coast. The usual horizontal traffic lights can be found everywhere else.

metas.name: Japan - Infrastructure - Yellow Circle Sign
metas.note: These specific black signs with two yellow circles are found in Kagawa. Other variations can be seen, including them stacked on top of each other, or with an arrow attached above.

metas.name: Japan - Landscape - Mount Fuji
metas.note:
Mount Fuji is the tallest mountain in Japan, with a gradual incline and often snowy summit.

Depending on the elevation, it can be seen from far away. This can create some excellent region guesses, especially if you account for direction and distance.

metas.name: Japan - Landscape - Plains
metas.note:
Japan is notably a very mountainous country. However, there are some regions that are quite flat, being the Nobi and Kanto plains. While at times they can look very similar, determining that it is one or the other can be very helpful.

NOTE: While there are, of course, other flat areas in Japan, these two are the most recognizable.

metas.name: Japan - Language - Cyrillic
metas.note: Cyrillic can be found on signs in the cities of Wakkanai and Nemuro, in northern Hokkaido.

metas.name: Japan - Vegetation - Bamboo
metas.note: In general, bamboo grows more often in the south, and slowly decreases further north. Population size and areas where it grows can vary, so use this information primarily in helping assist your region guess.

metas.name: Japan - Vegetation - Chinese Silver Grass
metas.note:
Chinese Silver Grass, referred to as Kyushu grass, is indeed very abundant on the island of Kyushu. However, use this tip with caution, as they can be seen outside of this area.

NOTE: Another notable region they can be found in is the prefectures of Niigata, Yamagata and Akita. Though, combining the rather large quantity found on Kyushu, its normally distinct vegetation, along with other information, there often will be a clear distinction.

metas.name: Japan - Vegetation - Giant Butterbur
metas.note: Giant butterbur (commonly referred to as cabbage) is abundant in Hokkaido and some northern prefectures. Plants found south of Hokkaido often have smaller leaves. It is often found growing along the roadside.

metas.name: Japan - Vegetation - Japanese White Birch
metas.note:
Japanese White Birch grows dominantly in the Chubu and Hokkaido regions, and to a lesser extent in Tohoku. Small areas of white birch can be found throughout Japan, so use this information primarily to help assist your region guess.

NOTE: Japanese Beech is another species of tree found in Japan. They, however, have more grey and spotted bark, as opposed to the mostly white Japanese White Birch.

metas.name: Landscape - 35
metas.note: Road 35 is surrounded by hills and mountains, and the ground is mostly covered in green shrubs. Curved lamp posts are posted at regular intervals on the northeastern side of the road.

metas.name: Landscape - 45 south of Mudayy
metas.note: Most of Road 45 south of Mudayy is unpaved and goes generally north to south, through some very rough hilly terrain. The soil is light and very rocky. Beware that the southernmost stretch is paved.

metas.name: Landscape - Adam Ridge
metas.note: Just north of Adam, you’ll find a flat desert landscape with greyish soil and mountains in the distance, notably one long ridge to the south followed by two smaller and rounder hills to the east and southeast. Other mountains are also visible to the north and west.

metas.name: Landscape - Al Amarat
metas.note: If you are surrounded by mountains on all sides, and you are in a somewhat urban area, you are likely just southeast of Muscat, in Al Amarat.

metas.name: Landscape - Bidiyah Landscape - Dunes
metas.note: South of Bidiyah you can find a couple of dirt roads going through a slightly rolling landscape consisting of orange-pink sand and small yellow-ish shrubs. The roads mainly go between long and low sand dunes with a general south-south-west direction.

metas.name: Landscape - Bidiyah Landscape - Flat
metas.note: Sandy desert with light coloured green and yellow shrubs can be found in northeastern Oman, mainly south and west of Bidiyah.

metas.name: Landscape - Coastal 41
metas.note: Coastal Road 41 features one of the sandiest landscapes in Oman, with very light sand all around. The coast is sometimes visible in the distance.

metas.name: Landscape - Coastal 41 - Ridge
metas.note: Coastal Road 41 features one of the sandiest landscapes in Oman, with very light sand all around. The coast is sometimes visible in the distance. On the north-to-south stretch, you can see a distant ridge to the west.

metas.name: Landscape - Dry Mountains
metas.note: Northern Oman features a dry mountainous landscape similar to eastern UAE. The south coast of Oman also rarely features some similar mountains.

metas.name: Landscape - Masirah
metas.note: Masirah Island features a dry and slightly hilly landscape, typically with somewhat grey soil and with brown shrubs visible. The front camera on the island is slightly smudged.

metas.name: Landscape - Masirah - 51
metas.note: Masirah Island features a dry and slightly hilly landscape, typically with somewhat grey soil and with brown shrubs visible. Road 51, which circulates the island, usually only has a white centre road line, which can help in recognising it. The front camera on the island is slightly smudged.

metas.name: Landscape - Max South 45
metas.note: Most of Road 45 south of Mudayy is unpaved and goes generally north to south, through some very rough hilly terrain. The soil is light and very rocky. Beware that the southernmost stretch is paved.

metas.name: Landscape - Musandam
metas.note: Most of the coverage in the Musandam Governorate exclave is coastal, with rocky cliffs usually hugging the road. A majority, but not all, of this coverage will have the coast to the west, excluding any other roads in the country with a similar look.

metas.name: Landscape - Narrow 32
metas.note: Going further north, Road 32 travels through a hilly desert landscape, in a general northern direction.

metas.name: Landscape - Nizwa Mountains
metas.note: The mountains north of Nizwa have an amount of green bushes that are unusually large for the north. The mountains are very rocky and jagged, which differentiates them from the more rolling mountains in the south.

metas.name: Landscape - North of Al Awaya Road
metas.note: The road north of Al Awaya features a desert landscape with dark grey soil, which is not common in the south. The road itself still has the orange tint characteristic of southwest Oman.

metas.name: Landscape - North of Al Mazyunah Road
metas.note: The unpaved road north of Al Mazyunah, near the Yemen border, has a north-north-west bound angle, and the desert has sandy, red-tinted sand, which still has some shrubbery around. You can see some hills in the distance. The southwards driving direction and sunny weather can be used as confirmation.

metas.name: Landscape - Orange Sanddunes
metas.note:
A road going through large orange-pink sand dunes can be found north of Fasad.

NOTE: The same dunes can be seen in the distance close to the northern part of the Yemen border.

metas.name: Landscape - Orocue Road
metas.note: This road leading from the 65 to the town of Orocue is characterized by its unique angle and the orange/brown dirt.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Colombia by Timo

metas.name: Landscape - Rolling Hills
metas.note: Close to the southern coast, especially around Salalah, you will find a rolling hills landscape. The area commonly features rocky ground, bushes and small trees as well as some fairly green valleys.

metas.name: Landscape - Sadah Coastal Road
metas.note: Road 42/49 east of Salalah is a scenic coastal road that features a lot of light-coloured tall rocky cliffs. The coast is also often visible.

metas.name: Landscape - Salalah Plains
metas.note: Salalah is located on a flat coastal plain with rolling mountains surrounding it to the north.

metas.name: Landscape - Ubar Fields
metas.note: Around the town of Ubar, you can find patches of green agricultural land surrounded by desert.

metas.name: Landscape - Western 41
metas.note: The western stretch of Road 41 has wide shoulders similar to Road 31, however, the more northwest-bound angle along with the reddish soil should tell them apart.

metas.name: Landscape - Wide 32
metas.note: Crossing into the Ash Sharqiyah North Governorate, the shoulders become wide, like those on Road 31. However, unlike Road 31, the desert here is darker and has more shrubs and greenery. A long portion of the road also has overcast coverage. The lighter red section is no longer road 32 but still features the wide shoulders. The landscape further north also gets hillier and more vegetated.

metas.name: Malta - Infrastructure - Blue Signs
metas.note: These blue signs are unique to Valletta.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/malta for more clues.

metas.name: Malta - Infrastructure - Bus Route with 3
metas.note: Bus routes starting with 3 are only found on Gozo Island. These can be quite hard to see, meaning they are most useful in moving games.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/malta for more clues.

metas.name: Malta - Infrastructure - Guardrail
metas.note: Regular metal guardrails are rare on Gozo Island. And thus mainly found on the main island lol
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/malta for more clues.

metas.name: Malta - Infrastructure - Low Stone Barrier
metas.note: Regular metal guardrails are rare on Gozo Island. Low stone barriers are more common instead.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/malta for more clues.

metas.name: Malta - Trekker - Ship Trekker
metas.note: This trekker on a ship that is painted white and blue can be seen between the main island and Gozo Island.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/malta for more clues.

metas.name: Mexico - Agriculture - Blue Agave
metas.note:
Commonly known as the blue agave, A. tequilana is immediately recognisable by its blue, sharply protruding leaves. This is the agave from which tequila is extracted, and it mainly inhabits Jalisco, where it is almost always observed in magnificent fields which can even coalesce into vast shades of blue from a distance.

Similar, but different: A. anguistifolia.

While it is difficult to distinguish them, A. tequilana is noticeably bluer. One other difference is that A. angustifolia is more commonly spotted in isolated groupings than A. tequilana, but expansive fields still exist.

metas.name: Mexico - Agriculture - Campeche Fields
metas.note: These red agricultural fields surrounded by dense forests of tropical trees are most common in northern Campeche.

metas.name: Mexico - Agriculture - Citrus Tree Plantation
metas.note: The area around Poza Rica in Veracruz features a lot of citrus tree plantations. It is common to see large amounts of these trees grown right on top of the hills.

metas.name: Mexico - Agriculture - Oil Palm
metas.note: Oil palm plantations are most common in Chiapas, and occasionally on the outskirts of the state in Veracruz, Tabasco, and Campeche.

metas.name: Mexico - Agriculture - Prickly Pear Farm
metas.note: In the northeast most area of State of Mexico, around the town Nopaltepec, they often farm Opuntia in vast plains. Farms of prickly pear are otherwise most commonly found in north east Morelos, where they foreground striking, sculpturally eroded dry hills. These farms can be found randomly elsewhere in the country, but much less commonly; if there is a third most common location for them it would be Guanajuato.

metas.name: Mexico - Agriculture - Pulque Agave Field
metas.note: One will often notice scattered farms of A. salmiana, gatherings which stretch limitlessly in neat rows; these will almost always be found around the city of Pachuca in Hidalgo, and rarely more south-east.

metas.name: Mexico - Agriculture - Red Agricultural Fields
metas.note: Red agricultural fields are commonly seen in Zacatecas and occasionally southern Durango.

metas.name: Mexico - Agriculture - Sugarcane
metas.note: Sugarcane can be found all over the country, but by far most common in Veracruz.

metas.name: Mexico - Agriculture - Very Dark Fields
metas.note: Extremely dark fields are common in Guanajuato.

metas.name: Mexico - Architecture - Mud Brick
metas.note: Mud brick buildings are most abundant in Durango, especially full houses constructed with mud brick. However, they can essentially be found in almost all of the dry desert states.

metas.name: Mexico - Architecture - Northern Mexico Architecture
metas.note: Architecture in northern Mexico often features design elements from American style bungalows. Many houses are coloured with light or pastel colours, gated and commonly have front yards. Orange tiles inspired by Spanish colonial architecture are also typical.

metas.name: Mexico - Architecture - Red Brick
metas.note: Red brick buildings are mostly concentrated in the states west of Mexico City, specifically Jalisco, Michoacan, Guanajuato, and Aguascalientes.

metas.name: Mexico - Architecture - Thatched Roof
metas.note: Thatched roofs are most common in the Yucatan peninsula and eastern San Luis Potosi. They can also be found elsewhere, mainly in the southeast.

metas.name: Mexico - Architecture - White Concrete Blocks
metas.note: White concrete block buildings are highly concentrated in the states surrounding Mexico city, and are generally more common to the east. They can however still be found all over the country.

metas.name: Mexico - Car Meta - Cofre de Perote Truck
metas.note: This white truck with visible rearview mirrors can be seen in the Cofre de Perote national park.

metas.name: Mexico - Car Meta - La Malinche Car
metas.note: This Street View car with a yellow hood can be found by the La Malinche volcano in Tlaxcala.

metas.name: Mexico - Car Meta - La Seca Car
metas.note: This red Street View car with a black roof can be found in the town of La Seca in Sinaloa.

metas.name: Mexico - Infrastructure - Asymmetric & Double-Stacked Insulator
metas.note: Poles with an asymmetric crossbar and double-stacked insulators are exclusive to Mexico City, State of Mexico, Hidalgo, and Morelos.

metas.name: Mexico - Infrastructure - Black Tar
metas.note:
Black tar on both sides of the yellow centre line can be seen in Sinaloa, Durango, and Guerrero.

NOTE: This is most reliable when the tar is not faded.

metas.name: Mexico - Infrastructure - Blue Grain Pavement
metas.note:
Grainy pavement with a blue-ish grey tinge is a common sight for the states of Tamaulipas and Nuevo Leon.

NOTE: In Tamaulipas, larger roads very commonly feature dashed outer lines.

metas.name: Mexico - Infrastructure - Cancun Lamp
metas.note: This lamp with five circular bulbs that looks like a dice is found in Cancun.

metas.name: Mexico - Infrastructure - CDMX Taxi
metas.note: Taxis in and around Mexico City have a white lower half with a pink upper half.

metas.name: Mexico - Infrastructure - Chihuahua Cross
metas.note: A thick cross can be seen on the back of signs in Chihuahua.

metas.name: Mexico - Infrastructure - Chihuahua Pole Paint
metas.note: Poles in Chihuahua city occasionally have a strip of white pole paint with the street name written in black or blue text.

metas.name: Mexico - Infrastructure - Cobblestone
metas.note: This style of cobblestone pavement, unorganised with irregular tiles, can be found in most of the central states, but is by far most commonly found in the states of Nayarit, Jalisco, Colima, and Queretaro.

metas.name: Mexico - Infrastructure - Cuernavaca Lamp
metas.note: This lamp with a black rectangular head is found in Cuernavaca.

metas.name: Mexico - Infrastructure - Durango Pole
metas.note: Poles with a lowered crossbar and a single support beam that extend from one end of the crossbar to the pole itself can be found in Durango.

metas.name: Mexico - Infrastructure - Eurus Wind Farm
metas.note: The Eurus Wind Farm is located in southeast Oaxaca and is the largest wind farm in Mexico. Rows of wind turbines can be found along the 190 around Juchitán de Zaragoza.

metas.name: Mexico - Infrastructure - Green Bottom Pole
metas.note:
The bottom half of poles in Cuernavaca are often painted green.

NOTE: In Generation 4, the paint usually looks faded, some to the point where it is barely visible.

metas.name: Mexico - Infrastructure - Hanging Insulator (Concrete)
metas.note: These concrete poles with insulators suspended below the crossbars are unique to the Yucatan peninsula.

metas.name: Mexico - Infrastructure - Hanging Insulator (Wooden)
metas.note: The wooden variant of the hanging pole is found on the Baja California peninsula.

metas.name: Mexico - Infrastructure - Hexagonal Tiles
metas.note: This pavement consisting of hexagonal tiles is found in Puebla and Tlaxcala.

metas.name: Mexico - Infrastructure - Jalisco Bollard
metas.note: Jalisco bollards will sometimes have a crown and the text ‘Jalisco’ written on it. These are usually barely legible unless very close, however no other Mexican bollard will have writing on it.

metas.name: Mexico - Infrastructure - Light Rock Wall
metas.note: These walls made of light coloured rock are found in the Yucatan peninsula, but most common in Yucatan state.

metas.name: Mexico - Infrastructure - Matamoros Lamp
metas.note: This lamp with a rectangular head and a ring-shaped light bulb is found in Matamoros.

metas.name: Mexico - Infrastructure - Mesh Pole
metas.note: Poles with a mesh body are most commonly found in San Luis Potosi, Guanajuato, and Queretaro.

metas.name: Mexico - Infrastructure - Nayarit Bollard
metas.note: Bollards with a red band near the top are unique to Nayarit, apart from one exception being Federal Highway 190 on the Oaxaca-Chiapas border.

metas.name: Mexico - Infrastructure - Oaxaca Pavement
metas.note: This exact pavement design with three lines of cobblestone patterning is exclusive to Oaxaca.

metas.name: Mexico - Infrastructure - Santiago de Queretaro Lamp
metas.note: This lamp with black front and back edges and a white middle section is found in Santiago de Queretaro.

metas.name: Mexico - Infrastructure - Tree Fences
metas.note:
These fences made out of trees with red-coloured bark are commonly found in Veracruz.

NOTE: These tree fences can still be found in other coastal states and are best utilised when combined with other clues.

metas.name: Mexico - Infrastructure - White Acorn Insulator
metas.note: White insulators that are shaped like acorns can be found along the coastal states of Mexico, but are by far most common in Michoacan, Colima, and Veracruz.

metas.name: Mexico - Infrastructure - White Roadlines
metas.note: White middle roadlines are most commonly found in Tabasco.

metas.name: Mexico - Infrastructure - Wooden & Low Crossbar
metas.note: Wooden poles with a lowered crossbar are mostly found in Sinaloa and Sonora.

metas.name: Mexico - Infrastructure - Yellow Edge Road Divider
metas.note: This road divider with a yellow top and bottom edge is found all along the 95D from Mexico City to Acapulco.

metas.name: Mexico - Infrastructure - Yellow Lamp Post
metas.note:
Most lamp posts and lamp arms in Aguascalientes city are yellow.

NOTE: They are not exclusive and are only very common.

metas.name: Mexico - Infrastructure - Zig-Zag Lamp
metas.note: This lamp with a zig-zag bent pole arm is found in Hermosillo.

metas.name: Mexico - Landscape - Cerro del Bernal
metas.note: Cerro del Bernal is a distinct extinct volcano that is found in southern Tamaulipas. It can be found heading directly northwest of Tampico or west of Morón.

metas.name: Mexico - Landscape - Ciudad Juarez
metas.note: The outskirts of Ciudad Juárez features a lot of dirt roads with a distinct shade of orange soil and low shrubs.

metas.name: Mexico - Landscape - Ciudad Obregon
metas.note: The area around Ciudad Obregon is distinct due to the pinkish-tan soil and canals found around the city’s agricultural areas.

metas.name: Mexico - Landscape - Coastal Cactus
metas.note: If you see a cactus in a coastal area, you're probably in Oaxaca.

metas.name: Mexico - Landscape - Guaymas Cliffs
metas.note: The town of Guaymas has a lot of jagged cliffs and mountains that make the area very distinct. The soil is also distinctly pinkish and organ-pipe cacti can be seen scattered on the hills and next to the road.

metas.name: Mexico - Landscape - Maderas del Carmen
metas.note:
This tall, flat ridge, with very prominent ridgelines, belongs to the Maderas del Carmen Biosphere Reserve in Northern Coahuila near the US border.

NOTE: The only road the mountain range can be observed from is the Federal Highway 53 that leads to Boquillas del Carmen.

metas.name: Mexico - Landscape - MEX-40D
metas.note: The 40D that crosses the Sinaloa-Durango state line is recognizable by the stunning lush cliffs and mountains along the road. The highway commonly passes through tunnels and the road itself features double yellow middle roadlines.

metas.name: Mexico - Landscape - MEX-54
metas.note: The 54 is a divided highway that runs through northeastern Zacatecas which features yucca trees spammed on both sides of the road. Additionally, the streetview car is often exposed and appears almost white due to the sunlight.

metas.name: Mexico - Landscape - Mexicali Landscape
metas.note: The area around Mexicali features flat farmland with a ridge to the west. Washingtonia palms are very common and these poles made out of brown wood can be found.

metas.name: Mexico - Landscape - Monterrey Mountains
metas.note: The Monterrey metropolitan area features tall stunning mountain ranges that surround the city.

metas.name: Mexico - Landscape - Morelos Prickly Pear Farms
metas.note: Farms of prickly pear are commonly found in north east Morelos, where they foreground **striking, sculpturally eroded dry hills. **

metas.name: Mexico - Landscape - Northern Baja Landscape
metas.note: These reddish brown-tinged hills, often accompanied by large boulders, are a common sight for the northern half of Baja California.

metas.name: Mexico - Landscape - Pink Lakes
metas.note: The town of Los Coloradas is famously known for the pink lakes around the area.

metas.name: Mexico - Landscape - San Cristóbal Suchixtlahuaca
metas.note: The area around San Cristóbal Suchixtlahuaca and south of it in Oaxaca often feature rolling hills with really distinct orange and beige-tinged soil, passing from one colour to the other with each hill. The beige-tinged soil can be seen more prominent in some locations.

metas.name: Mexico - Landscape - Sierra del Abra Tanchipa
metas.note: This extremely long and flat ridge is found in the Sierra del Abra Tanchipa Biosphere Reserve in eastern San Luis Potosi.

metas.name: Mexico - Landscape - Twin Volcanoes
metas.note: The twin volcanoes of Iztaccíhuatl and Popocatépetl are found on the border between the State of Mexico and Puebla. Keep in mind that they are usually much less visible than depicted in the image, which is just for reference.

metas.name: Mexico - Landscape - Western Chi/Dur Landscape
metas.note: The western parts of Chihuahua and Durango can feature a rocky mountainous landscape covered with pine forests. In general, these pines are shorter and more stunted in appearance than pine forests of the central or south.

metas.name: Mexico - Landscape - White Soil
metas.note:
Almost blindingly white soil in the Yucatan peninsula is most common in Quintana Roo.

NOTE: This is only consistent in Generation 3.

metas.name: Mexico - Vegetation - Agave angustifolia
metas.note:
blue, but less blue than tequilana, smaller grouping

found in Central Oaxaca

metas.name: Mexico - Vegetation - Agave Asperrina
metas.note: The rough century plant looks similar to the pulque agave but its leaves are blueish and it is much smaller. It is distributed nearly identically to A. lechuguilla (Durango and Coahuila, especially around Saltillo and West of Torreon, rarely SLP and Hidalgo), and is often difficult to spot from the road, only barely visible in the distance in batches.

metas.name: Mexico - Vegetation - Agave Cupreata
metas.note: Agave cupreata is a very rarely observed agave that is localised to central Guerrero. Its name is apt - it has a much more pronounced, cup-like appearance than other agaves, with the leaves lurching inwards. It is often found growing on walls in groups as depicted.

metas.name: Mexico - Vegetation - Agave Karwinskii
metas.note: A. karwinskii is exclusively seen in the central desert region of Oaxaca, mostly near the town Miahuatlán de Porfirio Díaz, even though technically its native distribution extends elsewhere in the state and barely into Puebla. Its spiky thin leaves, protruding from the centre in a cylindrical formation, make it quite distinct from other common agaves.

metas.name: Mexico - Vegetation - Agave Lechuguilla
metas.note: Agave lechuguilla is a very frequent sighting in the hills of Durango and Coahuila, particularly around the cities of Saltillo and west of Torreon. More rarely it can be found in San Luis Potosi and Hidalgo. It is distinguished by its slick, lime-green leaves that almost look as if they are combed to one side.

metas.name: Mexico - Vegetation - Blue Myrtle Cactus
metas.note: Myrtillocactus Geometrizans is a species of cactus in the genus Myrtillocactus, native to central and northern Mexico. It is especially abundant in San Luis Potosi, but also common in Queretaro and Hidalgo, and much more rarely Guanajuato.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Plant World by Zen

metas.name: Mexico - Vegetation - Boojum Tree
metas.note: Boojum trees can be recognized by their alien, tentacle-like appearance. They are almost exclusively found in the southern half of Baja California.

metas.name: Mexico - Vegetation - Brittlebush
metas.note: Brittlebush are small shrubs with bright silver-grey leaves that are most commonly found in Sonora, especially around Hermosillo.

metas.name: Mexico - Vegetation - Candelabro
metas.note: Pachycereus weberi is widespread in the Mexican states of Puebla, Guerrero, Morelos, Hidalgo and Oaxaca at altitudes of 600 to 1,500 m.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Plant World by Zen

metas.name: Mexico - Vegetation - Cephalocereus Mezcalaensis
metas.note: This tall, columnar cactus, with no branches, is native to northern Oaxaca and southern Puebla, and another of the many species present there. Much less commonly but still possibly it can be seen in central Guerrero.

metas.name: Mexico - Vegetation - Chiotilla
metas.note: The species originates from Mexico (Guerrero, Michoacán, Oaxaca, southern Puebla). It will almost always place you somewhere in Oaxaca, usually central in the state.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Plant World by Zen & Source: Mexico Deconstructed by Addlama

metas.name: Mexico - Vegetation - Coconut Palm
metas.note: Coconut palms can be found all across the coast, but are often found in large groups in Guerrero and Colima.

metas.name: Mexico - Vegetation - Florida Thach palm
metas.note:
This palm is recognizable through its round fan leaves.

Within Mexico, it's usually found in Yucatan.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Plant World by Zen

metas.name: Mexico - Vegetation - Fruit Cholla
metas.note: The golden glow of the fruit cholla is also unmistakable, and present mostly in the Western Half of Sonora.

metas.name: Mexico - Vegetation - Giant Cardon
metas.note: Pachycereus pringlei is a species of large cactus native to northwestern Mexico, in the states of Baja California, Baja California Sur. It can rarely be found on the Sonoran coast, around the area south of Puerto Libertad on the 3.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Plant World by Zen & Source: Mexico Deconstructed by Addlama

metas.name: Mexico - Vegetation - Golden Line
metas.note: These gold tufts of grass in a line right next to the road are most commonly found in Coahuila.

metas.name: Mexico - Vegetation - Indian Comb
metas.note: The Indian Comb (Pachycereus pecten-aboriginum), is a common cactus that always implies Sinaloa, or south Sonora near Sinaloa, although technically its habitat extends elsewhere. Its densely packed branches emerge from a single stem, but most recognisable is its inflorescence - the brightly coloured flowers which usually adorn the tip of its arms.

metas.name: Mexico - Vegetation - Organ Pipe Cactus
metas.note: This species is found mostly in Mexico, mainly in Sonora and southern Baja California and Northern Sinaloa. If the cactus is significantly larger than 3m, it's probably in Southern Baja.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Plant World by Zen

metas.name: Mexico - Vegetation - Organ Pipe Spam
metas.note: A huge abundance of Organ Pipe Cacti it is usually indicative of the reserve El Cajón del Diablo, south of Hermosillo.

metas.name: Mexico - Vegetation - Pitaya de Querétaro
metas.note:
In Pitaya the branches less organically sprout from the ground in the weed-like manner of the Organ Pipe, and instead curl smoothly outwards from a central stem.

It is mostly found in Jalisco, south of Guadalajara. Less commonly, it's seen in Guanajuato. It can be seen in Queretaro too, but surprisingly rarely.

metas.name: Mexico - Vegetation - Prickly Pear alone
metas.note: Prickly pear cacti with a total absence of other cacti, yucca, agaves or in general succulent plants except for the prickly pear is generally a good signal for the centre-west (Jalisco, Guanajuato, Michoacan).

metas.name: Mexico - Vegetation - Prickly Pear Cactus
metas.note:
Prickly pear cacti are distinct with their flat oval-shaped pads. They are noticeably more common centrally and are rarely seen in southern and coastal states.

They are also good for some 50/50:

  • Durango > Chihuahua
  • Durango > Sonora (less reliable)
  • Nuevo Leon > Tamaulipas
  • Other States > Mexico State
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & Source: Mexico Deconstructed by Addlama

metas.name: Mexico - Vegetation - Pulque Agave
metas.note:
Agave salmiana, colloquially the pulque agave, is native to central Mexico. Agaves in general are distinguishable by their crown-like appearance, with stiff leaves which fan outwards symmetrically. The pulque agave is no different, but has green leaves, relatively smooth edges, and flat leaves that curl slightly away from the central axis.

Note its distribution, in an arc around Mexico City and a second pocket of endemism which straddles San Luis Potosi city and Aguascalientes.

metas.name: Mexico - Vegetation - Quintana Roo Tree
metas.note: These thin, white-barked trees can be found in the Yucatan peninsula, but are most prevalent in Quintana Roo.

metas.name: Mexico - Vegetation - Sabal Mexicana
metas.note:
This palm seems to be prominent in coastal Texas, the east and the south coast of Mexico, Yucatán peninsula, and Guatemala. The key difference between this one and the other Sabal palms is the shape and arrangement of the leaves.

Sabal Mexicana has large, stiff, pointy leaves and densely packed.

Sabal Yapa has droopy, hanging leaves that almost look shredded at the tips. Sabal Rosei tends to have visible gaps between the leaves, and they are a brighter green color.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Plant World by Zen

metas.name: Mexico - Vegetation - Sabal Rosei
metas.note:
Sabal Rosei is native to the Pacific coast of Mexico, from Sinaloa to Jalisco but mostly concentrated in the state of Nayarit. The key difference between this one and the other Sabal palms is the shape and arrangement of the leaves.

Sabal Rosei tends to have visible gaps between the leaves, and they are a brighter green color.

Sabal Yapa has droopy, hanging leaves that almost look shredded at the tips. Sabal Mexicana has large, stiff, pointy leaves and densely packed.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Plant World by Zen

metas.name: Mexico - Vegetation - Sabal Yapa
metas.note:
This palm grows pretty much exclusively in the Yucatán peninsula. The key difference between this one and the other Sabal palms is the shape and arrangement of the leaves.

Sabal Yapa has droopy, hanging leaves that almost look shredded at the tips.

Sabal Mexicana has large, stiff, pointy leaves and densely packed. Sabal Rosei tends to have visible gaps between the leaves, and they are a brighter green color.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Plant World by Zen

metas.name: Mexico - Vegetation - Saguaro
metas.note: The Saguaro is endemic to the Sonoran Desert and is found primarily in western Sonora in Mexico, and in western Arizona in the US. Elevation is a limiting factor to its environment, as the saguaro is sensitive to extended frost or cold temperatures.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Plant World by Zen

metas.name: Mexico - Vegetation - Stenocereus fricii
metas.note: A rare and tall cactus, the thin and twirling branches of S. fricii are unique to Michoacan, especially on the 37D, where it is abundantly spammed.

metas.name: Mexico - Vegetation - Tlaxcala Bois
metas.note: These clumps of grass in almost a teardrop shape are common in the region around Tlaxcala.

metas.name: Mexico - Vegetation - Tree Cholla
metas.note:
The tree cholla is a cactus, and its skeletal, discoloured arms spurting in every direction make it recognisable.

Mostly found in San Luis Potosi, Queretaro and Hidalgo, often in Coahuila and Durango and rarely in Zacatecas.

metas.name: Mexico - Vegetation - Tree Cholla Group
metas.note: If it is present in groups, Tree Cholla is usually a good indication of San Luis Potosi.

metas.name: Mexico - Vegetation - Tree Yucca
metas.note: It is native to central mexico, most commonly found in Zacatecas and San Luis Potosí although it can be seen anywhere from Nuevo León down to Puebla, in dry regions.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Plant World by Zen

metas.name: Mexico - Vegetation - Umbrella Palm
metas.note: The Attalea rostrata is a huge palm recognizable from its upright leaves, almost resembling an umbrella. It is mostly exclusive to Veracruz and Tabasco, and can be rarely found in Chiapas.

metas.name: Mexico - Vegetation - Unknown Cactus
metas.note: Oaxaca is very diverse in Cacti, so if you see a strange cactus, or one that isn't explained in this map, you can consider going Oaxaca.

metas.name: Norway - Architecture - Røros Architecture
metas.note: The old mining town of Røros can be recognised by the densely built traditional wooden architecture.

metas.name: Norway - Architecture - White House Village
metas.note: While completely white wooden houses can be found in the entire country, they're especially common on the southern coast, where you'll commonly see entire villages made up of them.

metas.name: Norway - Coverage Meta - Snow Road
metas.note: The road between Atna and Ringebu in Innlandet is completely covered in snow. You will find a winter wonderland with green rocks
metas.footer: Source: Unique Roads of the World by Figsy

metas.name: Norway - Coverage Meta - Thick Snow Road
metas.note: This road between Aadneram and Nomeland in Agder features a thick 1m high snow along the skinny road. You will not find trees along this road.
metas.footer: Source: Unique Roads of the World by Figsy

metas.name: Norway - Infrastructure - Bamboo Snow Pole
metas.note: Bamboo snowpoles are regional and can mostly be found in Innlandet, Akershus, Østfold, Buskerud and Vestfold but can also be found rarely in Trøndelag, Vestland, Agder, Telemark and Rogaland.

metas.name: Norway - Infrastructure - Bergen Hydrant
metas.note: You can find this specific design of green fire hydrants in Bergen.

metas.name: Norway - Infrastructure - Big Wooden Snowpole
metas.note: Big wooden sticks are found on roads that are covered with snow almost the entire year. So far, they've been spotted on the road that runs north of Hardangervidda National Park, on the road west of Jotunheimen and southwest of Valdres Natur-og kulturpark.

metas.name: Norway - Infrastructure - Black Snow Poles
metas.note: Black plastic snowpoles are more regional and will mostly be found in Trøndelag, Møre og Romsdal and Vestland, but can also be found in Nordland and more rarely in Innlandet, Buskerud, Rogaland and Telemark

metas.name: Norway - Infrastructure - Oslo Pole Plate
metas.note: Fairly large black or red pole plates can be found in Oslo.

metas.name: Norway - Infrastructure - Rusty Guardrail
metas.note: Rusty guardrails are almost exclusively found in coastal regions, and particularly on the southern half of the west coast.

metas.name: Norway - Infrastructure - Senja Snowpoles
metas.note: Green plastic snowpoles are found mostly around the island of Senja in Troms since the company selling these is also located there. The company also sells other colors less frequently. These can also less commonly be found all over Troms and Finnmark.

metas.name: Norway - Infrastructure - Small Blue Snowpole
metas.note: Small blue snowpoles can be found around Elverum.

metas.name: Norway - Infrastructure - Two Red Stripes
metas.note: Two red stripes going around lamp posts are commonly found in Stavanger.

metas.name: Norway - Infrastructure - Wide Black ID
metas.note: Small, wide black pole plates, with a single line of letters and digits, can be found in southeastern Norway.

metas.name: Norway - Landscape - 82 (Andoya)
metas.note: The 82 on the island of Andoya, which is part of the Lofoten archipelago, is flat apart from one tabletop looking hill. In generall, the hills on this road are quite unique and recognizable. You will find short scrubs along the road. Often, you will be able to see water.
metas.footer: Source: Unique Roads of the World by Figsy

metas.name: Norway - Landscape - Atlanterhavsveien
metas.note:
This road uses dark rocks as bridges. You will see water on both sides of the road. The coverage features dark clouds.

The road includes the famous Storseisundet bridge.
metas.footer: Source: Unique Roads of the World by Figsy

metas.name: Norway - Landscape - Deep Fjords
metas.note: While fjords can be found along most of the Norwegian coast, deep fjords surrounded by tall mountains are most common between Bergen and Trondheim.

metas.name: Norway - Landscape - E10 in Lofoten
metas.note: This road features huge mountains. It is a skinny road that has water to the east. Lots of sections have bridges or open tunnels. You will frequently find fireweed on the sides of the road. The vegetation on this road has a yellowish tone.
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/norway for more clues.

metas.name: Norway - Landscape - E10 on the border of Troms and Nordland
metas.note: This road runs through a valley. You can see a big mountain range along the road, with no trees on the mountain. Some sections are very green, and some section feature fireweed.
metas.footer: Source: Unique Roads of the World by Figsy

metas.name: Norway - Landscape - E10, East of Narvik
metas.note: This road is very green and usually features big mountains with no trees. Right on the Swedish border you will find parts without trees.
metas.footer: Source: Unique Roads of the World by Figsy

metas.name: Norway - Landscape - End of the World Road
