metas.note: This famous road can be identified by the lack of trees and the small white rocks. The visibility in the coverage is somewhat low. Some sections are very flat, while others can have small hills and lakes.
metas.footer: Source: Unique Roads of the World by Figsy

metas.name: Norway - Landscape - Exposed Rock
metas.note: Exposed rock, often spotted with small coastal pines and bushes, is mainly found on the south coast.

metas.name: Norway - Landscape - Highlands
metas.note: Barren highlands, with no trees or bushes, and often with rocky mountains along the road, are mostly found in the southwest.

metas.name: Norway - Landscape - Lofoten Mountains
metas.note: Distinct, sharp, rocky mountains with few trees can be seen on the Lofoten Archipelago.

metas.name: Norway - Landscape - Lysevegen
metas.note: Lysevegen is a very windy and skinny road with 28 180° turns down the mountain. Notably, there are big power lines visible. You can see huge mountains in the distance. The coverage is very cloudy.
metas.footer: Source: Unique Roads of the World by Figsy

metas.name: Norway - Landscape - Northeastern Landscape
metas.note: The northeast of Norway can typically be recognized by a somewhat rolling landscape, rather than tall mountains, and vegetation mainly consisting of very small birches combined with patched grass.

metas.name: Norway - Landscape - Northern Coastal Grasslands
metas.note: Coastal grasslands with little to no other vegetation and only somewhat low, distant mountains can be found by coastal roads in the far north.

metas.name: Norway - Landscape - Oslo Farmlands
metas.note: The largest concentration of farmland is found in the southeast, in the general vicinity of Oslo. The area is much flatter than most of the country, and it is common to get a rolling landscape with smooth, round forested hills in the distance. The area southeast of Oslo is particularly flat.

metas.name: Norway - Landscape - Røst Island
metas.note: This island has only Gen 2 coverage. You will see lots of boats everywhere. The landscape is flat and islandish (duh).
metas.footer: Source: Unique Roads of the World by Figsy

metas.name: Norway - Landscape - Russian Border Road
metas.note: Along the Russian border you can see this noticeably humid and green-looking road, with very overcast and occasionally foggy coverage. The trees are somewhat low and mainly consist of thin birches and pines.

metas.name: Norway - Landscape - Stavanger Farmlands
metas.note: The farmland south of Stavanger is flatter than most of the country. The fields look vast and open, and it is very common to see rock walls made of large, round rocks. Furthermore, rather than crops, most fields will only contain grass.

metas.name: Norway - Landscape - Trollstigen
metas.note: Trollstigen leads down a huge mountain, and is surrounded by such. The road is very steep and windy. The rock is very dark and has green moss on it. Some sections are cut into the rock, with waterfalls appearing.
metas.footer: Source: Unique Roads of the World by Figsy

metas.name: Norway - Landscape - Trondheim Farmlands
metas.note: The farmlands surrounding Trondheim are generally very hilly, and the hills are typically both steeper and more uneven than in the southeast.

metas.name: Norway - Language - Russian language
metas.note: Russian can sometimes be seen alongside Norwegian on signs near the Russian border. It is mostly found on roads E6 and E105 near Kirkenes.

metas.name: Norway - Language - Sámi Signs
metas.note: Bilingual signs with Sámi can be found in several northern areas in Norway. While the Sámi languages are very different from Norwegian, the best way to recognize them are the letters Á, Đ and the use of several vowels in a row, something which is uncommon in Norwegian. Note that not all signs in these areas will be bilingual.

metas.name: Norway - Vegetation - Bracken
metas.note: This species of fern (Pteridium aquilinum, also known as bracken) which typically has a fairly tall stem and many wide leafs branching out, is mostly found in the south of Norway. Beware that other species of ferns can be found further north.

metas.name: Norway - Vegetation - Bright Moss
metas.note: Brightly colored moss is common to find in the area between Lillehammer and Oppdal

metas.name: Norway - Vegetation - Maple
metas.note: Maples are mainly found in the south, particularly by the farmlands around Oslo.

metas.name: Norway - Vegetation - Oaks
metas.note: Oaks are mainly found in the far south of Norway.

metas.name: Norway - Vegetation - Pine
metas.note: Pines are most common in coastal and far inland areas in the southern half of the country.

metas.name: Norway - Vegetation - Spruce
metas.note: Spruces are mainly found in the southern half of the country, particularly in the southeast and around Trondheim.

metas.name: Peru - Agriculture - Banana Plants
metas.note: Similarly to sugar cane plants, banana plants are generally found in agricultural regions adjacent to the coast in the northern half of the country.

metas.name: Peru - Agriculture - Olive Trees
metas.note: Olive tree plantations can be found in the far southern region of Tacna.

metas.name: Peru - Agriculture - Sugarcane
metas.note: Most of the sugar cane production is found in the northern coastal regions of Peru near the cities of Chiclayo and Trujillo. Typically you see large fields of sugar cane in these areas. Smaller areas of sugar cane can be found further south in other valleys close to the Pacific coast.

metas.name: Peru - Architecture - Overhanging Roof
metas.note: Buildings with overhanging roofs with wooden supports are mostly found in northern regions of Peru. These buildings are sometimes brightly coloured as well.

metas.name: Peru - Architecture - Titicaca Architecture
metas.note:
As a general rule, the closer you are to Lake Titicaca in Peru, houses and buildings made out of red brick become more common. This type of architecture resembles the predominant type of building seen in parts of western Bolivia, which is helpful for remembering where it is seen most commonly. Additionally, buildings with blue tinted glass can be seen most commonly in the same areas.

NOTE: Red brick buildings can be seen anywhere in the country, so use other clues before guessing.

metas.name: Peru - Car Meta - White Truck
metas.note: Within Peru, this white Street View car is found in central Cusco. It drives from the remote town of Aguas Calientes up to Machu Picchu.

metas.name: Peru - Infrastructure - Boulevard Street
metas.note: Most of the boulevard-type streets in Peru are in the city of Lima. These boulevards are typically long, straight streets divided by concrete or a grassy berm.

metas.name: Peru - Infrastructure - Cigarette Bollard
metas.note: This bollard, with a black and yellow stripe at the top, is unique to the state of Moquegua, which is located in the south of Peru.

metas.name: Peru - Infrastructure - Divided Highway
metas.note:
Highway 1N/S is divided in the highlighted area on the map.

NOTE: It is the only divided highway outside of cities.

metas.name: Peru - Infrastructure - Northern Tuk Tuks
metas.note:
Tuk-Tuks with open front compartments are primarily found in the northern half of Peru, and are especially common in northern Amazonian adjacent regions.

NOTE: This type of Tuk-Tuk can be found elsewhere to a lesser extent, so use other clues before guessing.

metas.name: Peru - Infrastructure - Pucallpa
metas.note:
The east-central Amazonian city of Pucallpa, which lies close to the Brazil border, has a consistent street grid of WSW to ENE.

NOTE: Some northern and eastern areas of the city feature grids of different orientation.

metas.name: Peru - Landscape - 1N (Piura - Lambayeque)
metas.note: The 1N near the Piura and Lambayeque border has a distinct looking landscape. It features a semidesert landscape and has overcast coverage in Generation 3. The new Generation 4 is drier but still looks somewhat similar.

metas.name: Peru - Landscape - 1S (Coastal)
metas.note: The 1S south of the city of Ica is not divided and mostly follows the coast. The soil is often red or orange in these areas, and there is little-to-no vegetation. This road is also entirely covered with the Generation 4 camera.

metas.name: Peru - Landscape - 28B
metas.note: Ruta 28B between the towns of Kimbiri and Echarate is a paved road with very faded or missing road lines. It is also characterised by being a relatively small road with Generation 4 coverage, which hugs the hillside and is located next to a river valley.

metas.name: Peru - Landscape - 30C
metas.note: Ruta 30C in eastern Peru uses a white Street View car in Generation 3 between the cities of Planchon and Iñapari. It features dense forest, few villages, and resembles interior areas of Brazil. Some of this area has been overwritten with Generation 4. Most of this segment runs north to south.

metas.name: Peru - Landscape - 5N (San Alejandro - Esperanza)
metas.note: Ruta 5N between the towns of San Alejandro and Esperanza is a relatively straight, flat road in good condition. This road primarily runs north-south through the rainforest.

metas.name: Peru - Landscape - Atacama Desert
metas.note: Areas near the cities of Ica, Arequipa, and Tacna feature barren and mostly flat desert landscapes that can resemble areas of northern Chile. You can typically see mountains in the distance, primarily while looking to the east.

metas.name: Peru - Landscape - Cusco
metas.note: The southern city of Cusco is recognizable by its prevalence of both red brick and Spanish colonial style buildings. Cusco is surrounded by mountains on all sides and features an airport in the middle of the city. Due to its proximity and similar architecture, Cusco superficially resembles the Bolivian city of La Paz.

metas.name: Peru - Landscape - Exposed Rock Outcroppings
metas.note:
In higher elevation areas near the centre of the country, exposed rocky outcroppings are commonly seen in the sides of hills and mountains. Some areas with the highest concentrations are near Lago Chinchaycocha (Junin District) stretching south towards the city of Ayacucho.

NOTE: Exposed rocks can rarely be seen anywhere in the country, so use this meta with some caution.

metas.name: Peru - Landscape - Flat Landscape between Mountains
metas.note:
A flat landscape in the mountains of Peru is usually seen in central Puno and around Lake Chinchaycocha.

NOTE: This landscape might look similar to Bolivia. Make sure to look out for other clues before guessing.

metas.name: Peru - Landscape - Iquitos
metas.note: Iquitos is a city in northeast Peru. It is an isolated city with only Generation 3 Street View coverage. Three-wheeled tuk-tuks, overcast skies, and rolling Amazonian landscapes are commonly seen in the area. This coverage is isolated from other areas of northern Peru.

metas.name: Peru - Landscape - Iquitos Road
metas.note: The road to Iquitos can be recognized by black car Gen 3, lack of center lines and rolling Amazonian landscape
metas.footer: Check out www.plonkit.net/peru for more clues.

metas.name: Peru - Landscape - Jauja Valley
metas.note: The valley connecting the cities of Jauja and Huancayo features a flat plain with plentiful trees, agricultural areas, and small villages. North-south oriented mountains can be seen on both edges of the valley.

metas.name: Peru - Landscape - Lake Chinchaycocha
metas.note: North of the city of Huancayo lies a shallow lake called Lake Chinchaycocha (also referred to as ‘the middle lake.’). This lake is generally marshy and a range of mountains can be seen to the east of the lake. This lake can look similar to Lake Titicaca, but is generally less densely populated and features fewer trees.

metas.name: Peru - Landscape - Lichen
metas.note: Patches of light green lichen can be seen covering rocks and growing on the ground in high elevation areas of central and southern Peru.

metas.name: Peru - Landscape - North of Titicaca Wetness
metas.note: The coverage on the north side of Lake Titicaca was taken during a significantly wetter season than the coverage taken on the south side of Lake Titicaca.

metas.name: Peru - Landscape - Northern Amazonian Landscape
metas.note: The areas adjacent to the northern Amazonian city of Tarapoto feature moderately tall foliage-covered mountains and can bear a similar resemblance to the hilly areas of Colombia or Brazil.

metas.name: Peru - Landscape - Northwestern Piura Landscape
metas.note: The landscape northwest of the city of Piura is generally dry, featuring a low amount of vegetation with a few shrubs and bushes. The landscape is hilly, which distinguishes it from other Piura regions.

metas.name: Peru - Landscape - Red Soil
metas.note: Dark red-tinted soil is found in several areas of Peru. Some notable areas include the areas near Cusco and Ayacucho in the south of the country, as well as areas near the northern cities of Cajamarca and Tarapoto. It can be found to a lesser extent in adjacent regions.

metas.name: Peru - Landscape - Sandwiched Agriculture
metas.note:
Coastal agricultural valleys in the middle and south are commonly sandwiched between dry mountains with no vegetation. The general orientation of these valleys are southwest-northeast.

NOTE: Agricultural valleys in the north of Peru can look similar, but often feature more shrubs and trees on the mountains.

metas.name: Peru - Landscape - Sharp Mountains
metas.note: Similarly, taller mountains near the middle of the country often feature rocky and sharp mountain tops. The main region of these mountains stretches from near the city of Huaraz southward to the city of Cusco; generally away from the coast.

metas.name: Peru - Landscape - Shrubby Mountains
metas.note: Far north Peru features mountains that are often covered in shrubby trees and bushes. Closer to the coast and the Ecuador border, these mountains are often quite dry in appearance.

metas.name: Peru - Landscape - Southwestern Piura Landscape
metas.note: The southwestern landscape of Piura is generally dry, featuring a low amount of vegetation with a few shrubs and bushes. The landscape is mostly flat, but you will sometimes see rolling hills.

metas.name: Peru - Landscape - Tacna Ridge
metas.note: The city of Tacna in the far south of Peru has this distinct dry ridge to the north.

metas.name: Peru - Landscape - Titicaca Villages
metas.note: Low grass, a few hills, stone walls in villages and brown brick buildings are typical for the region south of Lake Titicaca in eastern Peru.

metas.name: Peru - Landscape - Tumbes Landscape
metas.note:
These three landscapes are typically found along offroads in Tumbes. You will always see sandy soil with either green or withered bushes.

NOTE: In addition, Tumbes does not have black cars on off roads. Make sure to consider it whenever you see such landscapes with a white Street View car.

metas.name: Peru - Landscape - Volcanoes
metas.note:
Volcanoes are often seen in and around the city of Arequipa.

NOTE: Within Peru, volcanoes are only found in the southeast in the highlighted area.

metas.name: Peru - Trekker - Train Trekker
metas.note: A train track covered by a trekker is located between Aguas Calientes and Cusco.

metas.name: Peru - Vegetation - Palm Trees
metas.note: Coconut palms (and other species of tall palms) can sometimes be seen in coastal areas of Peru, mainly north of Lima. They are mainly found in the agricultural areas which are typically found around the major coastal cities.

metas.name: Peru - Vegetation - Pine Plantations
metas.note: Pine plantations are typically found in higher elevation areas of the country, away from the coastal deserts and Amazonian Regions. The most common types of pine trees planted are Pinus radiata and Pinus patula.

metas.name: Philippines - Agriculture - Banana Plantations
metas.note:
Banana plantations are almost exclusively found in central and southern Mindanao.

NOTE: Wild growing banana plants can be found all over the country, so make sure what you are seeing is an actual plantation before guessing.

metas.name: Philippines - Agriculture - Corn
metas.note: While corn can be found in most of the country, it is most common on northern Luzon and on Mindanao.

metas.name: Philippines - Agriculture - Oil
metas.note: The vast majority of Oil palm plantations are found on Mindanao.

metas.name: Philippines - Agriculture - Pineapple
metas.note: Pineapple plantations are mostly found on Mindanao.

metas.name: Philippines - Agriculture - Sugarcane
metas.note: The majority of sugarcane in the Philippines can be found on the islands of Negros and Panay.

metas.name: Philippines - Architecture - Diagonal Amakan
metas.note: Houses built with amakan walls (referred to as Sawali in the north) with a diagonally woven pattern are mostly found on the island of Palawan, but can also be found throughout the northern half of the country.

metas.name: Philippines - Architecture - Diamond Amakan
metas.note: Houses built with amakan walls, a traditionally woven bamboo mat, with a diamond pattern are almost exclusively found in the southern half of the country.

metas.name: Philippines - Architecture - Marawi
metas.note: In and around the city of Marawi, Mindanao you can find many destroyed houses and ruins from the Marawi siege in 2017.

metas.name: Philippines - Car Meta - General Santos Car
metas.note: You may find this black Street View car with a visible roof rack in and around the city of General Santos.

metas.name: Philippines - Car Meta - Mayon Vehicle
metas.note: This vehicle with several thick black bars can be found just south of the Mayon Volcano.

metas.name: Philippines - Car Meta - Orange Car
metas.note: An orange Street View car with visible side mirrors can be found on Corregidor Island.

metas.name: Philippines - Car Meta - Taped Car back
metas.note: In northwestern Bohol you can find this Street View car with tape on the back.

metas.name: Philippines - Culture -  Mountain Dew Decorations
metas.note: Decorations made of neon-green Mountain Dew bottles are commonly found in the north, particularly on northern Luzon.

metas.name: Philippines - Culture - Islam
metas.note: While most of the Philippines is strongly christian, a region of western Mindanao is majority muslim.

metas.name: Philippines - Culture - Roman Soldiers
metas.note: Images and statues of ancient Roman soldiers can be found on the island of Marinduque.

metas.name: Philippines - Infrastructure - Acne Blocks
metas.note: The southern peninsula of Quezon has these sloped concrete blocks with round spots made from small rocks that kind of look like a skin issue. Blocks in this style with straight edges are common throughout the country, and you can get slanted concrete blocks without the acne in other places as well, but the combination is exclusive to this area.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Philippines by Oliver, who is quoting sleepfor8hx3 on a document that unfortunately is not available at this point in time (2025/04/08)

metas.name: Philippines - Infrastructure - Bataan Death March
metas.note:
These large decorated white waystones, commemorating the Bataan Death March, can be seen along roads going from Mariveles and Bagac in the south to San Fernando in the north.

NOTE: The Bataan Death March continued from San Fernando to Capas by train, where a larger memorial has been built.

metas.name: Philippines - Infrastructure - Bicol Stripes
metas.note: White guardrails with three recurring black stripes are unique to the region of Bicol in southern Luzon.

metas.name: Philippines - Infrastructure - Black & Yellow Guardrail
metas.note: In the Cordillera Administrative Region you can find yellow and black striped concrete guardrails.

metas.name: Philippines - Infrastructure - Double Pancake Insulator
metas.note: Double pancake insulators are very rare, but most likely to be found along the coast of East Samar, from about the height of the island of Hilabaan all the way down to the southern tip.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Philippines by Oliver & Philippines Poles by vaivod & brikiiee

metas.name: Philippines - Infrastructure - Indented Pole
metas.note: Square concrete poles with an indent on both side, similar to the poles found in Chile, are mainly found north of Manila and in and around the city of Bacolod on the island of Negros.

metas.name: Philippines - Infrastructure - K-Waystone
metas.note:
These waystones with K and a number below show the distance related to Manila (or the max distances on specific islands)

This number can be used to narrow down guesses.

For example, certain islands cannot exceed the orange numbers on the image. As another example, Mindanao, and nowhere else, always has numbers above 1000.
metas.footer: Source: philippines km=0 marker by bullfrogggy

metas.name: Philippines - Infrastructure - Ladder Poletop
metas.note:
A poletop made up of two tall vertical metal bars having an L-shaped cross-section which are connected via several thin wires, making it resemble a ladder, is unique to Manila and the surrounding area.

NOTE: You may sometimes come across similar looking poletops, with square bars instead of L-shaped ones, throughout the entire country. They will however almost never have more than two connecting wires.

metas.name: Philippines - Infrastructure - Northern Cebu Yellow Blocks
metas.note: In northern Cebu, you will find gray concrete guard blocks with their edges painted yellow.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Philippines by Oliver, who is quoting sleepfor8hx3 on a document that unfortunately is not available at this point in time (2025/04/08)

metas.name: Philippines - Infrastructure - Northwest-Leyte & Biliran Insulator
metas.note: Three ridges plus a long extender at the top to carry the wire are most commonly found in Leyte and Biliran.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Philippines by Oliver & Philippines Poles by vaivod & brikiiee

metas.name: Philippines - Infrastructure - Palawan Highway
metas.note:
The highway going south from Puerto Princesa on Palawan can be characterised by being very wide, often featuring six lanes, while simultaneously having very little traffic.

Along the road you will usually see this double electrical wire, which can help confirm your guess.

metas.name: Philippines - Infrastructure - Quad Insulator
metas.note: This cylinder with four distinct ridges is most common in Ilocos Norte, but can also be found in Biliran.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Philippines by Oliver & Philippines Poles by vaivod & brikiiee

metas.name: Philippines - Infrastructure - Quad Pancake Insulator
metas.note: If you see a quadruple pancake insulator on a pole top, you're going to be on the one road with coverage in Davao Occidental, along the coast, between approximately Don Marcelino and Bukid.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Philippines by Oliver & Philippines Poles by vaivod & brikiiee

metas.name: Philippines - Infrastructure - Sausage Insulator
metas.note: This grey insulator with lots of small ridges that looks kind of solid is most common in and around Manila, but can rarely be found elsewhere.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Philippines by Oliver & Philippines Poles by vaivod & brikiiee

metas.name: Philippines - Infrastructure - Siquijor Lamp
metas.note: Lamp posts on Siquijor are typically painted yellow, with black stripes at the bottom.

metas.name: Philippines - Infrastructure - Square Metal Mesh Poles
metas.note:
Square metal mesh poles are found on Mindanao, mainly on the Zamboanga peninsula.

NOTE: Most of the poles found outside of the Zamboanga peninsula are found along highways and have poletops with three hanging insulators.

metas.name: Philippines - Infrastructure - Star Wars Insulator
metas.note: This type of insulator that looks like the buildings on Tatooine is most common in northern Luzon and in and around Manila.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Philippines by Oliver & Philippines Poles by vaivod & brikiiee

metas.name: Philippines - Infrastructure - Trike - Dipolog City
metas.note:
The Zamboanga Peninsula trike is recognizable through the passenger window shape (airplane window). Other notables parts are the roof leaning back, and the trike kinda bulging out from under the window. Some cities have specific variants of this Trike:

Dipolog City likes to have the tiniest window imaginable over the driver’s side of the car & a big number on the roof.
metas.footer: Source: A Comprehensive Guide to Filipino Trikes by vaivod

metas.name: Philippines - Infrastructure - Trike - Isulan
metas.note: These trikes with the large flat black roof, the small side window and no lines in the main window are found in Sultan Kudarat mainly. These green trikes with blue POBLACION text on them are specific to Isulan.
metas.footer: Source: A Comprehensive Guide to Filipino Trikes by vaivod

metas.name: Philippines - Infrastructure - Trike - Ozamiz City
metas.note:
The Zamboanga Peninsula trike is recognizable through the passenger window shape (airplane window). Other notables parts are the roof leaning back, and the trike kinda bulging out from under the window. Some cities have specific variants of this Trike:

One city-specific variant to note is this one, with these bubbly numbers on top of the driver’s window (the trike itself can be any color scheme), which are exclusive to Ozamiz City and surrounding areas.
metas.footer: Source: A Comprehensive Guide to Filipino Trikes by vaivod

metas.name: Philippines - Infrastructure - Trike - Square Roof
metas.note: These trikes with a square roof are also very common within Maguindanao.
metas.footer: Source: A Comprehensive Guide to Filipino Trikes by vaivod

metas.name: Philippines - Infrastructure - Trike - Sultan Kudarat
metas.note: These trikes with the large flat black roof, the small side window and no lines in the main window are found in Sultan Kudarat mainly.
metas.footer: Source: A Comprehensive Guide to Filipino Trikes by vaivod

metas.name: Philippines - Infrastructure - Trike - Tacurong City
metas.note: These trikes with the large flat black roof, the small side window and no lines in the main window are found in Sultan Kudarat mainly. This more colorful variant with a number on top is specific to Tacurong City.
metas.footer: Source: A Comprehensive Guide to Filipino Trikes by vaivod

metas.name: Philippines - Infrastructure - Trike - Umbrella
metas.note:
These trikes with an umbrella are super common in Maguindanao, Misamis Occidental, and Lanao del Sur. Note that these are really the only trikes found in Cotabato city, so if there’s only these guys it’s a good clue for there.

NOTE: These are also very common in Cebu!
metas.footer: Source: A Comprehensive Guide to Filipino Trikes by vaivod

metas.name: Philippines - Infrastructure - Trike - Zamboanga City
metas.note:
The Zamboanga Peninsula trike is recognizable through the passenger window shape (airplane window). Other notables parts are the roof leaning back, and the trike kinda bulging out from under the window. Some cities have specific variants of this Trike:

This trike is a Zamboanga city trike- they have a flat roof, a white line separating the passenger and the driver’s side. There’s a little bumper thing jutting out from under the window, and there’s still the vertical bit underneath the passenger’s window. Zamboanga city specifically has these super colorful trikes.

This type of trike is still identifiable from the back due to the black cloth roof, the large window with the singular white line, and the back having a side window. These less colorful variants can be found Northeast of the main city.
metas.footer: Source: A Comprehensive Guide to Filipino Trikes by vaivod

metas.name: Philippines - Infrastructure - Trike - Zamboanga City (non-colorful variant)
metas.note:
The Zamboanga Peninsula trike is recognizable through the passenger window shape (airplane window). Other notables parts are the roof leaning back, and the trike kinda bulging out from under the window. Some cities have specific variants of this Trike:

This trike is a Zamboanga city trike- they have a flat roof, a white line separating the passenger and the driver’s side. There’s a little bumper thing jutting out from under the window, and there’s still the vertical bit underneath the passenger’s window. Zamboanga city specifically has these super colorful trikes.

This type of trike is still identifiable from the back due to the black cloth roof, the large window with the singular white line, and the back having a side window. These less colorful variants can be found Northeast of the main city.
metas.footer: Source: A Comprehensive Guide to Filipino Trikes by vaivod

metas.name: Philippines - Infrastructure - Trike - Zamboanga Peninsula
metas.note:
This trike shape is essentially the only variant seen on the entire Zamboanga Peninsula. What sticks out to me is the passenger window shape- it’s kind of like an airplane window. Other notable parts are the roof leaning back, and the trike kinda bulging out from under the window.

It’s identifiable from the back as well from the singular window in the back, as well as the roof tilting, and the random bars on top.

A common variant is this one with a large window hanging over the driver’s side. You can tell it’s the same type of trike from the same shape of the passenger car- where it has the airplane window (even if it’s horizontal) and then the bit beneath it that’s completely vertical and flat, along with the roof tilting back.
metas.footer: Source: A Comprehensive Guide to Filipino Trikes by vaivod

metas.name: Philippines - Infrastructure - Yellow Backboards
metas.note: On the islands of Panay and Guimaras (the little island next to Iloilo), electricity counters are frequently mounted on yellow backboards. These can be horizontal or vertical, metal or wood.
metas.footer: Source: A Learnable Philippines by Oliver, who is quoting sleepfor8hx3 on a document that unfortunately is not available at this point in time (2025/04/08)

metas.name: Philippines - Landscape - Arayat Volcano
metas.note: The Arayat Volcano can be recognised by being completely surrounded by flat agricultural fields.

metas.name: Philippines - Landscape - Chocolate Hills
metas.note: On central Bohol you can find these distinct round grassy hills. The hills generally have dark brown soil beneath the grass, earning them the name of Chocolate Hills.

metas.name: Philippines - Landscape - Mayon Volcano
metas.note: The Mayon Volcano is one of the tallest mountains in the Philippines and can be recognised by its almost perfect smooth cone shape. Beware that it will very often be covered in clouds.

metas.name: Philippines - Landscape - Northern Luzon Landscape
metas.note: The forested mountain range in Northern Luzon is characterised by somewhat dry mountainsides and an abundance of pine trees. You may rarely come across a similar landscape on high-altitude roads in Mindanao.

metas.name: Philippines - Vegetation - Moluccan Albizia
metas.note: Moluccan albizia are trees with light coloured trunks and pinnate leaves near the top of the tree. They are mainly found on Mindanao and are especially common in the eastern and central regions of the island.

metas.name: Philippines - Vehicle - Crown Roof Tuk-Tuk
metas.note: Tuk-Tuks with a crown roof can be found mostly in Northern Luzon. The crown consists of two separate parts, a "rectangular" part and a "crown-shaped" part. Some Tuk-Tuks elsewhere will have a wavy top, but are not made of two parts and thus are not crowns.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & A Learnable Philippines by Oliver

metas.name: Philippines - Vehicle - Flat Roof Tuk-Tuk
metas.note: Flat roofs are mostly found in the south. If it's a three-wheeler (as seen on the leftmost), you're probably on Mindanao.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & A Learnable Philippines by Oliver

metas.name: Philippines - Vehicle - Kuliglig
metas.note: This type of tractor, called a kuliglig, is mostly found on the plains around Cauayan on northern Luzon.

metas.name: Philippines - Vehicle - Low Roof Tuk-Tuk
metas.note: Low roof Tuk-Tuks are generally found in the North.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & A Learnable Philippines by Oliver

metas.name: Philippines - Vehicle - Motorcycle Plate Meta
metas.note:
If a Motorcycle plate has a colorful stripe on it, you can use it to determine the region you're in.

In general, if the stripe is on the top, you're in the Northern half.

If it's on the bottom, you're in the Southern half
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & A Learnable Philippines by Oliver

metas.name: Philippines - Vehicle - Palawan Tuk Tuk
metas.note: This Tuk-Tuk with a single front window and flat roof is exclusive to Palawan.
metas.footer: Source: PlonkIt & A Learnable Philippines by Oliver

metas.name: South Africa - Agriculture - Pine Plantation
metas.note:
Tree plantations that consist mostly of pine are common to the west of Eswatini, and some to the south in KwaZulu-Natal.

NOTE: Pine tree plantations are typically seen within the country of Eswatini itself.

metas.name: South Africa - Agriculture - Sugarcane
metas.note: Sugarcane plantations are most commonly seen in KwaZulu-Natal, mostly along the coast. However, they can also be seen in Mpumalanga on the Mozambique border. For an overview, see this map.

metas.name: South Africa - Agriculture - Vineyards
metas.note: Vineyards are almost exclusively found in Western Cape, mostly in valleys near the coast. You can also commonly find them near Upington, in Northern Cape.

metas.name: South Africa - Car Meta - Kruger National Park Car
metas.note:
A camouflage car with black side mirrors and roof racks can be seen in Kruger National Park, on the Mozambique border.

NOTE: The Park now also has generation 4 coverage.

metas.name: South Africa - Infrastructure - <-Pole
metas.note: Poles with 2 diagonal bars forming a ‘<’ shape can be found mostly in the northeastern provinces, most commonly in Limpopo and North West.

metas.name: South Africa - Infrastructure - A-Poletop (narrow)
metas.note: Poles with 3 bars forming the letter ‘A’, with the bottom insulators being attached at the edges of a horizontal bar, can be found almost exclusively in Western Cape, and rarely in bordering provinces.

metas.name: South Africa - Infrastructure - A-Poletop (wide)
metas.note: Poles with 3 bars forming the letter ‘A’, with the bottom insulators being attached directly to the 'A' rather than a horizontal bar, can be found in Eastern Cape.

metas.name: South Africa - Infrastructure - Alternating Insulators
metas.note: Poles with 3 alternating insulators sticking out horizontally at the top are mostly seen in the four northern provinces of Limpopo, Gauteng, North West and Mpumalanga. They can also sometimes be found in Northern Cape. In the rest of the country, these pole tops are exceedingly rare.

metas.name: South Africa - Infrastructure - Bird Nest
metas.note: Big bird nests on top of poles are commonly seen in the northern part of the Northern Cape Province.

metas.name: South Africa - Infrastructure - Dodgy Adverts
metas.note: Poles or any public infrastructure will often be plastered with dodgy adverts for abortion services or penis enlargement pills in and around Gauteng, in particular in Johannesburg and Emalahleni.

metas.name: South Africa - Infrastructure - Durban Lamp
metas.note: While this lamp and arm can be found uncommonly across the country, Durban uniquely has this bump on the top. You may, however, still see the standard lamp and arm.

metas.name: South Africa - Infrastructure - Kruger National Park Waystone
metas.note: This distinctive directional waystone is commonly found at many junctions in Kruger National Park.

metas.name: South Africa - Infrastructure - Limpopo Pavement
metas.note: You can find this grainy, almost Texas-like pavement with a hint of pink in Limpopo.

metas.name: South Africa - Infrastructure - M-Road - Durban
metas.note: Metropolitan Routes are major roads around cities. They are designated with the letter M. These distinct and unique M route signs are commonly found in Durban.

metas.name: South Africa - Infrastructure - M-Road - Gqeberha
metas.note: Metropolitan Routes are major roads around cities. They are designated with the letter M. These distinct and unique M route signs are commonly found in Port Elizabeth (Gqeberha)

metas.name: South Africa - Infrastructure - Metal Arms
metas.note: Poles with 1 or 2 metal arms holding up insulators are most commonly seen in Mpumalanga.

metas.name: South Africa - Infrastructure - Powerplant
metas.note: Power plants are often seen in between the town of Secunda and eMalahleni in Mpumalanga.

metas.name: South Africa - Infrastructure - Red Sticker
metas.note:
Square, red stickers on the back of regular signs are often found in Eastern cape and close to Eastern cape in Northern Cape and Free State. You may see them in the North West province as well, but to a lesser extent.

NOTE: Red stickers on the back of chevrons can be seen in almost every province.

metas.name: South Africa - Infrastructure - Three Stripes
metas.note: Traffic lights and pedestrian crossing poles in Johannesburg are encircled by three strips of reflective tape.

metas.name: South Africa - Infrastructure - Trident Pole
metas.note: Trident pole tops are almost unique to KwaZulu-Natal.

metas.name: South Africa - Infrastructure - White Sticker
metas.note: White stickers on the back of chevrons are often seen in the Cape provinces.

metas.name: South Africa - Landscape - Cape Town Mountains
metas.note: The distinct Table Mountain, located west of Cape Town, can be recognized by its prominent three-kilometre plateau. It is flanked by Devil’s Peak, which is more pyramidal.

metas.name: South Africa - Landscape - George Mountains
metas.note: Mountains in the Witfontein Nature Reserve, likely George’s Peak, will be visible north from the city of George.

metas.name: South Africa - Landscape - Kruger National Park
metas.note:
The landscape around Kruger National Park is generally flat, with a savannah climate and dry vegetation. You will not see any agriculture and the vegetation is mostly made up of grasses, with small trees dotting the landscape. Red soil can also be seen below the grass.

NOTE: Within the coverage of the park, you will mostly find unpaved gravel roads or small and paved roads without road lines.

metas.name: South Africa - Landscape - Northeastern Dry Season
metas.note:
The northeast of the country can look very dry and somewhat barren, with a lot of orange or red soil. You will often see hills or mountains covered in shrubs.

NOTE: Depending on the season, the coverage can change drastically from dry to very green.

metas.name: South Africa - Landscape - Northern Cape
metas.note:
A dry landscape with red soil is typically found in the Northern Cape.

NOTE: This map is a useful guide in guessing based on the climate of South Africa.

metas.name: South Africa - Landscape - R360 North of Bokspits
metas.note:
The section of the R360 north of Bokspits, next to the Botswana border, has asphalt with a recognizable reddish tint. The landscape is arid and features dry greyish trees, shrubs and long golden grass. The road runs in a general north to south direction.

NOTE: Asphalt with a reddish tint can be found on other roads and the southern part of the R360. However, the landscape north of Bokspits looks predominantly like this.

metas.name: South Africa - Landscape - Rocky Mountains
metas.note:
Unique rocky, treeless mountains can be seen in Western Cape, with most of the mountains having tall, steep sides and sharp peaks.

NOTE: Similar mountains can be seen in and around Lesotho.

metas.name: South Africa - Landscape - Rolling Hills
metas.note: Grassy rolling hills are generally located in the coastal area of Western Cape between Cape Town and George, and just north of Cape Town. Tall ridges are usually visible to the north or east.

metas.name: South Africa - Landscape - South of Mozambique
metas.note: The landscape near the Mozambique border in the highlighted area is noticeably flat, with green subtropical vegetation.

metas.name: South Africa - Vegetation - Cook Pine
metas.note:
Uniquely tall Cook pine trees are found mostly between the cities of East London and Durban along the southeastern coast.

NOTE: These are planted and not native, so they can be found anywhere along the coast.

metas.name: Turkey - Agriculture - Banana
metas.note: Banana plants are found around the city of Alanya.

metas.name: Turkey - Agriculture - Cotton
metas.note: Cotton is mainly found in the region surrounding the city of Şanlıurfa.

metas.name: Turkey - Agriculture - Greenhouse
metas.note: If you find yourself surrounded by greenhouses, you are likely to be along the south coast west of Adana.

metas.name: Turkey - Agriculture - Olive
metas.note: Olive trees are mainly found on the Mediterranean coast.

metas.name: Turkey - Agriculture - Sunflower
metas.note: Sunflowers are mainly found in northwestern Turkey.

metas.name: Turkey - Agriculture - Tea
metas.note: Tea plantations are common in the province of Rize.

metas.name: Turkey - Agriculture - Vineyard
metas.note: A majority of all vineyards in Turkey can be found in a region east of Izmir.

metas.name: Turkey - Architecture - Bodrum Architecture
metas.note: Around the city of Bodrum you will commonly find this type of whitewashed buildings with flat roofs, often combined with blue details or unpainted stone walls.

metas.name: Turkey - Architecture - Flat Roof
metas.note: Flat roofs are mostly found in the southeast and to a lesser extent along the south coast.

metas.name: Turkey - Architecture - Metal Roof
metas.note: Metal roofs are most common in the east.

metas.name: Turkey - Architecture - Pyramid Metal Roof
metas.note: Sheet metal roofs shaped like low pyramids are mainly found far east, particularly in the general area surrounding Lake Van.

metas.name: Turkey - Architecture - Sandstone
metas.note: Many buildings in the Nevşehir Province are built by large, light and unevenly coloured, sandstone bricks.

metas.name: Turkey - Architecture - Tiled Roof
metas.note: Tiled roofs are mostly found in the western two thirds of the country.

metas.name: Turkey - Car Meta - Truck Coverage
metas.note: Generation 4 truck coverage is mainly found in the far east of the country and along the southern coast, with smaller pockets in the west and around Kastamonu.

metas.name: Turkey - Coverage Meta - D525 south of Söke
metas.note: Road D525 south of Söke is a completely straight road going south-south-west to north-north-east with winter Generation 3 coverage. Along the road you will typically find a large amount of reed.

metas.name: Turkey - Coverage Meta - E99 south of Sanliurfa
metas.note: Road E99 south of Şanlıurfa is a divided highway which can be recognised by the slightly hazy Generation 4 sunrise coverage combined with the flat agricultural landscape and general south-north road angle.

metas.name: Turkey - Infrastructure - Bozcaada Tourist Sign
metas.note: These light blue and grey touristic signs which are either arrow shaped or rectangular with a half circle on the top can be found on the island of Bozcaada.

metas.name: Turkey - Infrastructure - Chevron - Yellow on Black
metas.note: Yellow on black chevrons are mainly found in and around the Balıkesir Province in the west and in the Kars Province in the far east. Beware that you may very rarely find them elsewhere.

metas.name: Turkey - Infrastructure - Chevron Black on Yellow
metas.note: Black on yellow chevrons are mainly found north of Izmir.

metas.name: Turkey - Infrastructure - European Poleplate
metas.note: In the European part of Turkey, except Istanbul, utility poles, and other electrical infrastructure, will have a 6 digit code, which is often seen on a small pole plate under the yellow electricity warning plate.

metas.name: Turkey - Infrastructure - Highway without Divider
metas.note: Four-lane divided highways with no divider, other than double middle road lines, are almost exclusively found in the eastern half of the country.

metas.name: Turkey - Infrastructure - Red Oval Sign
metas.note: Street signs in Trabzon and Yalvaç are red and oval-shaped. House numbers also feature the same design.

metas.name: Turkey - Infrastructure - Streetsign - Ankara
metas.note:
Street signs in the Ankara Province are blue with a small round top. Similar street signs can very rarely be found in Giresun.

Beware that some newer street signs are red.

metas.name: Turkey - Infrastructure - Streetsign - Bolu
metas.note: Street signs in Bolu are also green, but are completely flat and lack any kind of border.

metas.name: Turkey - Infrastructure - Streetsign - Bursa
metas.note:
Street signs in Bursa are green, and generally have slightly extruded letters, meaning the signs are not completely flat.

NOTE: Several other types of infrastructure in Bursa, such as fences and guardrails, may also be coloured green.

metas.name: Turkey - Infrastructure - Streetsign - Istanbul
metas.note:
Red street signs with a coloured bottom strip are found in several cities. In the bottom right corner, you can find a white arrow and some numbers. If this arrow is pointing in both directions and has a single arrowhead, rather than double, then you are almost certainly in Istanbul.

Beware that simple arrows pointing in only one direction can be found in both Istanbul and in other cities. However, if you see such signs in combination with red house numbers, then you should be in Istanbul.

metas.name: Turkey - Infrastructure - Streetsign - Izmir
metas.note: Street signs in the Izmir Province are dark blue, noticeably bulge outwards and very commonly have the emblem of Izmir in white at the top of the sign.

metas.name: Turkey - Infrastructure - Watertank - Horizontal on top of Vertical
metas.note: Horizontal water tanks placed on top of vertical water tanks are primarily found in a line following the south coast and going up to Elâzığ.

metas.name: Turkey - Infrastructure - Watertank - Octagonal
metas.note: Square water tanks with angled corners are found in the south, approximately from İskenderun to Sanliurfa.

metas.name: Turkey - Infrastructure - Watertank - Spherical
metas.note: White spherical water tanks can be found in the southeast, mainly south of Batman.

metas.name: Turkey - Infrastructure - Watertank - Vertical
metas.note: Vertical water tanks can be found in most of Turkey, but are notably uncommon along the south and west coast.

metas.name: Turkey - Landscape - Cliff Valley
metas.note: River valleys surrounded by steep, barren and rocky cliff sides can be found between the cities of Erzurum and Artvin and in the southeast near the city of Hakkâri.

metas.name: Turkey - Landscape - Göreme Monoliths
metas.note: Göreme, west of Kayseri, can be recognised by the tall sandstone monoliths with ancient dwellings carved into them.

metas.name: Turkey - Landscape - Grassland
metas.note: In the northeast you will find uncultivated grasslands in valleys surrounded by round hills. Trees are very limited in the region. In Generation 3 the area has an extremely distinct look, with deep green grass covering the hills. It is significantly more difficult to recognise in Generation 4, where the grass has a more arid look.

metas.name: Turkey - Landscape - Lake Beysehir
metas.note: Along the western shore of Lake Beyşehir and Lake Eğirdir you can find this small single lane road with jagged, exposed rock and Turkish pines to the west. These two can be differentiated by the road west of Lake Eğirdir having a middle road line.

metas.name: Turkey - Landscape - Lake Egirdir
metas.note: Along the western shore of Lake Beyşehir and Lake Eğirdir you can find this small single lane road with jagged, exposed rock and Turkish pines to the west. These two can be differentiated by the road west of Lake Eğirdir having a middle road line.

metas.name: Turkey - Landscape - Lake Van
metas.note: Lake Van is by far the biggest lake in Turkey and has a semi-arid landscape, being surrounded by dry grassy hills and occasional trees and agricultural fields near the shore.

metas.name: Turkey - Landscape - Lush
metas.note: Northern Turkey tends to be significantly lusher and more forested than the rest of the country.

metas.name: Turkey - Landscape - Mount Ararat
metas.note: Mount Ararat, labelled as Ağrı Dağı on Google Maps, is a dormant volcano in far eastern Turkey and the tallest mountain in the country. It is often seen together with Küçük Ağrı, a smaller volcano to the southeast.

metas.name: Turkey - Landscape - Volcanic Rocks
metas.note: Dark, volcanic rocks are commonly found between the cities of Şanlıurfa and Diyarbakır.

metas.name: Turkey - Vegetation - Turkish Pine
metas.note:
Turkish pines (pinus brutia) are mainly found near the Mediterranean coast.

NOTE: Turkish pines can appear very similar to Aleppo pines, which are uncommon in Turkey, but are often found in other Mediterranean countries.

metas.name: United States - Agriculture - Canola
metas.note: Along the Canadian border in North Dakota, and rarely Montana, fields filled with short yellow canola flowers (Brassica napus) can commonly be seen from the road.

metas.name: United States - Agriculture - Center Pivot Irrigation
metas.note:
You may have noticed some difference between farmland in different states on satellite view… It can be difficult to tell the farmland apart unless you’re at a corner up close, but as it turns out, the circles are actually created by a giant machine you can see from a distance

This is called centre point irrigation and can be found in many regions in the country!!

The most common states are Idaho, Nebraska and Kansas
metas.footer: Source: UNITED STATES CENTRE PIVOT IRRIGAITON GUIDE

metas.name: United States - Agriculture - Corn
metas.note:
Corn fields can most commonly be found in these regions:-Iowa

-North of Iowa

-Nebraska without NW

metas.name: United States - Agriculture - Cotton
metas.note: Cotton is a crop that produces large fields of fluffy white flowers. It is most commonly produced in coastal Southeast States, the Lower Mississippi River Valley, Western Texas, and parts of California and Arizona.

metas.name: United States - Agriculture - Golden Fields
metas.note:
Agricultural golden fields can commonly be seen in eastern Washington.

NOTE: Flat areas of northern and eastern Oregon can have a similar appearance.

metas.name: United States - Agriculture - Rice
metas.note: Rice production only occurs in a few areas of the US, so it is very useful for region guessing. It is typically grown in large, flat fields that resemble low prairies. It is only grown in north-central California and the Lower Mississippi River Valley in Arkansas, Louisiana, Texas, and Mississippi.

metas.name: United States - Agriculture - Soy
metas.note: Soybeans are short, dark green crops organised in long rows and are found in similar regions where corn is grown. They are most common in the Eastern Plains, Midwest, Lower Mississippi Valley, and areas of the Mid Atlantic.

metas.name: United States - Architecture - Art Deco Architecture
metas.note:
Art Deco is a very distinctive architectural style that is found predominantly in Miami, FL.

There are many features that make it distinct (picture), and a good way to remember them is that they're inspired by ships, for example the Strong central vertical element, which gives the building an appearance like looking straight at a ship. Or round port hole windows, resembling ship windows.

Another distinctive feature is the so-called eyebrows above the windows which have a practical use, which is blocking the strong Miami sunlight from shining into the building and heating it up.

metas.name: United States - Architecture - Brick
metas.note: Brick buildings are more common in the Mid-Atlantic states than in other parts of the country. The area around Philadelphia especially has many brick buildings.
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Architecture - Brownstone Architecture
metas.note: ###

metas.name: United States - Architecture - Hank Schrader House
metas.note:
Pueblo Revival style houses are commonly seen in New Mexico. They are typically constructed of adobe or brick and concrete. They have rounded edges and flat roofs, and are usually sand-brown in colour. A famous example for a house like this is the Schrader's residence in Breaking Bad.

NOTE: Pueblo style houses can also be seen in Arizona and Colorado to a lesser extent.

metas.name: United States - Architecture - High Stilts
metas.note: Stilt houses can sometimes be seen on the coast. These are especially common toward the south, and on the Atlantic and Gulf coasts.

metas.name: United States - Architecture - Large Sloped Roofs
metas.note: Buildings with very large, sloped roofs are most common in the states of Oklahoma, Texas, and Louisiana. They can also be seen in neighbouring states to a lesser extent.

metas.name: United States - Architecture - Miami Modern Architecture
metas.note:
Miami Modern Architecture is characterized by "fun", unconventional designs, decorative elements, smooth corners, flat roofs and lots of glass.

It is find in certain districts of Miami and Miami Beach.

metas.name: United States - Architecture - New Orleans Architecture
metas.note:
Neighbourhoods all around the city of New Orleans feature many colourful, historic, shotgun-style houses.

Buildings in central areas of New Orleans often feature colourful facades with second story wrap-around balconies.

metas.name: United States - Architecture - North-Eastern House
metas.note: Houses in North-Eastern USA often have walls made up of horizontal, overlapping boards

metas.name: United States - Architecture - Red Metal Roof
metas.note:
Buildings with red metal rooftops are most commonly found in the Mid-South and Southern Appalachia states of Virginia, West Virginia, Ohio, Kentucky, Tennessee, Arkansas, and North Carolina.

NOTE: These types of rooftops can be found in other areas, so use other clues before guessing.

metas.name: United States - Architecture - Shingle Walls
metas.note: Houses in coastal New England often feature shingle walls, which are layered wood panels overlapping each other.

metas.name: United States - Architecture - Short Stilt House
metas.note: Houses with short stilts are common in the western and central Gulf Coast. These houses typically feature short stilts made of concrete or wood (30cm-90cm off the ground) and are primarily found in areas near the coast and any adjacent rivers.

metas.name: United States - Architecture - Shotgun House
metas.note: Very narrow, one-storey houses made out of wood are called ‘shotgun houses.’ They are most common in and around New Orleans (LA,) Houston (TX,) Louisville (KY,) and the state of Mississippi.

metas.name: United States - Architecture - Spanish Colonial Architecture
metas.note:
Spanish Colonial Revival Architecture can be categorised as buildings with lightly-coloured stucco walls and red clay-tile roofs. They can be found in the desert southwest states of California, Nevada, Arizona, and Texas. You can also find similar types of buildings in Florida and coastal Georgia.

Note by MB: See the second picture for an in-depth explanation of this architecture (sorry for the skew, it's a photo I took myself)

metas.name: United States - Architecture - Stacked Triplex
metas.note:
Older three story wooden houses, also called ‘stacked triplexes,’ are very common in urban areas of the Northeast. They are most prevalent in New York, Connecticut, Rhode Island, and Massachusetts.

NOTE: These types of houses are also somewhat common in cities in Atlantic Canada.

metas.name: United States - Architecture - Trailer House
metas.note: Small, rectangular manufactured homes, also known as mobile or ‘trailer’ homes, are popular in rural areas of the US. In general, mobile homes are more common in the Southeast but they can be seen anywhere in the country.

metas.name: United States - Architecture - Victorian Architecture
metas.note: Row Houses and other buildings in San Francisco are often in the style of Victorian architecture, with many bay windows, turrets, and ornate exterior details. These homes are built close together and can be very colourful.

metas.name: United States - Architecture - Wooden House
metas.note: Houses and commercial buildings in the interior Western US are often made of lots of dark wooden boards and timbers. Buildings at high elevations also commonly have metal roofs, to avoid snow build-up.

metas.name: United States - Car Meta - Daniel Boone Car
metas.note:
This section of road in Daniel Boone National Forest near Beattyville, KY has a unique Google car.

Note by MB: This coverage is overwritten afaik.
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Car Meta - Ford Bronco
metas.note:
As part of a promotional campaign, the TransAmerica Trail from Oregon to North Carolina was covered by a Ford Bronco. The car can recognised by its unblurred black roof and red hood, and is mostly found on unpaved rural roads.

Looking backwards, you will see two other Ford SUVs escorting the camera car.

metas.name: United States - Car Meta - Golden Gate Car
metas.note: This car can be found to the north of the Golden Gate Bridge in San Francisco.
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Car Meta - Santa Catalina Car
metas.note: This island to the south of Los Angeles has a unique Google car.
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Coverage Meta - Winter - Appalachians
metas.note: Within the Appalachians, Winter Coverage is most common in West Virginia.
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Coverage Meta - Winter - New England
metas.note: Winter/fall coverage such as this is commonplace in New England, particularly in Massachusetts, Connecticut, and Rhode Island. Be aware that winter coverage also exists in the South and hence why you may get Arkansas or another state in that region mixed up with New England if you’re trying to go based only on the vibes.
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Donner Park Trekker
metas.note: You can see this car all over the Donner Park in Columbus, IN.
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - 6 bolt bollard
metas.note:
This bollard has a white rectangular plate, with 6 bolts: 2 at the top, 2 in the middle and 2 at the bottom. There are different variants, with circular reflectors, rectangular reflectors, or no reflectors at all.

They're all found in California

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Adopt-A-Highway Signs
metas.note: Most states have unique, distinct and learnable Adopt-a-Highway signs, which can be seen on the side of roads. A map of those can be seen here. Keep in mind, some states have slight variations in design.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Arrow Street Number
metas.note:
North Carolina commonly uses a style of street signs showing street numbers and arrows in addition to the street name.

NOTE: Other states occasionally feature street signs with similar designs, so use other clues before guessing.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - ATV Route
metas.note: These green ATV Route signs are unique to Wisconsin.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Billboards
metas.note: Billboards are banned in Maine, Vermont, Alaska and Hawaii. So if you see one, you can rule those out.
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Black Tar
metas.note: A black stripe can sometimes be seen in between the two yellow, middle road lines in California.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Black/White Overpass Support
metas.note: These stripes on an overpass support are a dead giveaway that it’s South Carolina. Sometimes a sign with yellow and black stripes is used instead
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - California Bridge Marker
metas.note: California posts these bridge markers (with a lot of numbers) on bridges. The county abbreviations used on the bridge markers are different from those on the postal markers.
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - California Stripes
metas.note: Utility poles in California usually have markings at the bottom of the pole that consist of 3 yellow stripes.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Chattanooga Font
metas.note: The city of Chattanooga in Tennessee has its own unique font that is used on some signs in the city.
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Circular Fraction-Sign
metas.note: West Virginia sometimes features street signs with a symbol that resembles a fraction inside a circle.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Clearance on Overpass
metas.note: South Carolina is the only southeastern state to post the clearance on every overpass.
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Concrete Pavement
metas.note:
Concrete paving on main highways is much more common in Iowa than in other states.

NOTE: Concrete paving on residential streets is commonly seen throughout the Midwest states and parts of the East Coast.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - County Road - Clark County
metas.note: Clark County is the county Las Vegas is situated in and it uses a unique county route shield.
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Dark Wooden Fences
metas.note:
Dark-coloured wooden fences with several horizontal wooden supports are common in farming areas of central and southern Appalachia, stretching from Pennsylvania to Georgia.

NOTE: These types of fences can be found elsewhere to a lesser extent, so use other clues before guessing.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Diamond Bollard
metas.note:
The most common type of roadside bollard in South Dakota and Montana features a dark metal post with a white diamond on each side of the top.

NOTE: These bollards can be found to a lesser extent in other western states.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Double Signposts
metas.note:
Signs attached to two signposts can be seen in Michigan. Not all signs are attached to two signposts.

NOTE: Double signposts can also be seen in other states, but are not as common.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - E-2 Sign
metas.note: In New Hampshire there will often be a white metal sign with the characters ‘E-2’ on it adjacent to the road, typically at either end of bridges.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Exit Ramp / No Parking
metas.note: Georgia likes to decorate its freeway offramps with no parking signs.
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Exit with Speed Limit
metas.note: New Alabama coverage can have these combined exit/speed limit signs.
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Florida Bollard
metas.note: This bollard is found in Florida.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Green Overpass Marker
metas.note: Overpass bridges in Mississippi have green plaques with white numbers on them.
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Green US Route
metas.note: This green U.S. Route shield with the word business at the top is unique to Maryland.
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Green-White Sign
metas.note: This sign is Illinois-specific.
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Green/Red Bridge Marker
metas.note:
Maine, New Hampshire, and Massachusetts use small green and red rectangular signs to mark the ends of bridges and guardrails.

NOTE: Not all bridges and guardrails in these states will have these markers.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - H-Reflector
metas.note: Snowplowable raised pavement markers can only be found on highways in the eastern states shown in the image. They are built into the road and somewhat resemble the letter H.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Hanging Yellow Boxes
metas.note:
Many large intersections in Michigan have stop lights and signs that hang from wires that stretch across the middle of the intersection. These markers are commonly in yellow boxes.

NOTE: These are not completely unique to Michigan, but are most commonly seen there.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Highway Signs
metas.note: Maximum speed limits vary by state and territory. The maximum speed limits shown here will generally be seen on interstate highways. Some interstates and highways in their respective states or territories will have lower maximum speed limits than what is shown.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Horizontal Traffic Light
metas.note: Horizontal Traffic Lights are common in Nebraska, New Mexico, Texas and Louisiana. They also appear occasionally in Oklahoma, Louisiana and Georgia.
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - ICE Warning
metas.note: Signs warning about ice (like this) are commonplace in Louisiana.
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Indiana Blue Square
metas.note: This kind of blue square on a post is exclusive to Indiana.
metas.footer: Source: A Unique USA by mistystar

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Kansas Sign Reflectors
metas.note: These white reflectors on signposts are unique to Kansas. They are most commonly seen on ‘stop’ signs in rural areas.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Kentucky Rumble Strips
metas.note: Some roads and highways in the state of Kentucky use uniquely-shaped rumble strips that are thin, relatively long recessed lines on the very outside edges of the road.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Key West Poles
metas.note: Poles on Intersections in Key West have a white paint at the bottom which contains the name of the street its on.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Kilometer
metas.note:
Interstate 19 in Arizona from Tucson to the Mexico border uses kilometres on the exit and distance signs. This is the only part of the country that uses kilometres instead of miles for highway signs.

NOTE: Speed limit signs in this area still use MPH instead of KPH.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Large Center Line Gap
metas.note:
Yellow lines with a noticeably larger gap in between them are most common in Texas, Arkansas, Louisiana, Mississippi, and Oregon. They can also be found to a lesser extent in Washington, Alabama, and Michigan.

NOTE: Wide middle lines can also rarely appear in other states, so consider other clues before guessing.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Letter Highway Sign (with County)
metas.note: Wisconsin and Missouri are the only two states that use a lettering system (A - ZZZ) for their county highways. Wisconsin signs typically have the word ‘county’ above the letter, while Missouri signs typically do not. The borders of the signs also vary slightly.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - Letter Highway Sign (without County)
metas.note: Wisconsin and Missouri are the only two states that use a lettering system (A - ZZZ) for their county highways. Wisconsin signs typically have the word ‘county’ above the letter, while Missouri signs typically do not. The borders of the signs also vary slightly.

metas.name: United States - Infrastructure - License Plate - No Front Plates

Cars without Front Plates are mostly found south of the linie north of Arizona to North Carolina (except for Texas), Ohio and it's neighboring states + Delaware and Oklahoma.

In the picture, the yellow states do not require front license plates, the purple and blue states generally do.

Keep in mind that cars travel, and not all people follow the law, so use with caution.
